questions.text: Consider the following statements regarding the National Green Tribunal (NGT): 1. It is a specialized body set up to expeditiously deal with environmental related litigation. 2. The head of the NGT is known as the Chairperson, who is appointed by the President of India. 3. The decisions of the NGT are not subject to appeal in any court of law. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.label: A
options.text: 1 only

options.label: B
options.text: 2 and 3 only

options.label: C
options.text: 1 and 3 only

options.label: D
options.text: 1, 2 and 3

questions.solution: Statement 1 is correct as the NGT was established under the National Green Tribunal Act, 2010 to handle environmental disputes quickly. Statement 2 is correct; the Chairperson of the NGT is appointed by the President of India. Statement 3 is incorrect because Section 14 of the NGT Act allows for appeals to be filed directly to the Supreme Court of India against any order or decision of the Tribunal.

questions.text: As per the table below showing Budget Estimates (BE) 2023-24 for four major Central Government schemes (in Rs Lakh Crore), what is the approximate percentage share of PM Awas Yojana in the total allocation for these four schemes? | Scheme | Allocation (Rs Lakh Cr) | | :--- | :--- | | MGNREGA | 0.60 | | PM-KISAN | 0.60 | | Jal Jeevan Mission | 0.70 | | PM Awas Yojana | 0.79 |
questions.solution: **Shortcut (Approximation & Fraction Simplification):** Round allocations: 0.6, 0.6, 0.7, 0.8. Total ≈ 2.7. Target = 0.8. Fraction = 0.8 / 2.7 = 8/27. Since 27 × 3 = 81, 8/27 ≈ 29.6% (close to 30%). Option C (29.5%) is closest. **Step-by-Step:** 1. Calculate Total Allocation = 0.60 + 0.60 + 0.70 + 0.79 = 2.69 Lakh Cr. 2. PM Awas Allocation = 0.79 Lakh Cr. 3. Percentage = (0.79 / 2.69) × 100. 4. Simplify: 79 / 269 ≈ 0.2936. 5. 0.2936 × 100 = 29.36% ≈ 29.5%.

questions.text: As per the table below showing the Gross Value Added (GVA) at basic prices by economic activity for a hypothetical year (in Rs Lakh Crore), what is the approximate percentage share of the 'Services' sector in the total GVA? | Sector | GVA (Rs Lakh Crore) | | :--- | :--- | | Agriculture & Allied | 22.5 | | Industry | 31.0 | | Services | 58.5 |
questions.solution: Shortcut: Use approximation. Total ≈ 22.5 + 31 + 58.5 = 112. Services share = 58.5/112. Note 58.5 is slightly more than half of 112 (which is 56). 58.5/112 ≈ 52.2%. questions.solution: Shortcut: Use the denominator approximation trick. Increase = 3682 - 2967 = 715. Approximate base (2967) to 3000. Percentage ≈ (715/3000) × 100 ≈ 23.8% → ~24%. questions.solution: Shortcut: Elimination by anchor dates. Jallianwala Bagh (1919) is the earliest event. Non-Cooperation (1920) follows immediately. Dandi March (1930) is a decade later. questions.solution: Shortcut: Direct Taxes = Corp Tax + Income Tax = 10.43 + 11.87 = 22.30. Indirect Taxes ≈ 2.33 + 3.22 + 9.68 + 0.47 = 15.70. Total ≈ 38.00. % Direct = 22.3/38 ≈ 58.7% → ~58%. Sum Indirect Taxes: 2.33 + 3.22 + 9.68 + 0.47 = 15.70 Lakh Cr. 3. Total Gross Tax Revenue = 22.30 + 15.70 = 38.00 Lakh Cr. 4. Percentage = (22.30 / 38.00) × 100 = 58.68% ≈ 58%.

questions.text: Under Article 368 of the Constitution of India, which of the following categories of amendments requires ratification by the Legislatures of not less than one-half of the States?

options.label: A
options.text: Election of the President of India

options.label: B
options.text: Extent of the executive power of the Union and the States

options.label: C
options.text: Representation of States in Parliament

options.label: D
options.text: All of the above

questions.solution: Shortcut: Article 368 proviso lists specific federal provisions requiring state ratification. If a candidate identifies that even two of the listed options (e.g., Election of President and Representation of States) are entrenched federal provisions, 'All of the above' becomes the logical choice without verifying the third. Full Solution: Article 368 stipulates that amendments to provisions affecting the federal structure (listed in the proviso) require special majority of Parliament plus ratification by half the State Legislatures. The list explicitly includes: (a) Articles 54 and 55 (Election of President); (b) Articles 73 and 162 (Extent of executive power); (c) Chapter IV of Part V, Chapter V of Part VI, Chapter I of Part XI (Judiciary, Legislative Relations); (d) Any of the Lists in Seventh Schedule; (e) Representation of States in Parliament; (f) Proviso to Article 368 itself. Since all three options (A, B, C) are explicitly mentioned in the proviso to Article 368, option D is correct.

questions.text: Consider the following pairs of Ocean Currents and their characteristics: 1. Labrador Current — Cold current, flows southward along the coast of Labrador and Newfoundland. 2. Kuroshio Current — Cold current, flows northward along the coast of Japan. 3. Benguela Current — Warm current, flows northward along the southwestern coast of Africa. 4. questions.solution: Shortcut: Use the 'Hemisphere Temperature Rule' for quick elimination. In the Northern Hemisphere, currents flowing towards the pole (North) are Warm (Kuroshio, Gulf Stream); towards the equator (South) are Cold (Labrador, California). In the Southern Hemisphere, towards the pole (South) are Warm (East Australian, Brazil); towards equator (North) are Cold (Benguela, Peru/Humboldt). Pair 1: Labrador flows South (Equator-ward) in NH -> Cold (Correct). Pair 2: Kuroshio flows North (Pole-ward) in NH -> Warm (Incorrectly labeled Cold). Pair 3: Benguela flows North (Equator-ward) in SH -> Cold (Incorrectly labeled Warm). Pair 4: East Australian flows South (Pole-ward) in SH -> Warm (Correct). Only Pairs 1 and 4 are correct. Answer: Two pairs.

questions.text: With reference to the special majorities required in the Indian Parliament, which of the following provisions requires a majority of two-thirds of the members present and voting only, without requiring a majority of the total membership of the House?

options.label: C

options.text: Approval of a Proclamation of National Emergency under Article 352(6)

questions.solution: Shortcut: Elimination by 'Total Membership' clause. Articles 368, 124(2), and 352(6) explicitly mandate 'a majority of the total membership of the House' PLUS 'two-thirds of members present and voting'. Article 312 (Rajya Sabha resolution for All India Services) requires only 'not less than two-thirds of the members present and voting' (Special Majority under Art 249), with no total membership requirement. Worked Solution: 1. Art 368 (Constitutional Amendment): Requires majority of total membership + 2/3rd present and voting. 2. Art 124(2) (Removal of SC Judge): Requires same majority as Art 368 (majority of total membership + 2/3rd present and voting). 3. Art 352(6) (Emergency Approval): Requires same majority as Art 368 (majority of total membership + 2/3rd present and voting). 4. Art 312 (All India Services): Rajya Sabha resolution supported by 'not less than two-thirds of the members present and voting'. No mention of total membership. Hence, Option B is correct.

questions.text: Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes between 'value' and 'price' in the context of ecosystem services, and matches a service to its Millennium Ecosystem Assessment category?

questions.text: According to the Global Footprint Network 2022 edition data cited in the lesson, India's ecological footprint and biocapacity per capita imply which of the following?

questions.text: Which of the following statements correctly describes the rain-shadow effect created by the Western Ghats on the Peninsular Plateau?

options.text: Presence of towering minarets at each corner.

options.label: B
options.text: Deliberate omission of minarets.

options.label: C
options.text: Extensive use of marble inlay work.

options.label: D
options.text: Adoption of the Persian double‑dome system.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Deliberate omission of minarets..

questions.text: How did colonial hill‑station architecture adapt the European "Swiss chalet" motif?

options.label: A
options.text: By importing Swiss craftsmen and authentic Alpine timber for exact replication.

options.label: B
options.text: By using local timber (sal, teak) and simplified joinery, not imported Swiss craft.

options.label: C
options.text: By replacing timber framing with brick nogging entirely.

options.label: D
options.text: By adopting the motif only for decorative façades while retaining traditional Indian roof forms.

questions.solution: Correct answer: By using local timber (sal, teak) and simplified joinery, not imported Swiss craft..

questions.text: Which of the following statements correctly describes the relationship between the Harappan binary weight unit and later Mauryan metrological units?

options.label: A
options.text: The Harappan unit of 13.7 g is identical to the Mauryan masha.

options.label: B
options.text: The Mauryan karshapana of 13.7 g is exactly twice the Harappan grain unit.

options.label: C
options.text: The Mauryan masha (≈0.97 g) and karshapana (≈13.7 g) preserve the 1 : 14 ratio of the Harappan grain unit to its larger counterpart.

options.label: D
options.text: The Mauryan system abandoned the binary progression and adopted only a decimal series.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The Mauryan masha (≈0.97 g) and karshapana (≈13.7 g) preserve the 1 : 14 ratio of the Harappan grain unit to its larger counterpart..

questions.text: In the rock‑cut monastic complexes of the Western Deccan, the spatial sequence that guides a devotee from the communal area to the stupa‑focused worship space is best described as:

options.label: A
options.text: Cell → Courtyard → Chaitya hall → Pillared verandah

options.label: B
options.text: Courtyard → Cells on three sides → Chaitya hall on the fourth side → Central stupa

options.label: C
options.text: Chaitya hall → Courtyard → Cells → Stupa at the entrance

options.label: D
options.text: Pillared verandah → Courtyard → Cells → Chaitya hall with stupa at the apse

questions.solution: Correct answer: Courtyard → Cells on three sides → Chaitya hall on the fourth side → Central stupa.

questions.text: Which material source was identified by compositional analyses as the exclusive origin of Harappan chert weights?

options.label: A
options.text: Kachchh limestone quarries

options.label: B
options.text: Rohri Hills

options.label: C
options.text: Deccan basalt formations

options.label: D
options.text: Saurashtra sandstone beds

questions.solution: Correct answer: Rohri Hills.

questions.text: In Mughal garden hydraulics, the seasonal operation of the canal network is achieved by:

options.label: A
options.text: Adjusting the gradient of the main canal each season

options.label: B
options.text: Closing sluice gates during the monsoon to prevent overflow

options.label: C
options.text: Replacing water with rain‑water harvested in step‑wells

options.label: D
options.text: Reorienting the garden’s axial pathways to follow prevailing winds

questions.solution: Correct answer: Closing sluice gates during the monsoon to prevent overflow.

questions.text: The structural system that enables the great hall of the Madras High Court to span 30 m without intermediate columns combines which of the following features?

options.label: A
options.text: Riveted wrought‑iron trusses imported from Glasgow and a timber post‑and‑beam roof

options.label: B
options.text: A series of pointed arches clad in Mangalore tiles supported by stone arches

options.label: C
options.text: Riveted wrought‑iron trusses imported from Glasgow concealed behind load‑bearing basalt walls

options.label: D
options.text: A double‑shell dome with an inner brick vault and outer stone skin

questions.solution: Correct answer: Riveted wrought‑iron trusses imported from Glasgow concealed behind load‑bearing basalt walls.

questions.text: Which of the following statements accurately describes the metrological system evidenced at Harappan sites Chanhudaro, Lothal, and Dholavira?

options.label: A
options.text: A single decimal weight series was used uniformly for all commodities including carnelian beads and grain.

options.label: B
options.text: A binary weight series (1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64) was used for bulk commodities while a decimal series served precision crafts.

options.label: C
options.text: Both a binary series (1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64 units) and a decimal series coexisted, the latter reserved for bulk commodities such as grain.

options.label: D
options.text: Weight standardization was absent; each workshop produced its own weights leading to inter-site variation in bead-drill bit sizes.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Both a binary series (1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64 units) and a decimal series coexisted, the latter reserved for bulk commodities such as grain..

questions.text: In the structural evolution of the chaitya arch, which site marks the first appearance of fully monolithic stone ribs forming a true masonry barrel vault, eliminating tensile stresses at the crown?

options.label: A
options.text: Bhaja (2nd century BCE)

options.label: B
options.text: Karla (c. 50 CE)

options.label: C
options.text: Ajanta Cave 19 (5th century CE)

options.label: D
options.text: Ellora Cave 10 (7th century CE)

questions.solution: Correct answer: Ajanta Cave 19 (5th century CE).

questions.text: What is the common structural advantage of the double dome system across its regional variants in Indo-Islamic architecture, as described in the lesson?

options.label: A
options.text: It allows the use of lighter materials like timber in the outer shell to reduce seismic vulnerability.

options.label: B
options.text: It creates a whispering gallery that serves as the primary load-bearing element for the drum.

options.label: C
options.text: It decouples the external aesthetic profile from the structural thickness, enabling monumental silhouettes without proportionally massive masonry.

options.label: D
options.text: It eliminates the need for a drum by transferring all loads directly to the pendentives through the interstitial space.

questions.solution: Correct answer: It decouples the external aesthetic profile from the structural thickness, enabling monumental silhouettes without proportionally massive masonry..

questions.text: In the planning of New Delhi's Central Vista, the selection of *Ficus religiosa* and *Dalbergia sissoo* for the avenue's double rows primarily reflects:

options.label: A
options.text: A colonial ornamental preference for exotic species to symbolize imperial grandeur.

options.label: B
options.text: A direct replication of Ebenezer Howard's specific planting lists from Letchworth Garden City.

options.label: C
options.text: A deliberate climatic adaptation using indigenous species to mitigate summer heat, while adopting the Garden City 'green belt' concept.

options.label: D
options.text: A symbolic alignment with Mughal charbagh geometry where these two species represent the four rivers of paradise.

questions.solution: Correct answer: A deliberate climatic adaptation using indigenous species to mitigate summer heat, while adopting the Garden City 'green belt' concept..

questions.text: According to the Natya Shastra, which of the following sets correctly identifies the fourfold means of communication (abhinaya) used in classical dance?

options.label: A
options.text: Angika, Vachika, Aharya, Satvika

options.label: B
options.text: Nritta, Nritya, Natya, Rasa

options.label: C
options.text: Karanas, Mudras, Talas, Bhavas

options.label: D
options.text: Guru, Shishya, Parampara, Margam

questions.solution: Correct answer: Angika, Vachika, Aharya, Satvika.

questions.text: Which pairing correctly matches a classical dance form with the specific cultural milieu that shaped its movement vocabulary and repertoire, as described in the lesson?

options.label: A
options.text: Bharatanatyam – Mughal courtly patronage

options.label: B
options.text: Kathak – Temple rituals of devadasis

options.label: C
options.text: Kathakali – Monastic traditions of Assam

options.label: D
options.text: Kathak – Mughal courts with Persian aesthetic ideals

questions.solution: Correct answer: Kathak – Mughal courts with Persian aesthetic ideals.

questions.text: Which of the following features is a hallmark of the Mughal miniature painting tradition under Akbar, as described in the lesson?

options.label: A
options.text: Use of bold outlines and flat perspective with vibrant primary colours

options.label: B
options.text: Production of illustrated manuscripts like the Akbarnama and Hamzanama in an imperial atelier (karkhana)

options.label: C
options.text: Depiction of elongated eyes and distinctive profiles symbolising idealised beauty (Bani Thani)

options.label: D
options.text: Rapid, bold watercolour paintings on paper for the urban pilgrim market depicting deities and social satire

questions.solution: Correct answer: Production of illustrated manuscripts like the Akbarnama and Hamzanama in an imperial atelier (karkhana).

questions.text: The evolution of the Pahari schools of painting from Basohli to Kangra is characterised in the lesson by which of the following stylistic shifts?

options.label: A
options.text: From lyrical naturalism to intense, saturated palette

options.label: B
options.text: From delicate rendering of landscapes to hierarchical perspective

options.label: C
options.text: From intense, saturated palette to lyrical naturalism

options.label: D
options.text: From composite animals and fantastical landscapes to psychological portraiture

questions.solution: Correct answer: From intense, saturated palette to lyrical naturalism.

questions.text: Which temple tradition employs the attaprakaram acting manual that aligns each abhinaya gesture with a specific tala cycle?

options.label: A
options.text: Bharatanatyam in Tamil Nadu

options.label: B
options.text: Koodiyattam in Kerala

options.label: C
options.text: Odissi in Puri

options.label: D
options.text: Raslila in Braj

questions.solution: Correct answer: Koodiyattam in Kerala.

questions.text: The Imdadkhani (Etawah) gharana of sitar, known for its meend‑heavy gayaki ang, was codified in a notated gat repertoire published as Sitar Marg in 1955 by which musician?

options.label: A
options.text: Allauddin Khan

options.label: B
options.text: Vilayat Khan

options.label: C
options.text: Ravi Shankar

options.label: D
options.text: Baba Gopal Das

questions.solution: Correct answer: Vilayat Khan.

questions.text: In the context of miniature painting attribution, why is wasli paper preparation considered essential alongside pigment analysis?

options.label: A
options.text: Wasli paper was introduced only during the British Company painting period

options.label: B
options.text: Pigment analysis alone cannot differentiate workshops without substrate data

options.label: C
options.text: Wasli preparation is irrelevant for Mughal atelier works

options.label: D
options.text: It serves solely as a decorative backing for the painting

questions.solution: Correct answer: Pigment analysis alone cannot differentiate workshops without substrate data.

questions.text: Which 1851 event catalyzed the shift from courtly to colonial patronage and contributed to the creation of the Indian Museum, Calcutta?

options.label: A
options.text: The Great Exhibition

options.label: B
options.text: The Delhi Durbar

options.label: C
options.text: The founding of the Sangeet Natak Akademi

options.label: D
options.text: The establishment of the Kalakshetra Foundation

questions.solution: Correct answer: The Great Exhibition.

questions.text: What is a mandatory requirement for a nomination to UNESCO's Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage, as described in the lesson?

options.label: A
options.text: A guarantee of government funding for the element

options.label: B
options.text: Community participation evidenced by consent letters

options.label: C
options.text: Prior inclusion on the List of Intangible Cultural Heritage in Need of Urgent Safeguarding

options.label: D
options.text: Integration of the element into the national school curriculum before nomination

questions.solution: Correct answer: Community participation evidenced by consent letters.

questions.text: Which of the following statements accurately describes the contribution of Sadarang (Niamat Khan) and Adarang to the evolution of Khayal Gayaki in the 18th century?

options.label: A
options.text: They introduced the Persian melodic concepts into the indigenous dhrupad framework for the first time.

options.label: B
options.text: They formalised the modern khayal structure comprising a vilambit bandish in ektal or jhumra, an elaborate alap-jod-jhala exploration, and a drut bandish in teentaal.

options.label: C
options.text: They established the practice of presenting a vilambit bandish followed by a drut bandish in the same raga at Akbar's court.

options.label: D
options.text: They pioneered the 'bol-baant' technique where lyrical syllables are woven into melodic improvisation in the court of Wajid Ali Shah.

questions.solution: Correct answer: They formalised the modern khayal structure comprising a vilambit bandish in ektal or jhumra, an elaborate alap-jod-jhala exploration, and a drut bandish in teentaal..

questions.text: Regarding the All India Radio's 'National Programme of Music' (NPM) launched in 1952, which statement is correct based on the lesson?

options.label: A
options.text: The NPM broadcast format replicated the traditional 90-minute concert length without any compression.

options.label: B
options.text: The NPM was a weekly 60-minute broadcast that presented a full vilambit-drut khayal recital, a Carnatic kriti, and a short instrumental piece.

options.label: C
options.text: The NPM archive, preserved on magnetic tape from 1955 onward, constitutes the largest continuous audio record of only Hindustani concert practice.

options.label: D
options.text: The NPM was launched independently by AIR without collaboration from the Sangeet Natak Akademi.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The NPM was a weekly 60-minute broadcast that presented a full vilambit-drut khayal recital, a Carnatic kriti, and a short instrumental piece..

questions.text: Which of the following is identified in the lesson as a specific challenge or standard in the digital archiving of intangible performing arts?

options.label: A
options.text: The mandatory use of the OAIS reference model for all government-funded digital archives in India.

options.label: B
options.text: A 5-year migration cycle mandated for digital preservation, failure of which leads to data loss.

options.label: C
options.text: The allocation for digital preservation increased by 15% from the 2021 peak in the 2023 budget.

options.label: D
options.text: The 1957 Copyright Act's performer's right has no role in digital archiving consent negotiations.

questions.solution: Correct answer: A 5-year migration cycle mandated for digital preservation, failure of which leads to data loss..

questions.text: What was the specific target set by the Sangeet Natak Akademi's 2020 'Gender Equity Policy' regarding female representation, and was it achieved?

options.label: A
options.text: The policy mandated 30% female representation among fellowship recipients and jury members, a target achieved in the 2022 fellowship cycle with 34% female awardees.

options.label: B
options.text: The policy mandated 33% reservation for women in all Akademi-affiliated gurukuls, achieved by 2023.

options.label: C
options.text: The policy applied retroactively to fellowships awarded before 2020, resulting in a review of past awardees.

options.label: D
options.text: The policy mandated equal gender representation (50%) in all decision-making bodies by 2025.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The policy mandated 30% female representation among fellowship recipients and jury members, a target achieved in the 2022 fellowship cycle with 34% female awardees..

questions.text: Which statement correctly distinguishes between the Madras Devadasis (Prevention of Dedication) Act, 1947 and the Karnataka Devadasi (Prohibition of Dedication) Act, 1988 based on the lesson?

options.label: A
options.text: Both Acts were passed by the Central Parliament and applied uniformly across India.

options.label: B
options.text: The 1947 Act criminalised dedication but automatically conferred performance rights on former devadasis, unlike the 1988 Act.

options.label: C
options.text: The Acts differ in jurisdiction (Madras vs Karnataka) and penalty provisions, and neither automatically conferred performance rights on former devadasis.

options.label: D
options.text: The 1988 Karnataka Act was the first legislation to dismantle the devadasi system; the 1947 Madras Act only regulated it.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The Acts differ in jurisdiction (Madras vs Karnataka) and penalty provisions, and neither automatically conferred performance rights on former devadasis..

questions.text: Regarding the colonial classification of Indian performing arts, the text identifies the primary driver for the categorisation into "classical", "folk", and "tribal" as:

options.label: A
options.text: The indigenous aesthetic theories of the Natyashastra and Sangita Ratnakara which provided a ready-made taxonomy for British scholars.

options.label: B
options.text: The administrative requirements of the colonial state, specifically revenue assessment, law-and-order monitoring, and the formulation of cultural policy.

options.label: C
options.text: The missionary objective of documenting "heathen" practices to facilitate targeted religious conversion efforts in rural areas.

options.label: D
options.text: The scholarly pursuit of comparative musicology by the Asiatic Society of Bengal, aimed at establishing a universal history of world music.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The administrative requirements of the colonial state, specifically revenue assessment, law-and-order monitoring, and the formulation of cultural policy..

questions.text: In the context of the Legal Framework for Geographical Indications (GI) of traditional art forms, which of the following distinctions is correctly drawn based on the lesson?

options.label: A
options.text: The Geographical Indications Act, 1999 and the Copyright Act, 1957 protect the same subject matter but differ only in their enforcement mechanisms.

options.label: B
options.text: Registration under the GI Act requires only proof of antiquity of the art form, without needing to establish a link between geography and product quality.

options.label: C
options.text: Recognition as a "classical" art form by the Sangeet Natak Akademi confers statutory intellectual property rights equivalent to a GI registration.

options.label: D
options.text: The GI Act protects subject matter distinct from the Copyright Act, and mere honorary recognition by the Sangeet Natak Akademi does not grant statutory legal protection.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The GI Act protects subject matter distinct from the Copyright Act, and mere honorary recognition by the Sangeet Natak Akademi does not grant statutory legal protection..

questions.text: The lesson describes the pedagogical shift from the Gurukul system to institutional curricula in Classical Dance. Which statement best captures the current reality of this transition according to the text?

options.label: A
options.text: The guru-shishya parampara has been completely replaced by university degree programmes, rendering hereditary lineages obsolete.

options.label: B
options.text: Hereditary lineages continue to exist parallel to university programmes and often supply faculty to these institutions, indicating a coexistence rather than replacement.

options.label: C
options.text: Institutionalisation led to the standardisation of notation for dance, which was previously impossible due to the purely abstract nature of the guru-shishya oral tradition.

options.label: D
options.text: The Bhatkhande Music Institute (1926) and Madras Music Academy (1928) were established specifically to dismantle the guru-shishya system and enforce state-approved curricula.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Hereditary lineages continue to exist parallel to university programmes and often supply faculty to these institutions, indicating a coexistence rather than replacement..

questions.text: The Indo-Gangetic Plain is divided into three sub-regions based on the river systems that feed them. Which sub-region is characterised by a braided channel network and frequent avulsions?

options.label: A
options.text: The Punjab-Haryana plain fed by the Indus system

options.label: B
options.text: The Ganga plain dominated by the Ganga and its tributaries

options.label: C
options.text: The Brahmaputra plain characterised by a braided channel network and frequent avulsions

options.label: D
options.text: The Rajasthan plain fed by the Luni river system

questions.solution: Correct answer: The Brahmaputra plain characterised by a braided channel network and frequent avulsions.

questions.text: Regarding the Peninsular Plateau, which statement accurately reflects the geological features of the Deccan Traps and the Western Ghats?

options.label: A
options.text: The Deccan Traps are composed of granitic gneiss formed during the Precambrian, while the Western Ghats are a young fold mountain range parallel to the west coast.

options.label: B
options.text: The Deccan Traps consist of basaltic lava flows creating a stepped topography, and the Western Ghats form a continuous escarpment influencing orographic rainfall and hosting high biodiversity.

options.label: C
options.text: The Deccan Traps are sedimentary formations of the Paleozoic era, and the Western Ghats are discontinuous low hills with minimal climatic influence.

options.label: D
options.text: The Deccan Traps are metamorphic rocks of the Archaean age, while the Western Ghats are volcanic mountains formed by recent tectonic activity.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The Deccan Traps consist of basaltic lava flows creating a stepped topography, and the Western Ghats form a continuous escarpment influencing orographic rainfall and hosting high biodiversity..

questions.text: The Himalayan rivers exhibit high sediment load and dynamic channel patterns. Which of the following is a direct consequence of the high sediment flux in the Ganga-Brahmaputra system as mentioned in the lesson?

options.text: Creation of the Rann of Kutch as a seasonal salt marsh

options.text: Development of the Lakshadweep coral atolls in the Arabian Sea

questions.solution: Correct answer: Building of the Bengal delta and the Sundarbans mangrove forest.

questions.text: Peninsular rivers show pronounced seasonal variability. Which river basin is noted for receiving significant rainfall from both the southwest and northeast monsoons, resulting in a bimodal hydrograph that supports double-cropping in its delta?

options.label: A
options.text: The Godavari basin

options.label: B
options.text: The Krishna basin

questions.text: Which of the following statements correctly describes the interaction between the Indian Ocean Dipole (IOD) and ENSO as discussed in the lesson?

options.label: A
options.text: A positive IOD always enhances the monsoon irrespective of the ENSO phase.

options.text: A positive IOD can offset the monsoon‑suppressing effect of an El Niño, as illustrated by the 1997‑98 event.

questions.text: Regarding the Ken‑Betwa river interlinking project, which detail is accurate according to the lesson?

questions.text: What is the correct characterisation of hard‑rock aquifers and their recharge requirements as per the lesson?

options.label: B
options.text: Hard‑rock aquifers rely on fracture networks, so recharge structures must target weathered zones.

questions.text: Which statement about seismic zonation in India reflects the lesson’s emphasis on micro‑zonation?

options.text: Micro‑zonation reveals strong intra‑zone variability within Zone V.

questions.text: Based on the lesson, which combination of sea‑level rise data and Coastal Regulation Zone (CRZ) 2019 provisions is correct?

options.text: Mean sea‑level rise along the Indian coast is 5 mm/yr uniformly across both seas.

questions.text: Which thrust in the Himalayan thrust stack records the highest present‑day convergence rate according to GPS measurements?

questions.text: Which of the following statements regarding River Basin Organisations (RBOs) in India is correct?

options.text: All glacial lakes in the Hindu Kush-Himalaya region are classified as potentially dangerous by ICIMOD.

questions.text: Which of the following approaches is emphasized for urban flood resilience in the lesson?

options.label: A
options.text: Exclusive reliance on enlarging storm-water drain capacity to handle peak rainfall events.

options.label: B

questions.text: With reference to the Inter-State River Water Disputes Act and tribunal awards, which of the following statements is correct?

questions.text: Which of the following sets of evidence is explicitly cited in the lesson as supporting the theory of plate tectonics?

questions.text: Which of the following statements accurately describes the relationship between thermohaline circulation, upwelling, and marine productivity as explained in the lesson?

questions.text: In the mixed‑layer heat budget equation ∂T/∂t = (Qnet − Qpen)/ρcₚh − wₑ(T − Tₑ)/h, what does the term wₑ(T − Tₑ)/h represent?

questions.text: In periglacial environments, the active layer and the permafrost table are distinct features. Which statement accurately describes their relationship?

questions.text: In Oxygen Minimum Zones (OMZs), fixed nitrogen loss occurs through multiple microbial pathways. What does the lesson indicate about the relative roles of denitrification and anammox?

questions.text: In the context of continental rift evolution, numerical models indicate that a critical stretching factor (β) must be exceeded for continental breakup to occur. What is the approximate threshold range for β, and what is the consequence if this threshold is not met?

options.text: The Persian-to-English language shift in 1835 and the founding of the Anjuman-e-Taraqqi-e-Urdu in 1903

options.label: D
options.text: The Partition of Bengal in 1905 and the subsequent formation of the Nagari Pracharini Sabha in 1910

questions.solution: Correct answer: Fort William College and the Nagari Pracharini Sabha in the early 19th century.

questions.text: Regarding the textual transmission and authorship of women's devotional compositions in Bhakti and Sufi traditions, which statement is supported by the lesson?

options.label: A
options.text: Mirabai's padas exist in a single, authoritative autograph manuscript preserved in the Vallabha Sampradaya archives.

options.label: B
options.text: The Divya Prabandham was compiled contemporaneously with the Alvars, ensuring the authenticity of Andal's attributions.

options.label: C
options.text: Akka Mahadevi's vachanas appear in the Siddhanta Shikhamani and Vachana Sahitya collections compiled by later Virashaiva monks, revealing editorial standardization.

options.label: D
options.text: Lal Ded's vakhs were written down by her during her lifetime in the Sharada script, preserving the original Kashmiri phonology.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Akka Mahadevi's vachanas appear in the Siddhanta Shikhamani and Vachana Sahitya collections compiled by later Virashaiva monks, revealing editorial standardization..

questions.text: The doctrinal consequences of pramana differences are illustrated in the lesson by specific examples. Which of the following pairings of a school's pramana acceptance with its doctrinal application is correctly stated?

options.label: A
options.text: Nyaya's acceptance of upamana (comparison) underwrites its theory of analogy in medical diagnosis.

options.label: B
options.text: Mimamsa's acceptance of arthapatti (presumption) is indispensable for interpreting Vedic injunctions that are not directly observable.

options.label: C
options.text: Advaita's acceptance of anupalabdhi (non-perception) is used to prove the positive existence of Brahman.

options.label: D
options.text: Buddhism's denial of testimony as an independent pramana forces a reliance on the Buddha's words as perceptually validated.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Mimamsa's acceptance of arthapatti (presumption) is indispensable for interpreting Vedic injunctions that are not directly observable..

questions.text: Which statement accurately describes the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute's Mahabharata critical edition (1919‑1966)?

options.label: A
options.text: It classified manuscripts into eastern and western recensions and recorded about 5,000 variant passages.

options.label: B
options.text: It used a stemmatic method, classified manuscripts into northern and southern recensions, and recorded over 12,000 variant passages.

options.label: C
options.text: It was completed in 1919 and relied on a single manuscript from Nepal.

options.label: D
options.text: It adopted the vulgate text based on the oldest manuscripts from Gujarat and Bengal.

questions.solution: Correct answer: It used a stemmatic method, classified manuscripts into northern and southern recensions, and recorded over 12,000 variant passages..

questions.text: In the key methodological steps for producing a critical edition, which step involves hypothesizing genealogical relationships among manuscripts?

options.label: A
options.text: Manuscript survey and cataloguing across repositories.

options.label: B
options.text: Collation of readings using a base manuscript.

options.label: C
options.text: Construction of a stemma codicum to hypothesize genealogical relationships.

options.label: D
options.text: Publication of a critical apparatus recording all significant variants.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Construction of a stemma codicum to hypothesize genealogical relationships..

questions.text: What distinctive feature characterizes the Bengali Krittibasi Ramayan (c. 1400) by Krittibas Ojha?

options.label: A
options.text: It was composed in the ovi metre for kirtan performance.

options.label: B
options.text: It presented a philosophical exposition aligned with the Warkari tradition.

options.label: C
options.text: It transformed Valmiki’s narrative into a devotional poem emphasizing Rama’s accessibility to common folk.

options.label: D
options.text: It was rendered in three stages by the Kavitrayam poets.

questions.solution: Correct answer: It transformed Valmiki’s narrative into a devotional poem emphasizing Rama’s accessibility to common folk..

questions.text: Which statement correctly describes the Buddhist concept of Anatman?

options.label: A
options.text: Anatman asserts the complete non-existence of any continuity, amounting to nihilism.

options.label: B
options.text: Anatman denies a permanent self but affirms causal continuity through dependent origination.

options.label: C
options.text: Anatman posits an eternal soul (jiva) that transmigrates across births.

options.label: D
options.text: Anatman is identical to the Upanishadic Atman but expressed in negative terminology.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Anatman denies a permanent self but affirms causal continuity through dependent origination..

questions.text: How did Amir Khusrau adapt the Persian Masnavi form in the Indian context?

options.label: A
options.text: He used the Masnavi's quatrain structure (aaba) for philosophical verses on wine and fate.

options.label: B
options.text: He employed the Masnavi's rhymed couplets to compose Sufi narratives infused with Indian seasonal imagery.

options.label: C
options.text: He introduced the radif and qafiya conventions of the ghazal into the Masnavi.

options.label: D
options.text: He translated the Masnavi into Sanskrit for courtly recitation.

questions.solution: Correct answer: He employed the Masnavi's rhymed couplets to compose Sufi narratives infused with Indian seasonal imagery..

questions.text: Which of the following statements accurately describes Alauddin Khalji's market control measures as discussed in the lesson?

options.label: A
options.text: They were primarily aimed at reducing the tax burden on peasants while increasing merchant profits.

options.label: B
options.text: They fixed prices of essential commodities and imposed strict grain procurement systems to finance military campaigns.

options.label: C
options.text: They abolished the iqta system and replaced it with a direct cash salary system for all military officers.

options.label: D
options.text: They focused exclusively on controlling the spice trade with Southeast Asia through naval dominance.

questions.solution: Correct answer: They fixed prices of essential commodities and imposed strict grain procurement systems to finance military campaigns..

questions.text: The Battle of Talikota (1565) led to which of the following outcomes for the Vijayanagara Empire according to the lesson?

options.label: A
options.text: The complete and immediate annexation of all Vijayanagara territories by the Deccan Sultanates.

options.label: B
options.text: The sack of the capital city and a shift of political focus to southern Nayaka kingdoms, though the empire lingered in reduced form.

options.label: C
options.text: A decisive Vijayanagara victory that secured its northern frontiers for another century.

options.label: D
options.text: The forced conversion of the Vijayanagara rulers to Islam and the imposition of jizya.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The sack of the capital city and a shift of political focus to southern Nayaka kingdoms, though the empire lingered in reduced form..

questions.text: How did Akbar's religious policy of Sulh-i-Kul differ from Aurangzeb's approach as described in the lesson?

options.label: A
options.text: Akbar imposed Islamic law strictly while Aurangzeb promoted a composite culture blending Persian and Indian elements.

options.label: B
options.text: Akbar's Sulh-i-Kul represented an ideological commitment to inclusivity fostering a composite culture, whereas Aurangzeb's orthodoxy reversed this trend contributing to dissent.

options.label: C
options.text: Both rulers pursued identical policies of religious tolerance but differed in their administrative terminology.

options.label: D
options.text: Aurangzeb continued Akbar's Sulh-i-Kul but extended it to include European Christian communities.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Akbar's Sulh-i-Kul represented an ideological commitment to inclusivity fostering a composite culture, whereas Aurangzeb's orthodoxy reversed this trend contributing to dissent..

questions.text: Which feature of the Ahom Kingdom in the Northeast is highlighted in the lesson as distinctive?

options.label: A
options.text: Its adoption of the Mughal mansabdari system for military administration.

options.label: B
options.text: Its successful resistance against Mughal expansion through guerrilla warfare and diplomatic negotiations.

options.label: C
options.text: Its establishment of a maritime trade network linking the Brahmaputra valley to Southeast Asian ports.

options.label: D
options.text: Its early conversion to Islam under Mughal suzerainty in the 16th century.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Its successful resistance against Mughal expansion through guerrilla warfare and diplomatic negotiations..

questions.text: The Maratha Confederacy's fiscal policy of "chauth" is best described in the lesson as:

options.label: A
options.text: A land revenue assessment based on the iqta system allocated to military officers.

options.label: B
options.text: A tribute levied at one-fourth of the revenue of territories not under direct Maratha control, transforming a regional power into a pan-Indian confederacy.

options.label: C
options.text: A tax on maritime trade collected at ports like Surat to finance naval expansion.

options.label: D
options.text: A religious tax imposed on non-Hindu populations to fund temple construction.

questions.solution: Correct answer: A tribute levied at one-fourth of the revenue of territories not under direct Maratha control, transforming a regional power into a pan-Indian confederacy..

questions.text: Which of the following was a key feature of Alauddin Khalji's reformed iqta system?

options.label: A
options.text: Hereditary grants to muqtis

options.label: B
options.text: Revenue collected in kind

options.label: C
options.text: Land measurement (paimaish) and cash revenue deposit

options.label: D
options.text: No audits of muqti accounts

questions.solution: Correct answer: Land measurement (paimaish) and cash revenue deposit.

questions.text: What did the introduction of the "du‑aspah sih‑aspah" distinction under Jahangir allow a mansabdar to do?

options.label: A
options.text: Increase his zat without changing sawar

options.label: B
options.text: Hold a higher sawar than his zat

options.label: C
options.text: Make his jagir hereditary

options.label: D
options.text: Reduce his cavalry obligation

questions.solution: Correct answer: Hold a higher sawar than his zat.

questions.text: Which statement accurately describes the kavali tribute in the Vijayanagara Nayankara system?

options.label: A
options.text: It was a fixed cash amount paid annually

options.label: B
options.text: It was periodically reassessed based on agricultural output

options.label: C
options.text: It was collected directly by the emperor's central treasury

options.label: D
options.text: It was identical to the Mughal mansabdari revenue assignment

questions.solution: Correct answer: It was periodically reassessed based on agricultural output.

questions.text: How did chauth differ from sardeshmukhi in Maratha fiscal practice?

options.label: A
options.text: Both were identical levies of 25% of the assessed revenue

options.label: B
options.text: Chauth was a protective tribute (25% of jama) while sardeshmukhi was a superior zamindari claim (10% of jama)

options.label: C
options.text: Sardeshmukhi was collected by Mughal officials on behalf of the Marathas

options.label: D
options.text: Chauth was a direct land tax paid by peasants to the Maratha state

questions.solution: Correct answer: Chauth was a protective tribute (25% of jama) while sardeshmukhi was a superior zamindari claim (10% of jama).

questions.text: According to the data provided for c. 1650, which Deccan sultanate possessed the greatest number of heavy cannon?

options.label: A
options.text: Ahmadnagar

options.label: B
options.text: Bijapur

options.label: C
options.text: Golconda

options.label: D
options.text: Bidar

questions.solution: Correct answer: Bijapur.

questions.text: Which of the following statements accurately describes Sher Shah Suri's standardization of land measurement?

options.label: A
options.text: He adopted the existing Lodi bigha of 2,500 square yards for imperial use.

options.label: B
options.text: He introduced a uniform bigha of 3,025 square yards, replacing heterogeneous local units.

options.label: C
options.text: He retained the jarib of 60 gaz as the primary measuring rod for all surveys.

options.label: D
options.text: He delegated measurement standards to hereditary qanungos without central oversight.

questions.solution: Correct answer: He introduced a uniform bigha of 3,025 square yards, replacing heterogeneous local units..

questions.text: Regarding the Mughal dahsala system under Akbar, which statement is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: It mandated an annual reassessment of land revenue based on current harvest yields.

options.label: B
options.text: It fixed the state demand at one-half of the estimated produce for all crop categories.

options.label: C
options.text: It used a decennial (ten-year) average of actual yields to smooth seasonal fluctuations.

options.label: D
options.text: It applied uniformly to all provinces including the Deccan subahs from 1580 onwards.

questions.solution: Correct answer: It used a decennial (ten-year) average of actual yields to smooth seasonal fluctuations..

questions.text: The origin of the double-dome technique in Indo-Islamic architecture is correctly attributed to:

options.label: A
options.text: Mughal architects under Humayun, first seen in his tomb at Delhi.

options.label: B
options.text: Lodi period tombs, later refined by Mughal architects.

options.label: C
options.text: Persian master builders imported during Akbar's reign.

options.label: D
options.text: The Suri dynasty, as evidenced by Sher Shah's tomb at Sasaram.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Lodi period tombs, later refined by Mughal architects..

questions.text: Which statement best reflects the operational reality of the Portuguese cartaz system in Mughal India?

options.label: A
options.text: It was uniformly enforced on all Asian shipping without exception.

options.label: B
options.text: Mughal vessels frequently obtained exemptions through imperial farmans.

options.label: C
options.text: It applied only to European ships entering Portuguese-controlled ports.

options.label: D
options.text: It was abolished by Akbar's firman of 1573 granting free trade to all.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Mughal vessels frequently obtained exemptions through imperial farmans..

questions.text: The fundamental distinction between the Maratha 'sea-chauth' and the land 'chauth' was that the sea-chauth:

options.label: A
options.text: Was a 25% protective tribute levied on agrarian revenue in coastal districts.

options.label: B
options.text: Functioned as a customs duty on shipping entering the Konkan littoral.

options.label: C
options.text: Was collected by the Portuguese on behalf of the Angres under treaty.

options.label: D
options.text: Applied only to European vessels and exempted Indian merchantmen.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Functioned as a customs duty on shipping entering the Konkan littoral..

questions.text: What was the principal fiscal innovation of Jahangir's du-aspah sih-aspah mansab classification introduced around 1620?

options.label: A
options.text: It allowed the sawar (cavalry) rank to exceed the zat (personal) rank without a proportional increase in salary.

options.label: B
options.text: It merged the zat and sawar ranks into a single unified rank to simplify payroll.

options.label: C
options.text: It reduced the zat rank of all mansabdars by half to cut treasury expenditure.

options.label: D
options.text: It mandated that jagir revenue assignments be paid in cash rather than land grants.

questions.solution: Correct answer: It allowed the sawar (cavalry) rank to exceed the zat (personal) rank without a proportional increase in salary..

questions.text: Which of the following best describes the integrative function of the Mahanayakacharya in the Vijayanagara Empire?

options.label: A
options.text: He served solely as the commander-in-chief of the imperial army during wartime.

options.label: B
options.text: He coordinated nayaka appointments, temple revenues, irrigation works, and trade mediation to align provincial power with central policy.

options.label: C
options.text: He functioned as the chief priest of the Virupaksha temple, legitimizing royal authority through ritual.

options.label: D
options.text: He was the empire's chief revenue auditor, responsible only for assessing land tax yields.

questions.solution: Correct answer: He coordinated nayaka appointments, temple revenues, irrigation works, and trade mediation to align provincial power with central policy..

questions.text: The Ahom paik system is most accurately characterized as:

options.label: A
options.text: A land revenue tax collected in kind from peasant cultivators.

options.label: B
options.text: A corvée labour obligation tied to hereditary land grants (gaonburha) and mandatory military service.

options.text: A mercenary recruitment system where soldiers were paid fixed salaries from the royal treasury.

questions.text: Regarding Maratha revenue administration, which statement correctly distinguishes the kamavisdar from the Mughal faujdar?

options.label: A
options.text: The kamavisdar was a military governor with judicial powers, while the faujdar was a pure revenue collector.

options.label: B
options.text: The kamavisdar operated on a salary-plus-commission basis as a revenue officer, whereas the faujdar was primarily a military-administrative governor.

options.label: C
options.text: The kamavisdar held hereditary and non-revocable tenure, unlike the transferable faujdar.

options.label: D
options.text: The kamavisdar reported directly to the Peshwa's household, while the faujdar reported to the provincial diwan.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The kamavisdar operated on a salary-plus-commission basis as a revenue officer, whereas the faujdar was primarily a military-administrative governor..

questions.text: The resilience of Deccan Sultanate forts during prolonged sieges (e.g., Bijapur 1565, Golconda 1686) depended critically on:

options.label: A

options.label: B
options.text: Subterranean karez channels feeding internal cisterns (hauz) that secured water and logistical endurance.

options.label: C
options.text: The exclusive use of heavy bronze cannon mounted on curtain walls for offensive bombardment.

options.label: D
options.text: Diplomatic alliances with European trading companies for ammunition resupply by sea.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Subterranean karez channels feeding internal cisterns (hauz) that secured water and logistical endurance..

questions.text: The Battle of Plassey (1757) was fought between the British East India Company and

questions.text: Consider the following statements about the Government of India Act, 1935: 1. It provided for provincial autonomy. 2. It established a Federal Court. 3. It abolished separate electorates. 4. It introduced dyarchy at the centre. Which of the statements given above are correct?

questions.text: The States Reorganisation Act (1956) created states primarily on which basis?

questions.text: The Pitt's India Act of 1784 introduced a dual system of control over British India. Which of the following correctly describes this dual system?

questions.text: Which of the following statements accurately distinguishes the Permanent Settlement of Bengal from the Ryotwari system?

questions.text: The "drain of wealth" theory articulated by early Indian nationalists primarily referred to:

questions.text: The Doctrine of Lapse, articulated by Lord Dalhousie in 1848, led to the annexation of several princely states. Which of the following states was NOT annexed under this doctrine according to the lesson?

questions.text: Regarding the Ilbert Bill controversy, which statement reflects the final compromise as described in the lesson?

questions.text: Which of the following correctly describes the origin and nature of the first Famine Codes in British India?
