options.text: The Famine Codes were formulated by the Famine Commission of 1901 and applied uniformly across all provinces from 1902.

options.label: B
options.text: The Strachey Commission (1880) produced the first Famine Codes, which were issued province-wise and often ignored in practice.

options.label: C
options.text: The Famine Codes emerged from the 1857 Revolt's aftermath and mandated gratuitous relief as the primary relief mode.

options.label: D
options.text: The Codes were a central legislation passed by the Imperial Legislative Council in 1880, binding on all provincial governments.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The Strachey Commission (1880) produced the first Famine Codes, which were issued province-wise and often ignored in practice..

questions.text: Consider the following political associations: (1) British Indian Association, (2) Indian Association, (3) Poona Sarvajanik Sabha, (4) National Conference. Which sequence correctly orders them by year of foundation?
questions.solution: Correct answer: 1-3-2-4.

questions.text: Which of the following statements regarding the post-1857 reorganisation of the Indian Army is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: The Peel Commission (1859) recommended a ratio of one British soldier to three Indian soldiers.

options.label: B
options.text: The "martial races" doctrine was first codified in the Kitchener Reforms of 1902.

options.label: C
options.text: The Punjab Frontier Force, raised from 1849, became the model for selective recruitment based on the martial races theory.

options.label: D
options.text: The Bengal Army was retained intact after 1857 but its recruitment base was shifted to the Punjab.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The Punjab Frontier Force, raised from 1849, became the model for selective recruitment based on the martial races theory..

questions.text: With reference to the "guarantee system" for railway construction in India (1849-1869), which statement is accurate?

options.label: A
options.text: It guaranteed a 5% annual return on paid-up capital to private companies, backed by the Government of India.

options.label: B
options.text: It continued unchanged until 1885, by which time the network reached 9,000 miles.

options.label: C
options.text: The system applied to state-built railways after 1869 under the State Railway Department.

options.label: D
options.text: It ensured a 5% return on total capital expenditure including government subsidies.

questions.solution: Correct answer: It guaranteed a 5% annual return on paid-up capital to private companies, backed by the Government of India..

questions.text: What was the status of the Indian rupee's monetary standard during the period 1835-1885 as described in the lesson?

options.label: A
options.text: The rupee was placed on a gold-exchange standard in 1835 following the Coinage Act.

options.label: B
options.text: The rupee remained on a silver standard throughout the period; the gold-exchange standard was adopted only in 1899.

options.label: C
options.text: The rupee operated on a bimetallic standard with fixed gold-silver ratio after 1857.

options.label: D
options.text: The Currency Act of 1861 formally adopted the gold-exchange standard for India.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The rupee remained on a silver standard throughout the period; the gold-exchange standard was adopted only in 1899..

questions.text: Regarding Lord Ripon's Resolution of 1882 on local self-government, which of the following is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: It immediately introduced elected majorities in all municipal bodies across British India.

options.label: B
options.text: It applied only to the three Presidency towns of Bombay, Calcutta, and Madras.

options.label: C
options.text: Implementation varied, and many municipal bodies retained nominated majorities until the 1890s.

options.label: D
options.text: It was the same legislative measure as the Calcutta Municipal Act of 1876.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Implementation varied, and many municipal bodies retained nominated majorities until the 1890s..

questions.text: Which method characterises the Moderate phase (1885‑1905) of the Indian National Congress?

options.label: A
options.text: Boycott of British goods and promotion of Swadeshi

options.label: B
options.text: Prayer and petition: delegations to London, memoranda to the Secretary of State, and resolutions at annual sessions

options.label: C
options.text: Armed revolutionary activity and secret societies

options.label: D
options.text: Mass civil disobedience and non‑cooperation

questions.solution: Correct answer: Prayer and petition: delegations to London, memoranda to the Secretary of State, and resolutions at annual sessions.

questions.text: What ideological influences shaped the Extremist critique of British rule (1905‑1910)?

options.label: A
options.text: Faith in British constitutionalism and gradual reform

options.label: B
options.text: Writings of Bankim Chandra Chatterjee, Swami Vivekananda, and the Irish nationalist experience

options.label: C
options.text: Theosophical teachings of Annie Besant and the demand for dominion status

options.label: D
options.text: Acceptance of the Morley‑Minto Reforms as a sufficient step toward self‑government

questions.solution: Correct answer: Writings of Bankim Chandra Chatterjee, Swami Vivekananda, and the Irish nationalist experience.

questions.text: Which feature distinguishes the Home Rule Movement (1915‑1918) from the earlier Moderate and Extremist phases?

options.label: A
options.text: Demand for complete independence (Purna Swaraj) through revolutionary violence

options.label: B
options.text: Organisation of mass enrolment leagues, public lectures, and petition drives demanding dominion status within the Empire

options.label: C
options.text: Reliance solely on petitions to the British Parliament without any public mobilisation

options.label: D
options.text: Introduction of separate electorates for Muslims through the Morley‑Minto Reforms

questions.solution: Correct answer: Organisation of mass enrolment leagues, public lectures, and petition drives demanding dominion status within the Empire.

questions.text: According to the lesson, what was the approximate weekly print run of Kesari by 1908?

options.label: A
options.text: 2,000 copies

options.label: B
options.text: 5,000 copies

options.label: C
options.text: 12,000 copies

options.label: D
options.text: 20,000 copies

questions.solution: Correct answer: 12,000 copies.

questions.text: The 27,000 enrolled members figure mentioned in the lesson refers to which Home Rule League?

options.label: A
options.text: Tilak’s Indian Home Rule League

options.label: B
options.text: Besant’s All‑India Home Rule League

options.label: C
options.text: Combined membership of both leagues

options.label: D
options.text: Membership of the Joint Committee

questions.solution: Correct answer: Besant’s All‑India Home Rule League.

questions.text: The Rowlatt Committee (1918) recommended the continuation of which powers in peacetime, leading to the Rowlatt Act 1919?

options.label: A
options.text: Powers under the Defence of India Act 1915

options.label: B
options.text: Powers under the Indian Press Act 1910

options.label: C
options.text: Powers under the Newspaper (Incitement to Offences) Act 1908

options.label: D
options.text: Powers under the Rowlatt Act 1919 itself

questions.solution: Correct answer: Powers under the Defence of India Act 1915.

questions.text: What factor prompted the establishment of the Tata Iron and Steel Company (TISCO) at Jamshedpur in 1907, according to the lesson?

options.label: A
options.text: British government subsidies

options.label: B
options.text: Boycott of British piece‑goods creating a temporary market for Indian yarn

options.label: C
options.text: The 1909 Tariff Board granting protective duties to Indian mills

options.label: D
options.text: The Swadeshi Stores cooperative model

questions.solution: Correct answer: Boycott of British piece‑goods creating a temporary market for Indian yarn.

questions.text: Which statement correctly reflects a distinction highlighted in the lesson between the extremist demand and the Home Rule League demand?

options.label: A
options.text: The Home Rule Leagues demanded complete Swaraj, while extremists demanded dominion status.

options.label: B
options.text: The extremists demanded complete Swaraj, while the Home Rule Leagues demanded self‑government on colonial lines (dominion status).

options.label: C
options.text: Both extremists and Home Rule Leagues demanded complete independence from the outset.

options.label: D
options.text: The moderates endorsed economic non‑cooperation alongside the extremists.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The extremists demanded complete Swaraj, while the Home Rule Leagues demanded self‑government on colonial lines (dominion status)..

questions.text: Which of the following accurately describes a key political consequence of the 1911 reversal of the Partition of Bengal, as distinct from the 1905 partition itself?

options.label: A
options.text: It led to the immediate grant of separate electorates for Muslims through the Morley-Minto Reforms of 1909.

options.label: B
options.text: The creation of Bihar and Orissa as a separate province altered the demographic balance in the Bengal legislative council, strengthening the Muslim League's platform for separate electorates.

options.label: C
options.text: The capital shift from Calcutta to Delhi was primarily intended to appease the Bengali intelligentsia and reduce revolutionary violence.

options.label: D
options.text: Moderates and Extremists within the Indian National Congress unanimously welcomed the annulment as a victory for constitutional agitation.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The creation of Bihar and Orissa as a separate province altered the demographic balance in the Bengal legislative council, strengthening the Muslim League's platform for separate electorates..

questions.text: Regarding the Ghadar Party and the Home Rule Movement, which statement correctly identifies a fundamental difference in their objectives and methods?

options.label: A
options.text: Both movements sought dominion status through constitutional pressure within the British Empire.

options.label: B
options.text: The Ghadar Party aimed for complete independence through armed revolt leveraging the First World War, while the Home Rule Leagues demanded dominion status through constitutional pressure.

options.label: C
options.text: The Home Rule Movement was a transnational network founded by Indian expatriates in North America, whereas the Ghadar Party operated primarily within India.

options.label: D
options.text: The Ghadar Party's newspaper 'Ghadar' was published openly in Calcutta, while the Home Rule League's 'New India' circulated clandestinely aboard ships.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The Ghadar Party aimed for complete independence through armed revolt leveraging the First World War, while the Home Rule Leagues demanded dominion status through constitutional pressure..

questions.text: The Indian Press Act of 1910 selectively suppressed nationalist newspapers primarily through which financial mechanism?

options.label: A
options.text: Imposition of heavy customs duties on imported newsprint and printing machinery.

options.label: B
options.text: Mandatory security deposits that could be forfeited for 'seditious' content, disproportionately affecting low-circulation revolutionary papers.

options.label: C
options.text: A progressive tax on newspaper circulation revenue that targeted high-readership moderate journals.

options.label: D
options.text: Licensing fees scaled to the political affiliation of the editor, with higher fees for known extremists.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Mandatory security deposits that could be forfeited for 'seditious' content, disproportionately affecting low-circulation revolutionary papers..

questions.text: How did the Montagu Declaration of 1917 differ from a firm promise of immediate dominion status, and how did key nationalist factions respond?

options.label: A
options.text: It committed to 'progressive realisation' of responsible government without a timetable; Moderates welcomed it, Extremists rejected it as inadequate, and Home Rule leaders demanded clearer guarantees.

options.label: B
options.text: It promised immediate dominion status after the war; all factions united in support, leading to the 1919 Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms.

options.label: C
options.text: It offered only provincial autonomy with no central responsibility; Moderates opposed it, while Extremists and Home Rule leaders accepted it as a first step.

options.label: D
options.text: It declared full independence as the ultimate goal with a fixed 1920 deadline; the British retracted it under pressure from the Ghadar Party.

questions.solution: Correct answer: It committed to 'progressive realisation' of responsible government without a timetable; Moderates welcomed it, Extremists rejected it as inadequate, and Home Rule leaders demanded clearer guarantees..

questions.text: Which of the following represents an unprecedented formal organisational role for women in the Home Rule Movement (1916-1918), as distinct from their participation in the earlier Swadeshi Movement?

options.label: A
options.text: Women served as 'district organisers' in Annie Besant's Home Rule League, a formal title with defined responsibilities like coordinating lecture tours and managing vernacular pamphlet distribution.

options.label: B
options.text: Women participated in picketing foreign cloth shops and burning imported goods, activities that began during Swadeshi and continued unchanged into Home Rule.

options.label: C
options.text: Women were elected as presidents of provincial Home Rule League branches, exercising authority over male members.

options.label: D
options.text: Women's involvement was limited to fundraising and attending meetings, with no formal organisational positions in either movement.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Women served as 'district organisers' in Annie Besant's Home Rule League, a formal title with defined responsibilities like coordinating lecture tours and managing vernacular pamphlet distribution..

questions.text: The 1905 Russo-Japanese War influenced Extremist strategic thinking in India primarily by:

options.label: A
options.text: Providing a model for constitutional petitioning within the British imperial framework

options.label: B
options.text: Demonstrating that an Asian power could defeat a European power through modernisation and national spirit

options.label: C
options.text: Encouraging the Moderates to accelerate negotiations for the Morley-Minto Reforms

options.label: D
options.text: Leading to the immediate formation of the Ghadar Party in Punjab

questions.solution: Correct answer: Demonstrating that an Asian power could defeat a European power through modernisation and national spirit.

questions.text: Regarding the Anushilan Samiti and Jugantar, which statement accurately reflects their organisational relationship as described in the lesson?

options.label: A
options.text: Jugantar was founded in 1902 as the parent organisation of Anushilan Samiti

options.label: B
options.text: Anushilan Samiti (founded 1902) and Jugantar (emerged 1906) were distinct, with Jugantar as a more militant splinter faction

options.label: C
options.text: Both organisations were founded simultaneously in 1906 as parallel revolutionary groups in Bengal and Punjab

options.label: D
options.text: Anushilan Samiti was a cultural organisation while Jugantar was its political wing

questions.solution: Correct answer: Anushilan Samiti (founded 1902) and Jugantar (emerged 1906) were distinct, with Jugantar as a more militant splinter faction.

questions.text: The 1916 Lucknow Pact's provision for Muslim weightage in legislative councils was:

options.label: A
options.text: A permanent constitutional guarantee that could not be altered without Muslim League consent

options.label: B
options.text: Superseded by the 1919 Government of India Act and later negotiations

options.label: C
options.text: Rejected by the Congress at the 1917 Home Rule Conference

options.label: D
options.text: Extended to all minorities including Sikhs and Christians in the same session

questions.solution: Correct answer: Superseded by the 1919 Government of India Act and later negotiations.

questions.text: The fundamental difference between the Home Rule Movement's demand (1916-1918) and the later 'Purna Swaraj' resolution (1929) was that the former:

options.label: A
options.text: Demanded complete severance from the British Crown

options.label: B
options.text: Accepted Crown suzerainty in external affairs while seeking full internal autonomy

options.label: C
options.text: Was based on the American republican model rather than the British dominion model

options.label: D
options.text: Explicitly rejected the Montagu Declaration's promise of responsible government

questions.solution: Correct answer: Accepted Crown suzerainty in external affairs while seeking full internal autonomy.

questions.text: According to the lesson, what was the nature of Rabindranath Tagore's engagement with the extremist nationalist movement during the cultural renaissance?

options.label: A
options.text: He was the principal ideologue providing the philosophical foundation for revolutionary violence in Bengal.

options.label: B
options.text: He actively led the Ganapati and Shivaji festivals in Maharashtra to mobilize the masses for extremist causes.

options.label: C
options.text: He held nuanced and often critical views of militant nationalism, despite the renaissance providing fertile ground for extremism.

options.label: D
options.text: He collaborated closely with the Anushilan Samiti and Jugantar to integrate cultural revival with armed struggle.

questions.solution: Correct answer: He held nuanced and often critical views of militant nationalism, despite the renaissance providing fertile ground for extremism..

questions.text: What was the specific constitutional commitment made by the British Government in the Montagu Declaration of 1917?

options.label: A
options.text: Immediate grant of Home Rule (self-government) to India on par with the Dominions.

options.label: B
options.text: Progressive realisation of responsible government in India as an integral part of the British Empire.

options.label: C
options.text: Establishment of a fully elected legislative assembly with control over the executive (Swaraj).

options.label: D
options.text: Implementation of the Lucknow Pact provisions regarding separate electorates and provincial autonomy.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Progressive realisation of responsible government in India as an integral part of the British Empire..

questions.text: Which of the following best describes the financial constraint faced by nationalist movements during the Swadeshi and Home Rule phase, as highlighted in the lesson?

options.label: A
options.text: Complete reliance on British government grants for funding political activities.

options.label: B
options.text: Dependence on foreign capital from Germany and Turkey to sustain revolutionary activities.

options.label: C
options.text: Perpetual challenge of consistent and substantial funding despite widespread popular support.

options.label: D
options.text: State-sponsored fundraising through mandatory taxation powers granted by the Morley-Minto Reforms.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Perpetual challenge of consistent and substantial funding despite widespread popular support..

questions.text: Which legislative measure enacted in 1910 mandated publishers to deposit security with the government, liable to forfeiture for publishing seditious material, leading to the closure of many nationalist newspapers?

options.label: A
options.text: Newspapers (Incitement to Offences) Act, 1908

options.label: B
options.text: Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1908

options.label: C
options.text: Press Act, 1910

options.label: D
options.text: Defence of India Act, 1915

questions.solution: Correct answer: Press Act, 1910.

questions.text: Which of the following accurately describes the principal reason the Rowlatt Act of 1919 provoked nationwide opposition?

options.label: A
options.text: It was passed with the unanimous support of Indian members of the Imperial Legislative Council.

options.label: B
options.text: It extended wartime emergency powers into peacetime, allowing detention without trial and restricting civil liberties.

options.label: C
options.text: It was a direct response to the Non‑Cooperation Movement launched by Gandhi in 1920.

options.label: D
options.text: It granted full civil liberties and abolished preventive detention.

questions.solution: Correct answer: It extended wartime emergency powers into peacetime, allowing detention without trial and restricting civil liberties..

questions.text: What was Gandhi's immediate response to the Jallianwala Bagh massacre on 13 April 1919?

options.label: A
options.text: He intensified the Rowlatt Satyagraha and called for a nationwide strike.

options.label: B
options.text: He suspended the satyagraha on 18 April 1919, arguing the movement had lost its non‑violent character.

options.label: C
options.text: He demanded the immediate repeal of the Rowlatt Act and the prosecution of General Dyer.

options.label: D
options.text: He announced the launch of the Non‑Cooperation Movement at the Nagpur session.

questions.solution: Correct answer: He suspended the satyagraha on 18 April 1919, arguing the movement had lost its non‑violent character..

questions.text: Which sequence correctly links the major events of the Civil Disobedience Movement (1930‑1934) as described in the lesson?

options.label: A
options.text: Declaration of Purna Swaraj → Salt March → Gandhi‑Irwin Pact → Second Round Table Conference → Communal Award.

options.label: B
options.text: Salt March → Declaration of Purna Swaraj → Gandhi‑Irwin Pact → Communal Award → Second Round Table Conference.

options.label: C
options.text: Gandhi‑Irwin Pact → Salt March → Declaration of Purna Swaraj → Second Round Table Conference → Communal Award.

options.label: D
options.text: Communal Award → Salt March → Declaration of Purna Swaraj → Gandhi‑Irwin Pact → Second Round Table Conference.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Declaration of Purna Swaraj → Salt March → Gandhi‑Irwin Pact → Second Round Table Conference → Communal Award..

questions.text: Which woman is credited with operating an underground radio station during the Quit India Movement (1942)?

options.label: A
options.text: Sarojini Naidu

options.label: B
options.text: Usha Mehta

options.label: C
options.text: Kasturba Gandhi

options.label: D
options.text: Rani Gaidinliu

questions.solution: Correct answer: Usha Mehta.

questions.text: In which year was the All India Kisan Sabha founded and who was its first president?

options.label: A
options.text: 1934, N. G. Ranga

options.label: B
options.text: 1936, Swami Sahajanand Saraswati

options.label: C
options.text: 1939, Indulal Yagnik

options.label: D
options.text: 1942, Communist Party of India

questions.solution: Correct answer: 1936, Swami Sahajanand Saraswati.

questions.text: What was the primary factor that galvanised Indian public opinion in favour of the Indian National Army (INA)?

options.label: A
options.text: Military victories of the INA in Burma

options.label: B
options.text: The Red Fort Trials of INA officers

options.label: C
options.text: Subhas Chandra Bose's radio broadcasts from Southeast Asia

options.label: D
options.text: The formation of the Azad Hind Government in Singapore

questions.solution: Correct answer: The Red Fort Trials of INA officers.

questions.text: According to the lesson, what was the purpose of the 'opt‑out' clause included in the Cripps Mission proposals?

options.label: A
options.text: To grant full sovereign power to individual provinces

options.label: B
options.text: To legitimise the partition of India

options.label: C
options.text: To ensure the accession of princely states to the Union

options.label: D
options.text: To provide immediate independence without conditions

questions.solution: Correct answer: To legitimise the partition of India.

questions.text: The Poona Pact (1932) replaced the separate electorates for the Depressed Classes, as provided in the Communal Award, with which arrangement?

options.label: A
options.text: Separate electorates for Muslims only

options.label: B
options.text: Reserved seats in joint electorates

options.label: C
options.text: Universal adult franchise for all communities

options.label: D
options.text: A weighted voting system favouring landlords

questions.solution: Correct answer: Reserved seats in joint electorates.

questions.text: Which feature was introduced by the Government of India Act 1935 but was absent in the 1919 Act?

options.label: A
options.text: Dyarchy at the provincial level

options.label: B
options.text: Full provincial autonomy with all subjects transferred

options.label: C
options.text: Limited franchise based on property qualifications

options.label: D
options.text: Separate electorates for Muslims only

questions.solution: Correct answer: Full provincial autonomy with all subjects transferred.

questions.text: Which of the following was NOT a measure undertaken by the Congress ministries formed in 1937?

options.label: A
options.text: Release of political prisoners

options.label: B
options.text: Introduction of tenancy legislation to protect peasants

options.label: C
options.text: Nationalisation of railways

options.label: D
options.text: Promotion of khadi and village industries

questions.solution: Correct answer: Nationalisation of railways.

questions.text: What was the immediate trigger for the Royal Indian Navy mutiny in February 1946?

options.label: A
options.text: Demand for higher pay and better pensions

options.label: B
options.text: Racial discrimination, poor food, and the arrest of a rating for writing a slogan

options.label: C
options.text: Refusal to obey orders to sail to Southeast Asia

options.label: D
options.text: Political demand for immediate independence

questions.solution: Correct answer: Racial discrimination, poor food, and the arrest of a rating for writing a slogan.

questions.text: According to the lesson, which factor structured the outbreaks of partition violence rather than them being purely spontaneous?

options.label: A
options.text: Sudden economic collapse in Punjab and Bengal

options.label: B
options.text: Administrative delays in the Radcliffe Award and the political rhetoric of Direct Action Day

options.label: C
options.text: Absence of British military personnel after 1945

options.label: D
options.text: Long‑standing religious animosity without political mediation

questions.solution: Correct answer: Administrative delays in the Radcliffe Award and the political rhetoric of Direct Action Day.

questions.text: Which organisational step did Jinnah take after the 1937 elections to expand the Muslim League’s mass base?

options.label: A
options.text: Launching a new English‑language newspaper

options.label: B
options.text: Appointing provincial organising secretaries and opening district‑level offices

options.label: C
options.text: Forming a coalition government with the Congress in United Provinces

options.label: D
options.text: Requesting the British to increase Muslim representation in the civil services

questions.solution: Correct answer: Appointing provincial organising secretaries and opening district‑level offices.

questions.text: Which of the following statements accurately describes the British censorship regime against the vernacular press between 1919 and 1947?

options.label: A
options.text: The Indian Press Act of 1910 was repealed after the Non-Cooperation Movement and replaced by a single comprehensive Defence of India Rules.

options.label: B
options.text: The Indian Press (Emergency Powers) Act of 1931 empowered district magistrates to demand security deposits, seize presses, and imprison editors.

options.label: C
options.text: During the Quit India Movement, the British permitted Congress-affiliated papers to operate under strict guidelines to monitor nationalist sentiment.

options.label: D
options.text: The Defence of India Rules were invoked only during the 1942 Quit India phase and not during World War II's earlier years.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The Indian Press (Emergency Powers) Act of 1931 empowered district magistrates to demand security deposits, seize presses, and imprison editors..

questions.text: Regarding the 1943 Bengal Famine, which factor was a deliberate wartime policy choice by the colonial administration rather than a natural calamity?

options.label: A
options.text: The severe cyclone in October 1942 that destroyed the aman harvest.

options.label: B
options.text: The Japanese occupation of Burma cutting off rice imports.

options.label: C
options.text: The 'denial policy' involving destruction of boats and stockpiles to prevent Japanese use.

options.label: D
options.text: The global shipping shortage caused by Allied military requirements.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The 'denial policy' involving destruction of boats and stockpiles to prevent Japanese use..

questions.text: The integration of princely states into the Indian Union (1945-1948) involved which combination of methods?

options.label: A
options.text: Exclusively diplomatic negotiations and standstill agreements without any military intervention.

options.label: B
options.text: Military action in Hyderabad, plebiscites in Junagadh and Kashmir, and popular uprisings in Travancore.

options.label: C
options.text: A uniform process of referendums supervised by the United Nations across all princely states.

options.label: D
options.text: Voluntary accession by all rulers following the lapse of paramountcy, with no resistance encountered.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Military action in Hyderabad, plebiscites in Junagadh and Kashmir, and popular uprisings in Travancore..

questions.text: The INA Trials (1945-46) significantly eroded British authority primarily because:

options.label: A
options.text: The courts-martial strictly followed legal procedures and convicted all defendants, demonstrating British judicial fairness.

options.label: B
options.text: The trials functioned as political theatre that mobilised both civilians and serving soldiers, triggering the RIN mutiny and mass protests.

options.label: C
options.text: The Congress and Muslim League boycotted the trials, denying them political legitimacy and forcing British withdrawal.

options.label: D
options.text: The British government immediately pardoned all INA officers after the first trial to appease Indian public opinion.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The trials functioned as political theatre that mobilised both civilians and serving soldiers, triggering the RIN mutiny and mass protests..

questions.text: How did the Congress Socialist Party (CSP) differ from the Communist Party of India (CPI) during the 1934-1942 period?

options.label: A
options.text: The CSP operated outside the Congress, advocated revolutionary violence, and followed the Comintern's 'popular front' line.

options.label: B
options.text: The CSP remained a ginger group within Congress, accepted parliamentary methods, and rejected the Comintern's 'popular front' line.

options.label: C
options.text: The CSP merged with the CPI in 1938 to form a united left front for the 1937 provincial elections.

options.label: D
options.text: The CSP opposed the Quit India Movement, while the CPI supported it unconditionally after 1941.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The CSP remained a ginger group within Congress, accepted parliamentary methods, and rejected the Comintern's 'popular front' line..

questions.text: Which statement correctly distinguishes the Bombay Plan (1944) from the 1956 Industrial Policy Resolution?

options.label: A
options.text: The Bombay Plan was a government resolution while the 1956 Resolution was drafted by industrialists.

options.label: B
options.text: The Bombay Plan was a memorandum drafted by leading Indian industrialists, whereas the 1956 Industrial Policy Resolution was a government policy document.

options.label: C
options.text: Both the Bombay Plan and the 1956 Resolution were drafted by the Indian National Congress.

options.label: D
options.text: The 1956 Industrial Policy Resolution was a business‑drafted memorandum similar to the Bombay Plan.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The Bombay Plan was a memorandum drafted by leading Indian industrialists, whereas the 1956 Industrial Policy Resolution was a government policy document..

questions.text: What key factor compelled the Attlee Labour government to announce a definitive deadline for British withdrawal from India in February 1947?

options.label: A
options.text: Purely ideological commitment to Indian self‑government.

options.label: B
options.text: Intense pressure from the Indian National Congress leadership.

options.label: C
options.text: War‑exhausted finances, a balance‑of‑payments crisis, and the need to demobilise two million Indian soldiers.

options.label: D
options.text: A direct demand from the Muslim League for immediate partition.

questions.solution: Correct answer: War‑exhausted finances, a balance‑of‑payments crisis, and the need to demobilise two million Indian soldiers..

questions.text: Which description accurately reflects the mechanics of the 1946 Cabinet Mission’s grouping scheme?

options.label: A
options.text: It was solely a British design that ignored the Muslim League’s demand for autonomous Muslim zones.

options.label: B
options.text: It created a three‑tier grouping (Sections A, B, C) to preserve a united India while conceding provincial autonomy to Muslim‑majority zones.

options.label: C

questions.text: Regarding the Soviet‑Afghan War (1979‑1989), the lesson emphasizes that the conflict’s outcome cannot be attributed to a single factor. Which combination of external supports does the lesson identify as equally critical to the mujahideen’s resistance?

questions.text: The 1990‑91 Gulf War is distinguished from the 2003 Iraq War by its legal basis. Which UN Security Council resolution provided explicit authorisation for the use of force in the Gulf War?

questions.text: The Maastricht Treaty (1992) transformed the European Community into the European Union. Which of the following accurately describes its key institutional innovations?

questions.text: With reference to the Cabinet Mission Plan of 1946 and the Cripps Mission of 1942, which of the following statements is correct?

questions.text: The Government of India Act, 1935 is described in the lesson as the 'structural backbone' of the Indian Constitution. Which of the following features of the present Constitution is NOT primarily derived from the 1935 Act?

options.label: C

questions.solution: Correct answer: Parliamentary system of government with collective responsibility of the Council of Ministers to the Legislature.

questions.text: Which of the following best describes the 'Quasi-Federal' character of the Indian Constitution as highlighted in the lesson?

questions.text: Which Supreme Court case introduced the "date of judgment" rule that laws placed in the Ninth Schedule before 24 April 1973 are immune from basic‑structure review, while those inserted thereafter are subject to it?

questions.text: Which statement correctly describes the effect of the doctrine of eclipse on a pre‑Constitutional law that conflicts with a Fundamental Right?

questions.text: According to Supreme Court jurisprudence, which category of rights under Part III of the Constitution is non‑waivable?

questions.solution: Correct answer: The Bommai guidelines mandate a floor test in the state assembly before dissolution and require the Centre to place the material for President's satisfaction before Parliament..

questions.text: Regarding the flexi-fund mechanism under Centrally Sponsored Schemes as revised by the 15th Finance Commission (2021-26), which statement is accurate?

options.label: D
options.text: States require prior Union Cabinet approval for each flexi-fund utilisation plan submitted to the line ministry.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The 25% flexi-fund ceiling applies scheme-wise, and re-allocated funds must remain within the broad sectoral objectives of the respective CSS..

questions.text: With reference to the National Data Governance Framework Policy (NDGFP) and digital federalism, which of the following is correct?

questions.solution: Correct answer: The NDGFP is a draft executive policy that currently lacks statutory enforceability and does not mandate inter-state data sharing..

questions.text: Concerning the 101st Constitutional Amendment (GST) and the compensation regime, which statement is correct based on the State of Kerala v. Union of India (2023) judgment?

questions.text: In the context of the Inter-State Council's role in water disputes, which of the following accurately describes its function and outcomes in the Cauvery, Krishna, and Mahadayi cases?

questions.solution: Correct answer: The ISC's recommendations in the Cauvery dispute led to the constitution of the Cauvery Water Management Authority and Regulation Committee, illustrating its role as a political facilitator..

questions.text: Which of the following correctly describes a change in horizontal devolution criteria from the 14th to the 15th Finance Commission?

questions.text: Under Article 304 of the Constitution, as interpreted in the context of GST, what restriction applies to state taxation powers on inter-state goods?

questions.text: Which of the following statements correctly describes the doctrinal evolution of Article 14 as per the Supreme Court's jurisprudence?

questions.text: Referring to the Supreme Court's observation in Divisional Manager, Aravali Golf Club v. Chander Hass (2008), which principle of judicial conduct was emphasised to counter the risks of judicial activism?

options.label: A
options.text: The doctrine of prospective overruling to limit the retrospective effect of judgments

options.label: B
options.text: The doctrine of judicial restraint, cautioning courts against becoming 'super-administrators'

options.label: C
options.text: The principle of stare decisis, requiring strict adherence to precedent in administrative matters

options.label: D
options.text: The principle of separation of powers, directing the executive to frame guidelines for judicial appointments

questions.solution: Correct answer: The doctrine of judicial restraint, cautioning courts against becoming 'super-administrators'.

questions.text: Which case first articulated the Basic Structure Doctrine, holding that certain constitutional features cannot be amended by Parliament under Article 368?

options.label: A
options.text: Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala (1973)

options.label: B
options.text: Minerva Mills Ltd. v. Union of India (1980)

options.label: C
options.text: Waman Rao v. Union of India (1981)

options.label: D
options.text: I.R. Coelho v. State of Tamil Nadu (2007)

questions.solution: Correct answer: Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala (1973).

questions.text: Which judicial test provides that constitutional amendments made before 24 April 1973 are immune from challenge under the Basic Structure Doctrine?

options.label: A
options.text: Essential Features Test

options.label: B
options.text: Width Test

options.label: C
options.text: Prospective Application

options.label: D
options.text: Identity Test

questions.solution: Correct answer: Prospective Application.

questions.text: Under which constitutional articles do the Supreme Court and the High Courts derive their inherent power to punish contempt of themselves?

options.label: A
options.text: Articles 129 and 215

options.label: B
options.text: Articles 130 and 216

options.label: C
options.text: Articles 128 and 214

options.label: D
options.text: Articles 131 and 217

questions.solution: Correct answer: Articles 129 and 215.

questions.text: Which statement correctly distinguishes the in‑house procedure for judicial accountability from the statutory impeachment process under the Judges Inquiry Act?

options.label: A
options.text: The in‑house procedure is a statutory mechanism, while impeachment is constitutional.

options.label: B
options.text: The in‑house procedure is an internal administrative mechanism, while impeachment is a statutory process under the Judges Inquiry Act.

options.label: C
options.text: Both the in‑house procedure and impeachment are statutory processes enacted by Parliament.

options.label: D
options.text: Both the in‑house procedure and impeachment derive directly from the Constitution.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The in‑house procedure is an internal administrative mechanism, while impeachment is a statutory process under the Judges Inquiry Act..

questions.text: The Judicial Service Commission (JSC) with a 23‑member composition including the Chief Justice, Ministers, MPs, legal practitioners and civil‑society representatives is a feature of which country’s judicial appointment model?

options.label: A
options.text: United Kingdom

options.label: B
options.text: United States

options.label: C
options.text: South Africa

options.label: D
options.text: India

questions.solution: Correct answer: South Africa.

questions.text: In Union Carbide Corporation v. Union of India (1991), the Supreme Court refused to increase the compensation awarded under the Bhopal Gas Leak Disaster (Processing of Claims) Act, 1985, while exercising its power under Article 142. Which principle did this decision reinforce?

options.label: A
options.text: Article 142 empowers the Court to modify statutory compensation amounts when justice so requires.

options.label: B
options.text: Article 142 cannot be used to override substantive statutory provisions or create new rights.

options.label: C
options.text: The Court may invoke Article 142 to fill legislative gaps even if a specific statute governs the matter.

options.label: D
options.text: Orders under Article 142 are not binding on the legislature, only on the executive.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Article 142 cannot be used to override substantive statutory provisions or create new rights..

questions.text: Which of the following is a mandatory procedural requirement for a curative petition to be entertained by the Supreme Court, as laid down in Rupa Ashok Hurra v. Ashok Hurra (2002)?

options.label: A
options.text: The petition must be filed within 30 days of the dismissal of the review petition.

options.label: B
options.text: The petitioner must have exhausted all remedies under Article 226 before approaching the Supreme Court.

options.label: C
options.text: The petition must be certified by a senior advocate of the Supreme Court attesting that it meets the Hurra criteria.

options.label: D
options.text: The petition must demonstrate that the earlier judgment violated a fundamental right under Part III of the Constitution.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The petition must be certified by a senior advocate of the Supreme Court attesting that it meets the Hurra criteria..

questions.text: Regarding the hierarchy of standards for judicial review of administrative action in India, which statement accurately reflects the Supreme Court's position?

options.label: A
options.text: Wednesbury unreasonableness is the highest standard and applies exclusively to cases involving fundamental rights.

options.label: B
options.text: Proportionality applies only to administrative discretion involving economic policy, while Wednesbury applies to all other cases.

options.label: C
options.text: Legitimate expectation creates a substantive enforceable right that binds the administration to its prior representation.

options.label: D
options.text: Wednesbury is the baseline for non-fundamental-right cases; proportionality applies when fundamental rights are engaged; legitimate expectation adds a procedural fairness layer.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Wednesbury is the baseline for non-fundamental-right cases; proportionality applies when fundamental rights are engaged; legitimate expectation adds a procedural fairness layer..

questions.text: In the context of inter-state water disputes, what is the relationship between the Supreme Court's original jurisdiction under Article 131 and the tribunals constituted under the Inter-State Water Disputes Act, 1956?

options.label: A
options.text: The Supreme Court has no jurisdiction once a tribunal is constituted under the 1956 Act; its award is final and non-appealable.

options.label: B
options.text: The tribunals under the 1956 Act are the primary adjudicators, while the Supreme Court retains appellate and supervisory jurisdiction, including enforcement of awards.

options.label: C
options.text: Article 131 allows the Supreme Court to adjudicate water disputes only if both states consent to bypass the tribunal mechanism.

options.label: D
options.text: The Supreme Court can only issue interim directions under Article 131; final adjudication rests exclusively with the tribunal.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The tribunals under the 1956 Act are the primary adjudicators, while the Supreme Court retains appellate and supervisory jurisdiction, including enforcement of awards..

questions.text: The Supreme Court in Union of India v. G. Ganayutham (1997) clarified the scope of the doctrine of legitimate expectation. Which of the following correctly states the Court's holding?

options.label: A
options.text: Legitimate expectation creates a substantive right enforceable against the government, akin to a fundamental right.

options.label: B
options.text: Legitimate expectation arises only from a statutory provision, not from executive representations or consistent practice.

options.label: C
options.text: Legitimate expectation does not create a substantive right but entitles the claimant to a fair hearing before the expectation is frustrated.

options.label: D
options.text: The doctrine of legitimate expectation applies only to contractual obligations of the state, not to policy decisions.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Legitimate expectation does not create a substantive right but entitles the claimant to a fair hearing before the expectation is frustrated..

questions.text: Regarding post-retirement appointments of Supreme Court judges, which of the following statements is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: Article 124(7) imposes a complete ban on accepting any government office after retirement.

options.label: B
options.text: The 230th Law Commission Report recommended a mandatory two-year cooling-off period before taking up government positions.

options.label: C
options.text: A constitutional amendment enacted in 2009 mandates a cooling-off period for all High Court judges.

options.label: D
options.text: The 14th Law Commission Report endorsed such appointments to utilize judicial expertise for the nation.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The 230th Law Commission Report recommended a mandatory two-year cooling-off period before taking up government positions..

questions.text: Which of the following is identified as a measure to address judicial delays through Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR)?

options.label: A
options.text: Making arbitration awards appealable in High Courts as a matter of right to ensure fairness.

options.label: B
options.text: Establishing Lok Adalats and promoting mediation to divert disputes from the formal court system.

options.label: C
options.text: Mandating that all commercial disputes above a specified value must undergo compulsory adjudication.

options.label: D
options.text: Restricting the jurisdiction of Gram Nyayalayas to only criminal compoundable offences.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Establishing Lok Adalats and promoting mediation to divert disputes from the formal court system..

questions.text: What is the current status of Judicial Impact Assessment (JIA) in India's legislative process?

options.label: A
options.text: It is a mandatory constitutional requirement for all Bills introduced in Parliament under Article 117.

options.label: B
options.text: It has been fully institutionalised through the Judicial Impact Assessment Act, 2017.

options.label: C
options.text: It remains a recommended reform that is largely absent in practice and not a formal part of the process.

options.label: D
options.text: It is conducted exclusively by the Law Commission of India for every subordinate legislation.

questions.solution: Correct answer: It remains a recommended reform that is largely absent in practice and not a formal part of the process..

questions.text: Regarding the 'Restatement of Values of Judicial Life' (1997), which statement is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: It is a legally enforceable statute enacted by Parliament to regulate judicial conduct.

options.label: B
options.text: It mandates the public disclosure of assets and liabilities of all Supreme Court and High Court judges.

options.label: C
options.text: It serves as a guiding resolution adopted by the Supreme Court outlining ethical principles for judges.

options.label: D
options.text: It establishes an independent Judicial Complaints Commission to investigate allegations of misconduct.

questions.solution: Correct answer: It serves as a guiding resolution adopted by the Supreme Court outlining ethical principles for judges..

questions.text: The 73rd and 74th Constitutional Amendments were enacted to give mandatory constitutional status to local bodies. Which of the following statements correctly reflects the legislative intent behind these amendments as described in the lesson?

options.label: A
options.text: They were enacted to implement the recommendations of the Ashok Mehta Committee of 1977.

options.label: B
options.text: They were rooted in Article 40 of the Directive Principles of State Policy, which exhorts the State to organise village panchayats as units of self-government.

options.label: C
options.text: They aimed to replace the three-tier system recommended by the Balwant Rai Mehta Committee with a two-tier structure for administrative efficiency.

options.label: D
options.text: They were primarily a response to the 72nd Amendment Bill which lapsed due to the dissolution of the Lok Sabha in 1991.

questions.solution: Correct answer: They were rooted in Article 40 of the Directive Principles of State Policy, which exhorts the State to organise village panchayats as units of self-government..

questions.text: Regarding the protection of tenure for elected representatives under the 73rd Amendment, which of the following statements is accurate?

options.label: A
options.text: A Panchayat can be dissolved by the State Government at any time on grounds of administrative inefficiency.

options.label: B
options.text: The Governor can dissolve a Panchayat before the expiry of its term only on grounds specified in the Constitution.

options.label: C
options.text: The State Election Commission has the authority to dissolve a Panchayat if elections are not held on time.

options.label: D
options.text: A Panchayat dissolved before its term expires must be reconstituted within three months, failing which the State Government assumes its functions.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The Governor can dissolve a Panchayat before the expiry of its term only on grounds specified in the Constitution..

questions.text: The 74th Amendment mandates the constitution of Ward Committees in municipalities. What is the population threshold specified in the Constitution for this requirement?

options.label: A
options.text: One lakh or more

options.label: B
options.text: Two lakh or more

options.label: C
options.text: Three lakh or more

options.label: D
options.text: Five lakh or more

questions.solution: Correct answer: Three lakh or more.

questions.text: With reference to the State Finance Commission (SFC) mandated by the 73rd and 74th Amendments, which of the following statements is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: The SFC is constituted by the President of India every five years to review the financial position of Panchayats and Municipalities.

options.label: B
options.text: The SFC recommends the distribution of net proceeds of taxes between the State and local bodies, and determines the grants-in-aid to local bodies from the Consolidated Fund of the State.

options.label: C
options.text: The SFC's recommendations are binding on the State Government and do not require legislative approval.

options.label: D
options.text: The SFC replaces the Central Finance Commission in matters relating to local body finances.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The SFC recommends the distribution of net proceeds of taxes between the State and local bodies, and determines the grants-in-aid to local bodies from the Consolidated Fund of the State..

questions.text: Which of the following statements correctly describes a key structural difference between the District Planning Committee (DPC) and the Metropolitan Planning Committee (MPC) as per Articles 243ZD and 243ZE?

options.label: A
options.text: The DPC chairperson is always the District Collector, while the MPC chairperson is always the Mayor.

options.label: B
options.text: The DPC includes elected members of Panchayats and Municipalities, while the MPC includes elected members of Municipal Corporations and Councils only.

options.label: C
options.text: The DPC is constituted in all districts, whereas the MPC is constituted only in metropolitan areas with a population of ten lakh or more.

options.label: D
options.text: The DPC prepares a Metropolitan Development Plan, while the MPC prepares a District Development Plan.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The DPC is constituted in all districts, whereas the MPC is constituted only in metropolitan areas with a population of ten lakh or more..

questions.text: Under the Panchayats (Extension to Scheduled Areas) Act, 1996 (PESA), which of the following is true?

options.label: A
options.text: PESA extends Part IX of the Constitution to Sixth Schedule areas.

options.label: B
options.text: The Gram Sabha under PESA has ownership of minor forest produce and the power to prevent land alienation.

options.label: C
options.text: PESA mandates that the State Governor appoints the Chairperson of the Gram Sabha.

options.label: D
options.text: PESA applies uniformly to all tribal areas irrespective of Schedule.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The Gram Sabha under PESA has ownership of minor forest produce and the power to prevent land alienation..

questions.text: Regarding the State Election Commission (SEC) in India, which statement is correct as per the lesson and Supreme Court jurisprudence?

options.label: A
options.text: The Constitution fixes a uniform five‑year tenure for the State Election Commissioner across all states.

options.label: B
options.text: The Supreme Court in State of Uttar Pradesh v. Rajesh Kumar (2020) held that the SEC must be independent of the state executive and its tenure cannot be altered at the pleasure of the government.

options.label: C
options.text: The SEC is appointed by the Chief Minister and serves at the pleasure of the state government.

options.label: D
options.text: The SEC’s independence is guaranteed only for the conduct of Panchayat elections, not for municipal elections.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The Supreme Court in State of Uttar Pradesh v. Rajesh Kumar (2020) held that the SEC must be independent of the state executive and its tenure cannot be altered at the pleasure of the government..

questions.text: Which of the following is a condition for release of performance grants to local bodies under the Fifteenth Finance Commission?

options.label: A
options.text: Submission of a five‑year perspective plan approved by the State Legislature.

options.label: B
options.text: Maintenance of audited accounts, asset registers, and achievement of service‑level benchmarks.

options.label: C
options.text: Completion of at least 80% of the works sanctioned under MGNREGA in the previous year.

options.label: D
options.text: Direct election of the Mayor in the municipal corporation.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Maintenance of audited accounts, asset registers, and achievement of service‑level benchmarks..

questions.text: Which Supreme Court judgment affirmed that a directly elected Mayor cannot be reduced to a ceremonial figurehead and struck down a state amendment transferring executive powers to a state‑appointed Commissioner?

options.label: A
options.text: Rameshwar Prasad v. State of Bihar (2021).

options.label: B
options.text: State of Karnataka v. Union of India (2022).

options.label: C
options.text: K. Chandrasekhar v. State of Tamil Nadu (2018).

options.label: D
options.text: Gram Panchayat, Kothapally v. State of Telangana (2023).

questions.solution: Correct answer: K. Chandrasekhar v. State of Tamil Nadu (2018)..

questions.text: Which State has issued a comprehensive activity‑mapping notification that assigns each of the 29 Eleventh Schedule subjects to a specific Panchayat tier and identifies the functionaries to be transferred?

options.label: A
options.text: Kerala

options.label: B
options.text: Karnataka

options.label: C
options.text: Maharashtra

options.label: D
options.text: Tamil Nadu

questions.solution: Correct answer: Kerala.

questions.text: The three‑step institutional mechanism for activity mapping described in the lesson includes all of the following EXCEPT:

options.label: A
options.text: Drafting of the matrix by a State‑level committee chaired by the Chief Secretary or Minister for Panchayati Raj

options.label: B
options.text: Ratification of the draft by the State Legislature

options.label: C
options.text: Approval by the Union Ministry of Panchayati Raj

options.label: D
options.text: Publication of the final notification in the State Gazette

questions.solution: Correct answer: Approval by the Union Ministry of Panchayati Raj.

questions.text: As per the 2022 Panchayat elections, what percentage of all elected positions nationwide were occupied by women?
questions.solution: Correct answer: 46%.

questions.text: How many core common applications are included in the e‑Panchayat Mission Mode Project?
questions.solution: Correct answer: 11.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a requirement stipulated by SEBI for a municipality to issue municipal bonds?

options.label: A
options.text: A credit rating

options.label: B
options.text: A track record of audited accounts

options.label: C
options.text: A sinking fund

options.label: D
options.text: A minimum population of one million

questions.solution: Correct answer: A minimum population of one million.

questions.text: Which of the following taxes subsumed under the Goods and Services Tax historically formed a significant share of municipal own‑source revenue?

options.label: A
options.text: Property tax

options.label: B
options.text: Entry tax

options.label: C
options.text: Professional tax

options.label: D
options.text: Stamp duty

questions.solution: Correct answer: Entry tax.

questions.text: Which statement correctly describes the status of Participatory Budgeting in Indian Urban Local Bodies?

options.label: A
options.text: It is a mandatory feature under the 74th Constitutional Amendment

options.label: B
options.text: It has been adopted uniformly across all States through central legislation

options.label: C
options.text: Only a few States have legislated it, while the 74th Amendment provides for Ward Committees

options.label: D
options.text: It is implemented exclusively through the District Planning Committee

questions.solution: Correct answer: Only a few States have legislated it, while the 74th Amendment provides for Ward Committees.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about State Election Commissions (SECs) is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: The Election Commission of India directly supervises local body elections

options.label: B
options.text: SECs derive their powers from Articles 243K and 243ZA and are independent of the ECI

options.label: C
options.text: Delimitation of local constituencies is carried out by the Delimitation Commission of India

options.label: D
options.text: The FC‑XV SEC Strengthening Grant is conditional on the SEC being headed by a retired Supreme Court judge

questions.solution: Correct answer: SECs derive their powers from Articles 243K and 243ZA and are independent of the ECI.

questions.text: As per the National Disaster Management Plan 2019, which of the following is a requirement for accessing the 15th Finance Commission’s Local Body Disaster Mitigation Grants?

options.label: A
options.text: Existence of approved Local Disaster Management Plans

options.label: B
options.text: Completion of a state‑level climate risk assessment

options.label: C
options.text: Allocation of 10% of municipal budget to disaster mitigation

options.label: D
options.text: Signing of a memorandum of understanding with the National Disaster Response Force

questions.solution: Correct answer: Existence of approved Local Disaster Management Plans.

questions.text: Which of the following correctly states the procedural requirement for moving an Adjournment Motion in the Lok Sabha?

options.label: A
options.text: Support of at least 30 members and the Speaker's consent

options.label: B
options.text: Support of at least 50 members and the Speaker's consent

options.label: C
options.text: Support of at least 50 members only

options.label: D
options.text: Support of at least 100 members and the Speaker's consent

questions.solution: Correct answer: Support of at least 50 members and the Speaker's consent.

questions.text: Regarding the Speaker's certification of a Money Bill under Article 110, which statement is accurate?

options.label: A
options.text: The certification is final and cannot be challenged in any court

options.label: B
options.text: The certification can be challenged only through a parliamentary resolution

options.label: C
options.text: The certification is subject to judicial review and cannot be a colourable exercise of power

options.label: D
options.text: The certification requires prior concurrence of the Rajya Sabha

questions.solution: Correct answer: The certification is subject to judicial review and cannot be a colourable exercise of power.

questions.text: What is the correct status of Department‑Related Standing Committee (DRSC) reports in relation to the executive?

options.label: A
options.text: They are binding on the government and must be implemented

options.label: B
options.text: They are recommendatory, but the government must present an Action Taken Report

options.label: C
options.text: They are advisory only to the Speaker and have no executive relevance

options.label: D
options.text: They automatically become law once adopted by the House

questions.solution: Correct answer: They are recommendatory, but the government must present an Action Taken Report.

questions.text: Which of the following correctly distinguishes a Policy Cut Motion from a Token Cut Motion?

options.label: A
options.text: Policy Cut reduces the demand to Re 1; Token Cut reduces the demand by Rs 100

options.label: B
options.text: Policy Cut reduces the demand by Rs 100; Token Cut reduces the demand to Re 1

options.label: C
options.text: Both reduce the demand to Re 1

options.label: D
options.text: Both reduce the demand by Rs 100

questions.solution: Correct answer: Policy Cut reduces the demand to Re 1; Token Cut reduces the demand by Rs 100.

questions.text: Which statement accurately describes the Rajya Sabha's powers in financial legislation?

options.label: A
options.text: It can amend or reject the Appropriation Bill

options.label: B
options.text: It can introduce Money Bills under Article 110

options.label: C
options.text: It can only discuss and make recommendations on the Finance Bill and cannot vote on Demands for Grants

options.label: D
options.text: It possesses a veto over the Appropriation Bill

questions.solution: Correct answer: It can only discuss and make recommendations on the Finance Bill and cannot vote on Demands for Grants.

questions.text: What are the prescribed notice periods for a Starred Question and a Short‑Notice Question in the Lok Sabha?

options.label: A
options.text: 15 clear days for Starred; 3 days for Short‑Notice

options.label: B
options.text: 10 clear days for Starred; 5 days for Short‑Notice

options.label: C
options.text: 20 clear days for Starred; 7 days for Short‑Notice

options.label: D
options.text: 15 clear days for both Starred and Short‑Notice

questions.solution: Correct answer: 15 clear days for Starred; 3 days for Short‑Notice.

questions.text: How much maximum debate time is allotted to each Private Member's Bill in the Lok Sabha?

options.label: A
options.text: Thirty minutes on Fridays (or the last sitting day of the week)

options.label: B
options.text: One hour on any sitting day

options.label: C
options.text: Two hours on Fridays

options.label: D
options.text: No fixed limit; the Speaker decides case by case

questions.solution: Correct answer: Thirty minutes on Fridays (or the last sitting day of the week).

questions.text: What is the nature of the recommendations made by the Committee on Public Undertakings (COPU) and what follow‑up is required from the government?

options.label: A
options.text: Binding on the government; no further report needed

options.label: B
options.text: Advisory, but the government must submit an Action Taken Report

options.label: C
options.text: Purely advisory with no obligation for an Action Taken Report

options.label: D
options.text: Enforceable by Parliament through a separate resolution

questions.solution: Correct answer: Advisory, but the government must submit an Action Taken Report.

questions.text: Which category of international treaties must be enacted by Parliament before they become domestically enforceable?

options.label: A
options.text: All treaties signed by the executive

options.label: B
options.text: Only treaties that require domestic legislation for implementation

options.label: C
options.text: Only executive agreements

options.label: D
options.text: Only treaties ratified by the President

questions.solution: Correct answer: Only treaties that require domestic legislation for implementation.

questions.text: In which House can a Motion of No‑Confidence be moved, and what is the minimum number of members whose written support is required?

options.label: A
options.text: Lok Sabha; at least fifty members

options.label: B
options.text: Rajya Sabha; at least fifty members

options.label: C
options.text: Lok Sabha; at least one hundred members

options.label: D
options.text: Either House; at least fifty members

questions.solution: Correct answer: Lok Sabha; at least fifty members.

questions.text: Which of the following correctly describes the chairmanship of the Ethics Committee and the Committee on Privileges in the Lok Sabha?

options.label: A
options.text: Both committees are chaired by the Speaker.

options.label: B
options.text: The Ethics Committee is chaired by the Deputy Speaker, while the Privileges Committee elects its own chairperson.

options.label: C
options.text: The Ethics Committee elects its own chairperson, while the Privileges Committee is chaired by the Deputy Speaker by convention.

options.label: D
options.text: The chairpersons of both committees are appointed by the President on the advice of the Prime Minister.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The Ethics Committee elects its own chairperson, while the Privileges Committee is chaired by the Deputy Speaker by convention..

questions.text: What is the primary limitation of the Committee on Government Assurances in ensuring executive accountability?

options.label: A
options.text: It can impose penalties on ministers who fail to fulfil assurances.

options.label: B
options.text: It has the power to initiate judicial proceedings against defaulting ministries.

options.label: C
options.text: It only reports on the implementation of assurances and relies on political pressure for compliance.

options.label: D
options.text: It can amend the Rules of Procedure to make assurances legally binding.

questions.solution: Correct answer: It only reports on the implementation of assurances and relies on political pressure for compliance..

questions.text: Which statement is true regarding the constitutional scope of an ordinance promulgated by the President?

options.label: A
options.text: An ordinance can amend the Constitution if ratified by a simple majority in Parliament.

options.label: B
options.text: An ordinance cannot amend the Constitution; constitutional amendments require the Article 368 procedure.

options.label: C
options.text: An ordinance can override a Supreme Court judgment on a constitutional matter.

options.label: D
options.text: An ordinance remains in force indefinitely unless disapproved by both Houses.

questions.solution: Correct answer: An ordinance cannot amend the Constitution; constitutional amendments require the Article 368 procedure..

questions.text: How does a Calling Attention Motion differ from a Short Duration Discussion in terms of ministerial response?

options.label: A
options.text: Both require a formal motion and a mandatory ministerial reply.

options.label: B
options.text: A Calling Attention Motion mandates a ministerial reply, whereas a Short Duration Discussion involves a ministerial reply but no formal motion.

options.label: C
options.text: A Short Duration Discussion requires a ministerial reply, while a Calling Attention Motion does not.

options.label: D
options.text: Neither device obliges the minister to reply; both are purely deliberative.

questions.solution: Correct answer: A Calling Attention Motion mandates a ministerial reply, whereas a Short Duration Discussion involves a ministerial reply but no formal motion..

questions.text: Which Article of the Constitution provides for free and compulsory education for children aged 6–14 years?

options.label: A
options.text: Article 21

options.label: B
options.text: Article 21A

options.label: C
options.text: Article 45

options.label: D
options.text: Article 46

questions.solution: Correct answer: Article 21A.

questions.text: MGNREGA guarantees how many days of wage employment per rural household per year?

options.label: A
options.text: 50 days

options.label: B
options.text: 75 days

options.label: C
options.text: 100 days

options.label: D
options.text: 150 days

questions.solution: Correct answer: 100 days.

questions.text: Which of the following is a Directive Principle (non-justiciable), not a Fundamental Right?

options.label: A
options.text: Abolition of untouchability

options.label: B
options.text: Right to education (6–14 years)

options.label: C
options.text: Promotion of educational interests of SCs and STs

questions.solution: Correct answer: Promotion of educational interests of SCs and STs.

questions.text: The National Food Security Act, 2013 covers up to what percentage of the rural population under TPDS?
questions.solution: Correct answer: 75%.

questions.text: Which Supreme Court judgement recognised the right of transgender persons to self-identify their gender?

options.label: A
options.text: Navtej Singh Johar v. Union of India (2018)

options.label: B
options.text: NALSA v. Union of India (2014)

options.label: C

options.text: Shayara Bano v. Union of India (2017)

questions.text: Ayushman Bharat PMJAY provides health insurance cover of how much per family per year?

options.text: ₹10 lakh

questions.solution: Correct answer: ₹5 lakh.

questions.text: The 102nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 2018 gave constitutional status to which body?

options.label: A
options.text: National Commission for Scheduled Castes

options.label: B
options.text: National Commission for Scheduled Tribes

options.label: C
options.text: National Commission for Backward Classes

options.label: D

questions.solution: Correct answer: National Commission for Backward Classes.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a component of the National Health Mission (NHM)?

options.label: C
