questions.solution: Correct answer: Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (PMJAY).

questions.text: Under Article 74 of the Constitution, what is the extent of the President's discretion regarding the advice of the Council of Ministers?

options.label: A
options.text: The President may reject the advice outright and act independently.

options.label: B
options.text: The President must act on the advice but may require the Council to reconsider it once.

options.label: C
options.text: The President can act independently in all matters except financial bills.

options.label: D
options.text: The advice of the Council of Ministers is not binding on the President.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The President must act on the advice but may require the Council to reconsider it once..

questions.text: How is the Vice‑President of India elected?

options.label: A
options.text: Directly by the people of India.

options.label: B
options.text: By an electoral college consisting of members of both Houses of Parliament.

options.label: C
options.text: By the President on the advice of the Prime Minister.

options.label: D
options.text: By the elected members of State Legislative Assemblies.

questions.solution: Correct answer: By an electoral college consisting of members of both Houses of Parliament..

questions.text: What change did the 44th Constitutional Amendment (1978) make regarding the President's ordinance‑making power?

options.label: A
options.text: Extended the maximum life of an ordinance to six months.

options.label: B
options.text: Provided that an ordinance cannot be promulgated when both Houses of Parliament are in session.

options.label: C
options.text: Removed the President's power to promulgate ordinances altogether.

options.label: D
options.text: Allowed the President to issue ordinances without the advice of the Council of Ministers.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Provided that an ordinance cannot be promulgated when both Houses of Parliament are in session..

questions.text: The 91st Constitutional Amendment (2003) placed a ceiling on the size of the Union Council of Ministers. What is that ceiling?

options.label: A
options.text: 10 % of the total strength of the Lok Sabha.

options.label: B
options.text: 15 % of the total strength of the Lok Sabha.

options.label: C
options.text: 20 % of the total strength of the Lok Sabha.

options.label: D
options.text: No ceiling; the size is determined by the Prime Minister.

questions.solution: Correct answer: 15 % of the total strength of the Lok Sabha..

questions.text: Which Article of the Constitution provides for the creation of All‑India Services, and which body recruits them?

options.label: A
options.text: Article 309 – Staff Selection Commission.

options.label: B
options.text: Article 312 – Union Public Service Commission.

options.label: C
options.text: Article 315 – State Public Service Commissions.

options.label: D
options.text: Article 320 – Department of Personnel and Training.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Article 312 – Union Public Service Commission..

questions.text: Regarding the ordinance-making power of the President under Article 123, which principle was laid down by the Supreme Court in D.C. Wadhwa v. State of Bihar (1987)?

options.label: A
options.text: The President's satisfaction regarding the necessity of immediate legislation is entirely subjective and non-justiciable.

options.label: B
options.text: An ordinance can be repromulgated indefinitely without legislative approval as long as the President deems it necessary.

options.label: C
options.text: Repeated repromulgation of ordinances without legislative approval constitutes a fraud on the Constitution and an abuse of the ordinance-making power.

options.label: D
options.text: Ordinances lapse automatically after six weeks of Parliament's reassembly only if both Houses pass a resolution disapproving them.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Repeated repromulgation of ordinances without legislative approval constitutes a fraud on the Constitution and an abuse of the ordinance-making power..

questions.text: Which of the following statements about Cabinet Committees in India is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: Cabinet Committees are statutory bodies established under an Act of Parliament.

options.label: B
options.text: The Cabinet Committee on Security (CCS) includes the National Security Adviser (NSA) as a permanent invitee.

options.label: C
options.text: The Cabinet Secretariat has no role in the functioning of Cabinet Committees.

options.label: D
options.text: Ad-hoc Groups of Ministers (GoMs) submit their recommendations directly to the Prime Minister, bypassing standing Cabinet Committees.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The Cabinet Committee on Security (CCS) includes the National Security Adviser (NSA) as a permanent invitee..

questions.text: In T.S.R. Subramanian v. Union of India (2013), the Supreme Court issued directions to insulate civil services from political interference. Which of the following was NOT a direction given by the Court?

options.label: A
options.text: Establishment of a Civil Services Board at the Centre and in each state to recommend transfers, postings, and disciplinary actions.

options.label: B
options.text: Mandating fixed tenures for key posts such as Director General of Police and Chief Secretary.

options.label: C
options.text: Requiring that any premature transfer be recorded with reasons.

options.label: D
options.text: Making the Civil Services Board's recommendations binding on the political executive with no discretion to deviate.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Making the Civil Services Board's recommendations binding on the political executive with no discretion to deviate..

questions.text: Regarding Article 143 of the Constitution, which statement is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: The Supreme Court's advisory opinion is binding on the President and the Council of Ministers.

options.label: B
options.text: The President may refer only questions of fact, not questions of law, to the Supreme Court.

options.label: C
options.text: The advisory opinion is not binding but carries significant persuasive authority.

options.label: D
options.text: The Supreme Court is constitutionally compelled to answer every reference made by the President.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The advisory opinion is not binding but carries significant persuasive authority..

questions.text: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the Prime Minister's Office (PMO) from the Cabinet Secretariat?

options.label: A
options.text: Both are constitutional bodies established under Article 74 of the Constitution.

options.label: B
options.text: The PMO is a constitutional‑administrative body, while the Cabinet Secretariat is a political office.

options.label: C
options.text: The PMO is a political office, whereas the Cabinet Secretariat is a constitutional‑administrative body.

options.label: D
options.text: The two offices are functionally interchangeable and share identical accountability mechanisms.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The PMO is a political office, whereas the Cabinet Secretariat is a constitutional‑administrative body..

questions.text: Under the doctrine of pleasure (Article 310) and the safeguards of Article 311, which statement is accurate?

options.label: A
options.text: Article 311 protections apply to all civil servants from the date of recruitment, including probationers.

options.label: B
options.text: Article 311 protections apply only after a servant has been appointed to a substantive post, not during probation.

options.label: C
options.text: Parliament cannot modify the procedural safeguards of Article 311 through ordinary legislation.

options.label: D
options.text: The protections of Article 311 extend to employees of public sector undertakings and autonomous bodies.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Article 311 protections apply only after a servant has been appointed to a substantive post, not during probation..

questions.text: What change did the Cadre Allocation Policy, 2017 introduce for All India Services officers?

options.label: A
options.text: It abolished the state‑cadre system and created a single national cadre pool.

options.label: B
options.text: It introduced a zone‑based allocation requiring officers to serve in at least one cadre outside their home zone.

options.label: C
options.text: It allowed officers to choose any state cadre solely on the basis of personal preference.

options.label: D
options.text: It removed the mandatory central deputation requirement for all AIS officers.

questions.solution: Correct answer: It introduced a zone‑based allocation requiring officers to serve in at least one cadre outside their home zone..

questions.text: With reference to the imposition of President's Rule under Article 356, which of the following statements is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: The President's satisfaction is absolute and not subject to judicial review.

options.label: B
options.text: The proclamation must be approved by Parliament within one month.

options.label: C
options.text: The Supreme Court in S.R. Bommai mandated a floor test in the State Assembly within a reasonable time, preferably 48 hours, before imposition.

options.label: D
options.text: The dissolution of the State Assembly is a mandatory and routine sequel to the proclamation.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The Supreme Court in S.R. Bommai mandated a floor test in the State Assembly within a reasonable time, preferably 48 hours, before imposition..

questions.text: Consider the following statements regarding the President's pardoning power under Article 72: 1. It is an absolute discretionary power of the President. 2. It is exercised on the aid and advice of the Council of Ministers. 3. It is immune from judicial review. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.label: A
options.text: 1 and 2 only

options.label: B
options.text: 2 only

options.label: C
options.text: 2 and 3 only

options.label: D
options.text: 1, 2 and 3

questions.solution: Correct answer: 2 only.

questions.text: In the context of a minority government or a hung Parliament, which of the following accurately describes the President's discretion regarding the dissolution of the Lok Sabha?

options.label: A
options.text: The President is bound to dissolve the Lok Sabha immediately on the advice of the Prime Minister.

options.label: B
options.text: The President may refuse dissolution if a viable alternative government can be formed.

options.text: The President must refer the matter to the Supreme Court for advisory opinion before dissolving the House.

options.text: The President can dissolve the Lok Sabha only after a confidence motion is defeated on the floor of the House.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about the 360-degree Performance Appraisal Report (PAR) under Mission Karmayogi is correct?

questions.solution: Correct answer: It applies only from the Under Secretary level upward, while lower-level officers continue under the older ACR system..

questions.text: With reference to Financial Emergency under Article 360 of the Constitution, which of the following statements is correct?

options.text: The proclamation must be approved by both Houses of Parliament within one month.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The provision has never been invoked since the commencement of the Constitution..

questions.text: The Targeted Public Distribution System (TPDS) introduced in 1997 classified households into which categories based on a consumption-expenditure survey?

options.text: Universal, Categorical, and Means-Tested categories

options.text: Priority and Non-Priority households under NFSA

questions.solution: Correct answer: Above Poverty Line (APL) and Below Poverty Line (BPL) only.

questions.text: Which of the following correctly describes the three targeting mechanisms discussed in the lesson's design principles section?

questions.text: According to the lesson, what role did the Aadhaar biometric identity system play in the evolution of welfare delivery?

questions.text: What is the correct coverage entitlement under the National Food Security Act (NFSA) as described in the lesson?

questions.text: Which governance reform mechanism is mandated under both MGNREGA and NFSA to empower gram sabhas to scrutinise expenditure and verify beneficiary lists?

questions.text: Which of the following statements correctly reflects the Supreme Court's 2018 ruling in Justice K.S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India regarding Aadhaar and welfare services?

options.text: Aadhaar cannot be made mandatory for services that are not backed by law, and alternative identifiers must be provided.

options.text: Aadhaar authentication is optional only for Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) schemes.

questions.text: Under the Janani Suraksha Yojana (JSY), the cash benefit is conditioned on which specific health‑seeking behaviour?

questions.text: What is the nature of the social audit requirement under the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA) and the National Food Security Act (NFSA)?

options.label: C
options.text: An optional exercise left to the discretion of the Gram Panchayat.

options.text: A central government‑led audit with no role for local institutions.

questions.solution: Correct answer: A mandatory periodic process that must be carried out at regular intervals..

questions.text: For Centrally Sponsored Schemes (CSS), what is the standard Centre‑State funding ratio for general category states?
questions.solution: Correct answer: 60:40.

questions.text: Which provisions were introduced by the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 to govern data use in digital welfare delivery?

options.text: Purpose limitation, data minimisation, and establishment of a Data Protection Board.

questions.text: Which of the following measures was introduced by the Ministry of Women and Child Development in 2022 to rationalise the workload of Anganwadi Workers?

options.text: Capping AWW responsibilities at 30 core activities and removing non‑core duties such as election work.

options.text: Linking frontline workers to a portable pension‑cum‑insurance scheme financed by a 0.5 % cess.

questions.text: In the Union Budget 2023‑24 Gender Budget Statement (Statement 13), how are gender‑neutral schemes treated?

questions.text: When citing evidence from sanitation interventions, why is it important to distinguish between cluster randomised controlled trials (cluster RCTs) and individual‑level randomisation?

options.text: The unit of randomisation determines the appropriate statistical analysis and the risk of contamination across households.

options.text: Individual‑level randomisation is not permitted for public health interventions in India.

options.text: Cluster RCTs are the only design accepted by the Ministry of Statistics for welfare evaluations.

questions.text: What is the role of Community‑Based Enumeration (CBE) in welfare delivery to non‑notified urban settlements according to the lesson?

options.text: CBE is a complementary identification tool that helps include households lacking formal tenure.

options.text: CBE is mandatory for all households to access the 10 % flexi‑fund window under DAY‑NULM.

questions.text: Under the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, which of the following statements about beneficiary consent for welfare schemes is correct?

options.text: Consent fatigue is addressed by allowing ministries to process secondary data without any consent.

questions.text: India’s integration of climate triggers into cash‑transfer architecture was prompted by its exposure to which hydro‑meteorological hazards?

questions.text: Which of the following frameworks is specifically mentioned in the lesson as an alternative to GDP that incorporates environmental sustainability through a standardized statistical framework adopted by the UN Statistical Commission?

questions.text: The Aspirational Districts Programme (ADP), launched in 2018, aims to address development deficits in 112 districts through a specific governance and monitoring mechanism. Which feature of the ADP is highlighted in the lesson as a key innovation?

questions.text: The satellite account for the digital economy adopts a three‑layer structure (core, narrow, broad). Which layer corresponds to ‘digital‑enabling services’ such as e‑commerce and platform intermediation?

questions.text: In a beta convergence regression gᵢ = α + β ln(yᵢ,₀) + εᵢ, a negative and statistically significant β coefficient implies:

questions.text: In the Growth Diagnostics framework by Hausmann, Rodrik and Velasco (2005), if the social return to capital is found to be high, what is the immediate next diagnostic step according to the decision‑tree logic?

questions.text: The NITI Aayog's "State‑Level Growth Diagnostics" (2019) applied the binding‑constraints framework to Indian states. Which of the following pairs correctly matches the binding constraint identified with the region?

questions.text: In estimating India's informal economy, the Central Statistics Office (CSO) uses a "mixed method" combining survey and administrative data. Which of the following describes the correct sequence of this reconciliation process?

questions.text: Under the forthcoming SNA 2025, Research and Development (R&D) expenditure is capitalised as a produced asset if it meets four criteria. Which of the following expenditures is explicitly EXCLUDED from the R&D asset boundary?

questions.text: According to the lesson, which of the following structural shifts has NOT contributed to the decline in India's long-run exchange-rate pass-through (ERPT) coefficient from roughly 0.6 in the early 1990s to below 0.2 after 2016?

options.label: A
options.text: A larger share of imported intermediate goods priced in domestic currency through invoicing practices

options.label: B
options.text: Deeper domestic financial markets allowing firms to hedge currency risk

options.label: C
options.text: Anchoring of inflation expectations by the Monetary Policy Framework Agreement (MPFA) of 2015

options.label: D
options.text: Adoption of a fixed exchange rate regime pegged to the US dollar

questions.solution: Correct answer: Adoption of a fixed exchange rate regime pegged to the US dollar.

questions.text: In the context of current account adjustment, the lesson states that the Marshall-Lerner condition must hold for a real effective exchange rate (REER) depreciation to improve the trade balance. Which of the following best describes the implication of this condition for India's expenditure-switching policy?

options.label: A
options.text: A depreciation will immediately improve the trade balance regardless of import elasticity

options.label: B
options.text: Supply-side constraints and the J-curve effect mean depreciation may worsen the trade balance before improving it, and the sum of export and import demand elasticities must exceed unity

options.label: C
options.text: Expenditure-reducing policies are always superior to expenditure-switching because they avoid valuation effects

options.label: D
options.text: The RBI should maintain an overvalued REER to keep import costs low and permanently fix the current account deficit

questions.solution: Correct answer: Supply-side constraints and the J-curve effect mean depreciation may worsen the trade balance before improving it, and the sum of export and import demand elasticities must exceed unity.

questions.text: Regarding sterilised foreign exchange intervention, the lesson highlights a common misconception. Which statement accurately reflects the lesson's treatment of the fiscal costs associated with sterilised intervention?

options.label: A
options.text: Sterilised intervention has no fiscal cost because the central bank's balance sheet remains unchanged

options.label: B
options.text: The quasi-fiscal loss from interest-rate differentials between sterilisation instruments and reserve assets can be material

options.label: C
options.text: Sterilisation eliminates all monetary policy trade-offs, granting full independence under the impossible trinity

options.label: D
options.text: The RBI uses unsterilised intervention exclusively to avoid any interest-rate differential losses

questions.solution: Correct answer: The quasi-fiscal loss from interest-rate differentials between sterilisation instruments and reserve assets can be material.

questions.text: The lesson discusses rupee-denominated Vostro account settlements as a response to geopolitical sanctions. How does the lesson characterise these arrangements under IMF guidance?

options.label: A
options.text: As a permanent substitute for convertible-currency payments that fully liberalises the capital account

options.label: B
options.text: As temporary capital flow management measures (CFMs) that do not constitute capital-account liberalisation

options.label: C
options.text: As a violation of FEMA that requires immediate regulatory reversal

options.label: D
options.text: As a mechanism that eliminates the need for foreign exchange reserves entirely

questions.solution: Correct answer: As temporary capital flow management measures (CFMs) that do not constitute capital-account liberalisation.

questions.text: According to the RBI's Reserve Management Guidelines (revised 2022) and the diversification strategy since 2018, which of the following statements is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: The guidelines set a maximum single-currency exposure of 80 per cent and a minimum gold share of 3 per cent

options.label: B
options.text: Gold's negative correlation with the dollar (approximately -0.4 over the past decade) improves the risk-adjusted return of the reserve portfolio, especially during dollar strength

options.label: C
options.text: SDRs are a static, non-yielding asset with an interest rate fixed at 0.5 per cent by the IMF Articles of Agreement

options.label: D
options.text: The liquidity-first hierarchy places tactical allocation to high-quality corporate bonds in non-reserve currencies at the top (priority 1) of the reserve structure

questions.solution: Correct answer: Gold's negative correlation with the dollar (approximately -0.4 over the past decade) improves the risk-adjusted return of the reserve portfolio, especially during dollar strength.

questions.text: Which of the following committees is correctly matched with its primary area of recommendation in the context of Indian financial sector reforms?

options.label: A
options.text: Narasimham Committee – Capital market development and securities regulation

options.label: B
options.text: Khan Committee – Banking sector reforms and prudential norms

options.label: C
options.text: Narasimham Committee – Banking sector reforms and prudential norms

options.label: D
options.text: Khan Committee – Insurance sector regulation and pension fund oversight

questions.solution: Correct answer: Narasimham Committee – Banking sector reforms and prudential norms.

questions.text: With reference to the market infrastructure institutions in India, which of the following statements is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: The National Securities Depository Limited (NSDL) and Central Depository Services Limited (CDSL) hold securities in physical certificate form to ensure tangible ownership records.

options.label: B
options.text: The introduction of the T+1 settlement cycle in 2023 increased counterparty risk by extending the settlement period.

options.label: C
options.text: The National Stock Exchange (NSE) and Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) dominate equity trading, while NSDL and CDSL hold securities in dematerialised form.

options.label: D
options.text: Clearing corporations operate independently of stock exchanges and do not participate in the settlement of trades executed on exchanges.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The National Stock Exchange (NSE) and Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) dominate equity trading, while NSDL and CDSL hold securities in dematerialised form..

questions.text: Under the SEBI (Issue and Listing of Non-Convertible Securities) Regulations, 2021, which of the following is a mandatory requirement for public issues of non-convertible debentures?

options.label: A
options.text: A minimum speculative-grade credit rating from a SEBI-registered credit rating agency

options.label: B
options.text: A minimum investment-grade credit rating from a SEBI-registered credit rating agency

options.label: C
options.text: No credit rating requirement if the issue size is below Rs. 100 crore

options.label: D
options.text: Credit rating is optional for public issues but mandatory for private placements

questions.solution: Correct answer: A minimum investment-grade credit rating from a SEBI-registered credit rating agency.

questions.text: Which of the following measures has NOT been introduced to address liquidity constraints in the Indian corporate bond market?

options.label: A
options.text: Corporate bond repo facility

options.label: B
options.text: Trade reporting platform on stock exchanges

options.label: C
options.text: Request for Quote (RFQ) system for anonymous price discovery

options.label: D
options.text: Mandatory market making by all scheduled commercial banks for all corporate bonds

questions.solution: Correct answer: Mandatory market making by all scheduled commercial banks for all corporate bonds.

questions.text: According to the comparison of Government Securities and Corporate Bonds provided in the lesson, which of the following statements is accurate?

options.label: A
options.text: Corporate bonds serve as the risk-free benchmark rate for pricing all financial assets in the economy.

options.label: B
options.text: Government securities have virtually zero credit risk due to sovereign guarantee, while corporate bonds carry varying credit risk rated by credit rating agencies.

options.label: C
options.text: Interest on government securities is fully tax-exempt, while interest on corporate bonds is taxable with special exemptions for infrastructure bonds.

options.label: D
options.text: Corporate bonds generally exhibit higher liquidity than government securities due to active retail participation in secondary markets.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Government securities have virtually zero credit risk due to sovereign guarantee, while corporate bonds carry varying credit risk rated by credit rating agencies..

questions.text: Under the RBI's Scale Based Regulation (SBR) framework for NBFCs introduced in 2019, which of the following statements correctly describes the regulatory treatment of the 'Upper Layer' NBFCs?

options.label: A
options.text: They are subject to the same capital adequacy requirement of 15% Tier-I capital as Base Layer NBFCs but with no leverage limit.

options.label: B
options.text: They face enhanced disclosures, stricter liquidity coverage ratios, and a mandatory requirement to appoint a Chief Risk Officer.

options.label: C
options.text: They are exempt from the Prompt Corrective Action (PCA) matrix applicable to NBFCs breaching capital or asset quality thresholds.

options.label: D
options.text: They are permitted to exceed the single counterparty exposure limit of 20% of Tier-I capital without any additional conditions.

questions.solution: Correct answer: They face enhanced disclosures, stricter liquidity coverage ratios, and a mandatory requirement to appoint a Chief Risk Officer..

questions.text: Which of the following distinctions between the SARFAESI Act, 2002 and the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (IBC), 2016 is accurately stated?

options.label: A
options.text: SARFAESI enables secured creditors to enforce security interest without court intervention, while IBC resolution is court-supervised and time-bound.

options.label: B
options.text: SARFAESI applies only to financial assets secured by movable property, whereas IBC covers both movable and immovable property secured debts.

options.label: C
options.text: Under SARFAESI, the secured creditor must obtain NCLT approval before taking possession of collateral, while IBC allows automatic stay on enforcement.

options.label: D
options.text: SARFAESI provides for a resolution professional to manage the debtor's business, while IBC allows the secured creditor to directly sell the asset.

questions.solution: Correct answer: SARFAESI enables secured creditors to enforce security interest without court intervention, while IBC resolution is court-supervised and time-bound..

questions.text: Regarding the settlement cycle and risk management in Indian financial market infrastructure, which of the following statements is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: The T+1 settlement cycle has been implemented uniformly across all market segments including the trade-for-trade segment.

options.label: B
options.text: Clearing Corporations (CCPs) perform novation, netting, and margin collection, while settlement banks are responsible for funds transfer.

options.label: C
options.text: The Core Settlement Guarantee Fund (CSGF) is funded solely by the Clearing Corporation's own capital without member contributions.

options.label: D
options.text: Initial margin in CCPs is calculated solely based on Extreme Loss Margin (ELM) to cover tail-risk scenarios.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Clearing Corporations (CCPs) perform novation, netting, and margin collection, while settlement banks are responsible for funds transfer..

questions.text: Regarding the RBI's 'Framework for Macro-Stress Testing of NBFCs' (June 2022), which of the following statements is accurate?

options.label: A
options.text: All NBFCs including Base Layer must conduct quarterly stress tests covering credit, market, liquidity, and interest-rate shocks.

options.label: B
options.text: The stress test scenarios are calibrated exclusively to NBFC-specific parameters without reference to the RBI's macro-economic paths used for banks.

options.label: C
options.text: Results must be submitted to the Department of Supervision within 30 days of quarter-end, and material deterioration triggers a supervisory action plan.

options.label: D
options.text: The Countercyclical Capital Buffer (CCyB) for NBFCs is activated when the credit-to-GDP ratio exceeds the RBI's threshold, not the credit-to-GDP gap.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Results must be submitted to the Department of Supervision within 30 days of quarter-end, and material deterioration triggers a supervisory action plan..

questions.text: With reference to India's Sovereign Green Bond framework and the India Green Taxonomy (Draft, July 2023), which statement is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: The Sovereign Green Bond framework aligns with ICMA Green Bond Principles but does not incorporate the EU Taxonomy's 'Do No Significant Harm' criteria.

options.label: B
options.text: Proceeds from sovereign green bonds are tracked through a Green Bond Register maintained by the RBI's Department of Currency Management.

options.label: C
options.text: The India Green Taxonomy classifies economic activities into 'Green', 'Transition', and 'Enabling' categories based on quantitative thresholds.

options.label: D
options.text: Annual allocation and impact reports for sovereign green bonds are audited by the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI).

questions.solution: Correct answer: The India Green Taxonomy classifies economic activities into 'Green', 'Transition', and 'Enabling' categories based on quantitative thresholds..

questions.text: In the resolution regime for Systemically Important Financial Market Infrastructures (FMIs) / Central Counterparties (CCPs), what is the correct hierarchy of loss absorption and the position of government backstop?

options.label: A
options.text: CCP equity → Default Fund contributions of clearing members → Variation margin gains haircutting → Government backstop (first resort).

options.label: B
options.text: Default Fund contributions of clearing members → CCP equity → Assessment powers on surviving members → Government backstop (last resort).

options.label: C
options.text: CCP equity → Default Fund contributions of clearing members → Assessment powers on surviving members → Government backstop (only as last resort).

options.label: D
options.text: Variation margin gains haircutting → CCP equity → Default Fund contributions → Government backstop (only as last resort).

questions.solution: Correct answer: CCP equity → Default Fund contributions of clearing members → Assessment powers on surviving members → Government backstop (only as last resort)..

questions.text: Under the RBI's Digital Lending Guidelines (September 2022), which of the following requirements applies to all Regulated Entities originating, servicing, or facilitating digital loans?

options.label: A
options.text: A mandatory cooling-off period of 7 days during which the borrower can cancel without penalty, applicable only if no e-mandate is signed.

options.label: B
options.text: Loan-to-Value (LTV) caps for unsecured digital loans at 50% of the borrower's assessed income, with a standardized Key Fact Statement (KFS) disclosed after loan sanction.

options.label: C
options.text: A mandatory cooling-off period of 3 days during which the borrower can cancel without penalty, applying even if the borrower signs an e-mandate for auto-debit.

options.label: D
options.text: Prohibition of auto-debit mandates without explicit consent, but consent once given cannot be revoked during the loan tenure.

questions.solution: Correct answer: A mandatory cooling-off period of 3 days during which the borrower can cancel without penalty, applying even if the borrower signs an e-mandate for auto-debit..

questions.text: Under the SEBI (LODR) Regulations, the Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report (BRSR) is mandatory for which category of listed entities from FY 2022‑23?

options.label: A
options.text: All listed companies irrespective of size

options.label: B
options.text: Top 1,000 listed companies by market capitalisation

options.label: C
options.text: Top 500 listed companies by market capitalisation

options.label: D
options.text: Only companies in the financial sector

questions.solution: Correct answer: Top 1,000 listed companies by market capitalisation.

questions.text: Who chairs the Investor Education and Protection Fund (IEPF) Authority as per the Companies Act, 2013?

options.label: A

options.label: B
options.text: Secretary, Ministry of Corporate Affairs

options.label: C
options.text: Governor, Reserve Bank of India

questions.text: Which statement correctly describes the tax treatment difference between REITs and InvITs regarding SPV‑level dividend exemption?

options.label: A

options.label: C
options.text: REIT distributions are tax‑exempt at the SPV level while InvIT distributions are fully taxable

options.label: D
options.text: InvIT distributions are tax‑exempt at the SPV level while REIT distributions are fully taxable

questions.solution: Correct answer: Both are taxed in the hands of unit holders, but the underlying SPV dividend exemption differs under Section 10(23FC).

questions.text: In the tri‑party repo mechanism, what are the prescribed haircuts for AAA‑rated and AA‑rated corporate bonds?

options.label: C
options.text: AAA 10%, AA 5%

questions.solution: Correct answer: AAA 2%, AA 5%.

questions.text: What is the annual aggregate limit for outward remittances under the Liberalised Remittance Scheme (LRS) per PAN across all Authorised Dealer banks?

options.label: A

options.label: B
options.text: USD 250,000 annual aggregate per PAN

options.label: C
options.text: USD 250,000 per transaction

options.label: D
options.text: USD 500,000 annual aggregate per PAN

questions.solution: Correct answer: USD 250,000 annual aggregate per PAN.

questions.text: Under Article 112 of the Constitution, the Annual Financial Statement must distinguish between three specific funds. Which of the following correctly identifies these three funds and the key restriction on the Consolidated Fund?

options.label: A
options.text: Consolidated Fund, Contingency Fund, Public Account; no money can be withdrawn from the Consolidated Fund without parliamentary authorisation

options.label: B
options.text: Consolidated Fund, Emergency Fund, Public Account; withdrawals from the Consolidated Fund require only executive approval

options.label: C
options.text: Revenue Fund, Capital Fund, Contingency Fund; the Consolidated Fund can be accessed through ordinances

options.label: D
options.text: Consolidated Fund, Development Fund, Public Account; parliamentary authorisation is required only for capital expenditure

questions.solution: Correct answer: Consolidated Fund, Contingency Fund, Public Account; no money can be withdrawn from the Consolidated Fund without parliamentary authorisation.

questions.text: The Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act, 2003 originally targeted the elimination of the revenue deficit by 2008-09. What does a persistent revenue deficit indicate about the quality of public finances, according to the lesson?

options.label: A
options.text: It indicates that the government is borrowing to finance consumption, eroding the quality of public finances and limiting space for productive capital outlays

options.label: B
options.text: It indicates that capital expenditure is exceeding revenue receipts, requiring higher market borrowings for asset creation

options.label: C
options.text: It indicates that tax buoyancy has improved but non-tax revenues have declined, creating a temporary mismatch

options.label: D
options.text: It indicates that the primary deficit is being managed effectively while the fiscal deficit remains within FRBM targets

questions.solution: Correct answer: It indicates that the government is borrowing to finance consumption, eroding the quality of public finances and limiting space for productive capital outlays.

questions.text: During the GST compensation shortfall in 2020-21, the Centre borrowed funds and passed them to States as back-to-back loans. What was the primary fiscal rationale for this mechanism?

options.label: A
options.text: To preserve States' fiscal space without violating FRBM borrowing limits, while honouring the compensation guarantee

options.label: B
options.text: To increase the Centre's fiscal deficit temporarily while reducing States' debt-to-GDP ratios permanently

options.label: C
options.text: To shift the compensation burden to the RBI through monetised deficit financing

options.label: D
options.text: To allow States to exceed their FRBM borrowing limits with Centre's guarantee

questions.solution: Correct answer: To preserve States' fiscal space without violating FRBM borrowing limits, while honouring the compensation guarantee.

questions.text: According to the lesson, what is the key condition that allows a higher primary deficit without destabilising the debt-to-GDP ratio?

options.label: A
options.text: A favourable growth-interest differential where nominal GDP growth exceeds the effective interest rate on debt

options.label: B
options.text: A declining revenue deficit coupled with increasing capital expenditure financed by disinvestment proceeds

options.label: C
options.text: A reduction in the share of short-term treasury bills in the total debt portfolio

options.label: D
options.text: An increase in tax buoyancy through base broadening while maintaining subsidy levels

questions.solution: Correct answer: A favourable growth-interest differential where nominal GDP growth exceeds the effective interest rate on debt.

questions.text: The lesson describes the classification of expenditure until 2017-18 and the subsequent change. Which statement accurately reflects this transition?

options.label: A
options.text: Expenditure was classified into plan and non-plan heads until 2017-18, when it was replaced by scheme-based classification

options.label: B
options.text: Expenditure was classified into revenue and capital heads until 2017-18, when plan/non-plan classification was introduced

options.label: C
options.text: Expenditure was classified into scheme-based heads until 2017-18, when it was replaced by plan/non-plan classification

options.label: D
options.text: Expenditure classification has remained unchanged since the FRBM Act, 2003, with only minor modifications in 2017-18

questions.solution: Correct answer: Expenditure was classified into plan and non-plan heads until 2017-18, when it was replaced by scheme-based classification.

questions.text: Which of the following correctly describes the relationship between the Medium‑Term Fiscal Policy Statement (MTFPS) and the Fiscal Strategy Statement (FSS) under the FRBM Act?

options.label: A
options.text: MTFPS sets annual policy actions while FSS provides a rolling three‑year fiscal framework.

options.label: B
options.text: MTFPS is a statutory rolling three‑year target document; FSS translates those targets into concrete annual policy actions such as expenditure prioritisation and borrowing plans.

options.label: C
options.text: Both MTFPS and FSS are identical documents presented together in the Budget.

options.label: D
options.text: FSS is a standalone document not linked to the Union Budget.

questions.solution: Correct answer: MTFPS is a statutory rolling three‑year target document; FSS translates those targets into concrete annual policy actions such as expenditure prioritisation and borrowing plans..

questions.text: According to the lesson, tax buoyancy is defined as the responsiveness of tax revenue to changes in nominal GDP holding tax policy constant. Which formula represents this definition?

options.label: A
options.text: (ΔTax Revenue / Tax Revenue) ÷ (ΔNominal GDP / Nominal GDP)

options.label: B
options.text: (ΔTax Revenue / Tax Revenue) ÷ (ΔReal GDP / Real GDP)

options.label: C
options.text: (ΔTax Revenue / Tax Revenue) ÷ (ΔTax Rate / Tax Rate)

options.label: D
options.text: (ΔTax Revenue / Tax Revenue) ÷ (ΔTax Base / Tax Base)

questions.solution: Correct answer: (ΔTax Revenue / Tax Revenue) ÷ (ΔNominal GDP / Nominal GDP).

questions.text: The 15th Finance Commission recommended a guarantee commission rate of 0.5 % and a guarantee redemption fund for State guarantees. Which statement about the financing of this fund is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: The guarantee redemption fund is financed by the commission, not the other way round.

options.label: B
options.text: The commission rate is 1 % and the fund finances the commission.

options.label: C
options.text: The fund finances the commission, making the commission dependent on the fund corpus.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The guarantee redemption fund is financed by the commission, not the other way round..

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a component of the Treasury Single Account (TSA) as implemented by the Union Government?

options.text: Contingency Fund

options.text: Public Account

options.text: State‑level provident fund accounts

questions.text: Regarding the Expenditure Management Commission (EMC) recommendations, which statement is accurate?

options.label: A
options.text: The EMC mandated universal zero‑based budgeting for all Centrally Sponsored Schemes (CSS).

questions.text: Which of the following operates as an automatic stabiliser in India without requiring fresh legislative action?

options.label: B
options.text: Progressive personal income tax structure

options.label: C
options.text: Additional allocation for capital outlay in the Union Budget

options.label: D
options.text: Changes in the repo rate by the Monetary Policy Committee

questions.solution: Correct answer: Progressive personal income tax structure.

questions.text: With reference to Ways and Means Advances (WMA), which of the following statements is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: WMA is a primary tool for financing the fiscal deficit on a permanent basis

options.label: B
options.text: WMA is a cash-management facility that does not alter the fiscal deficit unless overdrawn

questions.text: In the context of Union Government finance, disinvestment proceeds are classified as:

options.label: A
options.text: Revenue receipts that reduce the revenue deficit

options.label: C

questions.text: Which of the following accurately describes the function of the Public Accounts Committee (PAC) in budgetary oversight?

questions.text: The Taxpayer Charter notified in August 2020 is legally enforceable through which of the following provisions?

options.text: Section 119 of the Income-Tax Act, 1961 and Section 171 of the CGST Act, 2017

questions.text: Regarding cold chain technology options in India, which statement accurately reflects the lesson's description of the evolution and current status?

questions.text: What is the fundamental design principle of the Mega Food Park (MFP) scheme that distinguishes it from traditional food parks?

questions.text: The Essential Commodities (Amendment) Act, 2020 deregulated the stockholding limits for which category of commodities, subject to specific trigger conditions?

questions.text: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the interest subvention limits under the PMFME scheme and the Agriculture Infrastructure Fund (AIF)?

options.text: Reference at least two translations (one Assamese, one English) of the same source text and discuss how each translation's paratext frames the Bodo work for its target audience.

options.label: B
options.text: Provide a back-translation of the Bodo source text into English to demonstrate semantic fidelity before comparing published translations.

options.label: C
options.text: Focus exclusively on lexical deviations in the Assamese translation because it represents the dominant language's appropriation of Bodo literature.

options.label: D
options.text: Prioritise the English translation for analysis since it follows foreignising principles aligned with postcolonial theory preferred in UPSC syllabi.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Reference at least two translations (one Assamese, one English) of the same source text and discuss how each translation's paratext frames the Bodo work for its target audience..

questions.text: Which of the following best describes the theoretical shift in Bodo literary criticism that examiners expect candidates to demonstrate chronological awareness of, according to the lesson?

questions.text: In the critical editions of Bodo poetry, what specific orthographic problem arises from the representation of the high central vowel /ɨ/ during the script transition from Roman to Devanagari?

options.label: A
options.text: The vowel was represented as 'y' in Roman script but early Devanagari primers omitted the nukta diacritic on 'इ', producing a systematic orthographic ambiguity

options.label: B
options.text: The vowel was represented as 'ü' in Roman script but Devanagari used 'उ' without any diacritic distinction

options.label: C
options.text: The vowel had no representation in Roman script but was assigned a new Devanagari character created specifically for Bodo

options.label: D
options.text: The vowel was written as 'i' in both scripts but with different phonological values in Western versus Eastern dialects

questions.solution: Correct answer: The vowel was represented as 'y' in Roman script but early Devanagari primers omitted the nukta diacritic on 'इ', producing a systematic orthographic ambiguity.

questions.text: A key distinction between Half-Bridge Submodules (HBSM) and Full-Bridge Submodules (FBSM) in Modular Multilevel Converters (MMC) is the number of voltage levels generated and the resulting DC fault capability. Which statement correctly describes this distinction?

questions.text: For a 200 km transmission line with impedance Z_L = 0.05 + j0.4 Ω/km, protected by a distance relay, and an adjacent line of 150 km, what is the correct basis for setting the Zone-2 reach impedance (Z_2) to ensure coordination, avoiding the common error mentioned in the lesson?

questions.text: The lesson cites the difference between Q1 Hamlet ("Enter Hamlet reading on a book") and F1 (which omits the prop) to illustrate which principle of dramatic textual analysis?

questions.text: In the context of feminist recovery strategies and canon formation, the lesson identifies which practice as a critical pitfall to avoid in examination answers?

questions.text: The lesson prescribes a "three-layer method" for ecocritical examination answers. Which of the following correctly sequences these three required layers?

questions.text: According to the lesson, T.S. Eliot's 1921 essay 'The Metaphysical Poets' praised the 'unification of sensibility' in Donne and his contemporaries. What strategic critical purpose did this rehabilitation serve for Eliot's own poetic practice?

questions.solution: Correct answer: It legitimized Eliot's own fragmented, allusive, and intellectually dense method by claiming the Metaphysicals as ancestors..

questions.text: The lesson identifies a 'Single-Technique Trap' in analyzing the novel's formal evolution. Which of the following best exemplifies this trap when discussing stream of consciousness?

questions.text: In the section on 'Drama's Structural Shifts,' the 'well-made play' (pièce bien faite) is characterized by a specific mechanical structure. Which of the following is identified in the lesson as a core component of that structure?

options.label: D

questions.solution: Correct answer: The use of a 'secret' known to the audience but withheld from the protagonist, driving the action toward an 'obligatory scene'..

questions.text: The lesson outlines a trajectory of criticism from Johnson to Leavis to Post-Structuralism. Which statement accurately reflects F.R. Leavis's 'Great Tradition' project as described in the text?

questions.text: The concept of 'writing back' (Ashcroft, Griffiths, Tiffin) is central to the lesson's section on the colonial encounter. Which of the following accurately describes Jean Rhys's Wide Sargasso Sea (1966) as a 'writing back' to Charlotte Brontë's Jane Eyre (1847)?

questions.text: According to the lesson, what is the examiner's primary test regarding the sonnet sequence's dual nature?

questions.text: Which statement accurately reflects the lesson's warning against the 'Thematic Reduction Trap' in studying the mock-epic?

questions.text: How does the lesson characterize the relationship between the Victorian and Modernist dramatic monologue?

options.text: The form exhibits continuity in irony, rhetorical performance, and the silent listener, but ruptures in the shift from a stable to a fragmented subject.

options.text: Victorian dramatic monologues rely on fragmented syntax, while modernist monologues restore coherent psychological unity.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The form exhibits continuity in irony, rhetorical performance, and the silent listener, but ruptures in the shift from a stable to a fragmented subject..

questions.text: What does the lesson identify as the 'Gothic-as-Horror Trap' and its correction?

questions.text: Which description aligns with the lesson's analysis of the pastoral and anti-pastoral tradition?

questions.text: According to the lesson, which statement best characterizes the trajectory of the English essay from Bacon to Woolf?

questions.text: The lesson identifies the 'periodic sentence' as a hallmark of English prose shaped by classical rhetoric. Which of the following accurately describes its structural principle as presented in the text?

questions.text: In the context of climate sensitivity metrics, why is the Transient Climate Response (TCR) lower than the Equilibrium Climate Sensitivity (ECS) for a doubling of CO₂?

questions.text: Which of the following best explains the structural tension between Umashankar Joshi's Nishkant and Pannalal Patel's Manvi ni Bhavai regarding their treatment of time?

questions.text: In a comparative synthesis question asking about the treatment of 'womanhood' in Saraswatichandra versus Manvi ni Bhavai, which structural role difference is highlighted?

questions.text: Regarding the evolution of Gujarati literature from the Navyug movement to modernism, which statement correctly grounds the argument in historical context without over-generalizing?

questions.text: Which of the following accurately describes Narmadashankar Dave's (Narmad) specific contribution to the standardisation of Gujarati prose in the 19th century?

questions.text: In the context of the Chhayavad movement, poets consciously avoided the heavy Sanskritization found in earlier court poetry to express modern existential angst. Which dialect did they adopt as a standard literary language to unify diverse influences?

options.label: B
options.text: Khadi Boli

options.label: C
options.text: Uttarakhandi

options.label: D
options.text: Rajasthani

questions.solution: Correct answer: Khadi Boli.

questions.text: Identify the exception regarding language usage and stylistic approach in the Chhayavad movement compared to the preceding Ritikal period.

options.label: A
options.text: Chhayavad poets used ornate metaphors for courtly love similar to Ritikal poets.

options.label: B
options.text: Chhayavad poetry utilized a raw, unpolished language rejecting Vakrokti (twisted speech) and Alamkara (ornamentation) to depict suffering.

options.label: C
options.text: Chhayavad poets reverted to Sanskritized Hindi to mimic Persian aesthetics like Keshavdas did in Ritikal.

options.label: D
options.text: Chhayavad literature focused solely on religious devotion rather than social reform or industrialization.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Chhayavad poetry utilized a raw, unpolished language rejecting Vakrokti (twisted speech) and Alamkara (ornamentation) to depict suffering..

questions.text: Analyze the socio-political context linking the rise of the Navya movement in the 1940s-50s to a major historical event.

options.label: A
options.text: The Partition of India and the Nehruvian vision of socialism, characterized by themes of Vigyan (science) and Sarva-dharma-samabhav (religious equality).

options.label: B
options.text: The colonial economic structure leading to a focus on landlordism critique similar to Premchand's early works.

options.label: C
options.text: The 1857 uprising which primarily influenced the shift from Sanskritized Apabhramsha to vernacular dialects.

options.label: D
options.text: The decline of the Mughal empire which led to the rise of courtly poets like Keshavdas.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The Partition of India and the Nehruvian vision of socialism, characterized by themes of Vigyan (science) and Sarva-dharma-samabhav (religious equality)..

questions.text: Which of the following statements accurately distinguishes between Premchand's literary contribution and the stylistic evolution of the Navya movement?

options.label: A
options.text: Premchand belongs to the Progressive Writers' Movement and used literature for social reform, whereas Navya is a later stylistic evolution in poetry and fiction.

options.label: B
options.text: Premchand wrote Kamayani, which exemplifies the raw language of the Navya movement.

options.label: C
options.text: Premchand's early works already displayed the full characteristics of the Navya movement including themes of displacement and refugee crises.

options.label: D
options.text: Premchand was a courtly poet who intentionally reverted to ornate Hindi to mimic Persian aesthetics.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Premchand belongs to the Progressive Writers' Movement and used literature for social reform, whereas Navya is a later stylistic evolution in poetry and fiction..

questions.text: Which of the following statements accurately describes the role of the Nagari Pracharini Sabha in the standardisation of Hindi orthography?

options.label: A
options.text: It was established in 1881 and introduced the nuqta for Perso-Arabic phonemes, later jointly publishing the Hindi Shabd Sangrah with the Hindi Sahitya Sammelan in the 1920s.

options.label: B
options.text: It was founded at Fort William College in 1805 to oversee the publication of Prem Sagar and Rani Ketaki Ki Kahani in Devanagari script.

options.label: C
options.text: It successfully eliminated the Kaithi and Mahajani scripts from commercial use by the 1880s through colonial administrative orders.

options.label: D
options.text: Its 1900 spelling conventions were immediately adopted as the official script of the Union under Article 343 of the Constitution.

questions.solution: Correct answer: It was established in 1881 and introduced the nuqta for Perso-Arabic phonemes, later jointly publishing the Hindi Shabd Sangrah with the Hindi Sahitya Sammelan in the 1920s..

questions.text: Which of the following assertions about the interplay of folk traditions and classical poetics in Bhakti and Ritikal is supported by the lesson?

options.label: B
options.text: Hazari Prasad Dwivedi highlighted the continuity of folk metres from Apabhramsha into early Khari Boli.

options.label: C
options.text: Ramchandra Shukla viewed Ritikal as a period where folk traditions were organically integrated into courtly poetics.

options.label: D
options.text: The commercial press fossilised oral folk forms without any influence from classical Sanskrit metrics.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Hazari Prasad Dwivedi highlighted the continuity of folk metres from Apabhramsha into early Khari Boli..

questions.text: What specific role did the Sahitya Akademi's translation programme play in post-independence canon formation, according to the lesson?

options.label: A

options.text: Its translation programme is explicitly cited as a factor in canon formation that examinees should not overlook.

options.text: It standardised the spelling of Tatsama words through the Hindi Shabd Sangrah in the 1920s.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Its translation programme is explicitly cited as a factor in canon formation that examinees should not overlook..

questions.text: Which of the following correctly characterises the methodological shift in contemporary Hindi literary scholarship (post-2000) as described in the lesson?

options.label: A

options.text: Interdisciplinary methods including digital humanities, corpus linguistics, and book-history approaches.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Interdisciplinary methods including digital humanities, corpus linguistics, and book-history approaches..

questions.text: In the colonial period, the Fort William College project (1800–1830) produced Hindi prose translations of Sanskrit epics using munshis such as Lallu Lal and Sadal Misra. What was the primary linguistic consequence of these translations for modern Hindi?

questions.solution: Correct answer: They standardised a Sanskritised Khari Boli that became the literary norm..

questions.text: The lesson warns against treating Mahadevi Varma’s feminism as a monolithic category. Which distinction is essential for a high-scoring analysis of her contribution?

questions.text: Which combination of laws and novels must be cited to adequately answer a question on how state patronage and censorship shaped Hindi novels between 1930 and 1980?

questions.text: Computational analysis of the Hindi Corpus at JNU (2004/2012) revealed a steady increase in Tatsama vocabulary in prose from 12% (1900) to 28% (1970). What does the lesson identify as the correlate of this trend, and what is a major methodological limitation of the corpus?

questions.solution: Correct answer: Correlate: Akademi’s language-planning policies; Limitation: OCR error rates for Devanagari above 8%.

questions.text: Which editorial policy did Mahavir Prasad Dwivedi enforce at Saraswati that shaped the emerging Khari Boli literary register?

questions.text: What is the dual function of temporal displacement in Bhisham Sahni’s “Do Aakhri Din” according to the lesson?

questions.text: According to the lesson, what is the significance of Khari Boli standardisation in Hindi literary criticism?

questions.text: Computational stylometry applied to the Hindi Sahitya Digital Archive (HSDA) corpus revealed a measurable shift in Premchand's Godaan across its 1936, 1942, and 1955 editions, specifically:
