questions.text: In the context of the 'Modernist Shift' post-1930s, how does the lesson distinguish the source of authority for the Vachana movement compared to the Navodaya movement?

options.label: A
options.text: Vachanas drew from rationalist humanism while Navodaya relied on divine intuition found in Shiva's teachings.

options.label: B
options.text: Both movements derived their authority primarily from the patronage of the Hoysala court and feudal structures.

options.label: C
options.text: Vachanas drew from divine intuition (Shiva) whereas Navodaya drew from rationalist humanism and social reform.

options.label: D
options.text: The Vachana movement focused on epic grandeur while Navodaya focused on strict adherence to classical Sanskrit metrics.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Vachanas drew from divine intuition (Shiva) whereas Navodaya drew from rationalist humanism and social reform..

questions.text: When analyzing Kuvempu's stylistic evolution as a landmark case study, what specific hybridity does the examiner look for in an advanced analysis?

options.label: A
options.text: The complete abandonment of Sanskrit metrics to adopt purely English literary syntax.

options.label: B
options.text: The blending of classical Sanskrit metrics with modern Kannada vernacular syntax to create epic grandeur.

options.label: C
options.text: The use of archaic courtly language exclusively to reject contemporary dialogue and modern themes.

options.label: D
options.text: A focus solely on the author's biography rather than the stylistic evolution from romantic poetry to epic.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The blending of classical Sanskrit metrics with modern Kannada vernacular syntax to create epic grandeur..

questions.text: In a comparative period analysis of linguistic texture, how did the 'Sanskritization' trend evolve differently between the Old Kannada period (Kavirajamarga era) and the Modernist period?

options.label: A
options.text: In the Old period, Sanskritization was prescriptive for purity; in the Modernist period, it shifted to aesthetic enrichment.

options.label: B
options.text: In both periods, the core syntax leaned heavily towards the spoken vernacular while ignoring Sanskrit vocabulary entirely.

options.label: C
options.text: The Old period favored pure Prakrit while the Modernist period strictly regulated language against any foreign influence.

options.label: D
options.text: Sanskritization was absent in the Modernist period, replaced entirely by the use of only colloquial Odia idioms.

questions.solution: Correct answer: In the Old period, Sanskritization was prescriptive for purity; in the Modernist period, it shifted to aesthetic enrichment..

questions.text: Regarding the publication of Kannada Prabha in 1908, what critical shift in literary transmission does this data point signify according to the lesson?

options.label: A
options.text: It marked the beginning of oral/monastic transmission replacing print culture for social reform ideas.

options.label: B
options.text: It signifies the transition from oral/monastic transmission to print culture, accelerating the spread of social reform ideas.

options.label: C
options.text: It indicates that women writers like Akka Mahadevi began utilizing print media immediately after its publication.

options.label: D
options.text: It represents a decline in the use of Sanskrit vocabulary in favor of purely English literary structures.

questions.solution: Correct answer: It signifies the transition from oral/monastic transmission to print culture, accelerating the spread of social reform ideas..

questions.text: Which of the following statements accurately describes the chronological sequence and impact of printing presses on Kannada orthographic standardization?

options.label: A
options.text: The Basel Mission Press (1840) preceded the Serampore Mission Press (1817) and introduced the first standardized glyph set for Kannada.

options.label: B
options.text: The Serampore Mission Press (1817) preceded the Basel Mission Press (1840), and print technology forced adoption of a single glyph per phoneme and removal of regional variant forms.

options.label: C
options.text: Ferdinand Kittel's 1881 grammar was published by the Basel Mission Press and introduced the 'zero-width joiner' for digital conjunct rendering.

options.label: D
options.text: The Karnataka Sahitya Parishat (1915) established the first printing press in Kannada, leading to the 1970 'Kannada Lipi Nirdeshana' for Unicode compliance.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The Serampore Mission Press (1817) preceded the Basel Mission Press (1840), and print technology forced adoption of a single glyph per phoneme and removal of regional variant forms..

questions.text: A candidate claims that the vachana form of the 12th-century Veerashaiva movement is essentially identical to the 'free verse' (muktakavita) adopted by Navya modernist poets in the 1960s. Which distinction from the lesson refutes this claim most precisely?

options.label: A
options.text: The vachana used a conversational register and paradoxical koan-like statements, whereas Navya free verse employed strict shatpadi metre for confessional poetry.

options.label: B
options.text: The vachana was a doctrinal form tied to Lingayat theology and social reform, while the 1960s free verse was an aesthetic experiment detached from religious doctrine.

options.label: C
options.text: The vachana was authored exclusively by upper-caste men, while Navya free verse democratized authorship to include women and Dalits.

options.label: D
options.text: The vachana rejected all Sanskrit metres, whereas Navya poets revived the ragale metre for lyrical intensity in their free verse.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The vachana was a doctrinal form tied to Lingayat theology and social reform, while the 1960s free verse was an aesthetic experiment detached from religious doctrine..

questions.text: Regarding the Navodaya movement, which of the following statements aligns with the lesson's characterization of its internal complexity and institutionalization?

options.label: A
options.text: The Navodaya movement was a monolithic bloc unified around B. M. Srikantaiah's 'English Geethegalu' and the Mysore University Kannada department.

options.label: B
options.text: The movement contained competing modernist and nationalist factions, and its institutionalization involved the Karnataka Sahitya Parishat (1915) and the University Kannada department.

options.label: C
options.text: Navodaya poets exclusively used the ragale metre for lyrical poetry, rejecting the shatpadi as a Jain relic unsuited to modern humanism.

options.label: D
options.text: The movement's print culture was solely driven by the Basel Mission Press, which published the journal 'Prabuddha Karnataka' from 1920.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The movement contained competing modernist and nationalist factions, and its institutionalization involved the Karnataka Sahitya Parishat (1915) and the University Kannada department..

questions.text: Which of the following correctly identifies the metrical structure of the tripadi and its modern adaptation in Bandaya poetry?

options.label: A
options.text: Tripadi is a four-line stanza with an 8-8-8-8 syllabic pattern, used by Siddalingaiah for extended narrative protest poems.

options.label: B
options.text: Tripadi is a three-line stanza with a 6-8-6 syllable pattern, exploited by Siddalingaiah for its brevity to compress protest slogans with pamphleteering effect.

options.label: C
options.text: Tripadi is a six-line stanza with 11 syllables per line and a caesura after the 5th syllable, adapted by Bandaya poets for epic-scale Dalit narratives.

options.label: D
options.text: Tripadi is a four-line stanza with a refrain, originating in Haridasa suladi, which feminist poets like Vaidehi use to echo cyclical domestic labour.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Tripadi is a three-line stanza with a 6-8-6 syllable pattern, exploited by Siddalingaiah for its brevity to compress protest slogans with pamphleteering effect..

questions.text: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the musical structure of the Haridasa suladi from the formal characteristics of Navya poetry?

options.label: A
options.text: The suladi employs a fixed tala cycle across sections while Navya poetry uses variable line lengths and enjambment.

options.label: B
options.text: The suladi is a free-form piece without fixed tala while Navya poetry adheres to traditional shatpadi metre.

options.label: C
options.text: Both the suladi and Navya poetry discard fixed metres in favour of psychological discontinuity.

options.label: D
options.text: The suladi uses a single raga throughout while Navya poetry employs changing talas across stanzas.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The suladi employs a fixed tala cycle across sections while Navya poetry uses variable line lengths and enjambment..

questions.text: Regarding the inception of the Navya movement, which statement accurately reflects the lesson's emphasis on institutional factors beyond a single editor?

options.label: A
options.text: The movement was launched solely through Gopalakrishna Adiga's 1965 anthology Navya.

options.label: B
options.text: The editorial role of Kavya magazine in shaping the Navya manifesto was as crucial as Adiga's anthology.

options.label: C
options.text: Navya emerged from the pages of Prabuddha Karnataka, which published the first Navya poems.

options.label: D
options.text: The movement's manifesto was first articulated in Sankramana, a Marxist‑Ambedkarite little magazine.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The editorial role of Kavya magazine in shaping the Navya manifesto was as crucial as Adiga's anthology..

questions.text: The lesson identifies a common examination error concerning the metre of Yakshagana's prasanga verses. What is the correct metrical description?

options.label: A
options.text: Prasanga verses are composed in the six‑line shatpadi metre.

options.label: B
options.text: Prasanga verses predominantly use a four‑line ragale‑type metre with a refrain.

options.label: C
options.text: Prasanga verses follow the tripadi three‑line structure common in Janapada songs.

options.label: D
options.text: Prasanga verses are written in free verse without any fixed metrical pattern.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Prasanga verses predominantly use a four‑line ragale‑type metre with a refrain..

questions.text: How does the lesson characterize the ideological diversity among Kannada little magazines?

options.label: A
options.text: All little magazines shared a nationalist ideology, differing only in literary taste.

options.label: B
options.text: Little magazines were ideologically homogeneous, uniformly promoting Marxist‑Ambedkarite thought.

options.label: C
options.text: Prabuddha Karnataka was nationalist, Sankramana Marxist‑Ambedkarite, and Samvada feminist‑Dalit, showing clear ideological differentiation.

options.label: D
options.text: The magazines avoided explicit ideology, focusing solely on formal experimentation in poetry.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Prabuddha Karnataka was nationalist, Sankramana Marxist‑Ambedkarite, and Samvada feminist‑Dalit, showing clear ideological differentiation..

questions.text: The lesson identifies a specific error regarding the Kavirajamarga's relationship to Sanskrit poetics. Which of the following statements accurately reflects the lesson's correction of this error?

options.label: A
options.text: The Kavirajamarga should not be treated as a pure Sanskrit-derived treatise because it contains an explicit formulation of a Kannada-specific rasa taxonomy.

options.label: B
options.text: The Kavirajamarga is a direct translation of Bharata's Natyashastra with no indigenous modifications.

options.label: C
options.text: The Kavirajamarga ignores Sanskrit alankara shastra entirely and creates a completely independent aesthetic system.

options.label: D
options.text: The Kavirajamarga's only contribution is the adoption of Sanskrit metres (vrttas) for Kannada poetry.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The Kavirajamarga should not be treated as a pure Sanskrit-derived treatise because it contains an explicit formulation of a Kannada-specific rasa taxonomy..

questions.text: Which of the following best describes the core theoretical disagreement within the Pragatishila movement regarding literary form in the 1940s–1950s?

options.label: A
options.text: Whether to adopt Sanskritised vocabulary or colloquial Kannada for mass communication.

options.label: B
options.text: Whether social commitment required accessible realist prose-poetry (gadyakavya) or permitted formal innovation like free verse to address modern alienation.

options.label: C
options.text: Whether to align with the Communist Party of India's cultural directives or maintain artistic autonomy from political parties.

options.label: D
options.text: Whether to focus on feudal exploitation in rural settings or industrial labour in urban centres as the primary subject matter.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Whether social commitment required accessible realist prose-poetry (gadyakavya) or permitted formal innovation like free verse to address modern alienation..

questions.text: According to the lesson, how should Akkamahadevi's rejection of conventional marriage be interpreted within the context of 12th-century Virashaiva theology?

options.label: A
options.text: As a proto-feminist assertion of individual autonomy against patriarchal structures, anticipating modern gender politics.

options.label: B
options.text: As a theological assertion of sharanatva (surrender to Shiva) within the specific doctrinal debates of the Virashaiva movement.

options.label: C
options.text: As a strategic negotiation to gain entry into the male-dominated Anubhava Mantapa assembly of Sharanas.

options.label: D
options.text: As a reflection of the broader Bhakti movement's emphasis on emotional devotion over ritual orthodoxy.

questions.solution: Correct answer: As a theological assertion of sharanatva (surrender to Shiva) within the specific doctrinal debates of the Virashaiva movement..

questions.text: What does the lesson identify as the key distinction between the narrative strategies of Masti Venkatesha Iyengar and Gorur Ramaswamy Iyengar in the early modern Kannada short story?

options.label: A
options.text: Masti wrote primarily about urban middle-class life, while Gorur focused on rural folk narratives.

options.label: B
options.text: Masti employed an ironic omniscient narrator, whereas Gorur adopted the persona of a folk raconteur.

options.label: C
options.text: Masti was influenced by English modernism, while Gorur drew exclusively from the Harikatha tradition.

options.label: D
options.text: Masti's stories were published in mainstream journals, while Gorur's appeared only in little magazines.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Masti employed an ironic omniscient narrator, whereas Gorur adopted the persona of a folk raconteur..

questions.text: What is the central argument of D.R. Nagaraj's critique of the Rice-Narasimhachar periodisation framework in Kannada literary historiography?

options.label: A
options.text: The framework relies excessively on dynastic chronology and should be replaced by a purely genre-based periodisation.

options.label: B
options.text: The framework is a Brahminical-colonial co-production that constructed a 'high culture' canon legitimising Wodeyar rule while marginalising traditions like the vachanas as 'sectarian'.

options.label: C
options.text: The framework incorrectly dates the Kavirajamarga and fails to account for the oral literature of Dalit and pastoral communities.

options.label: D
options.text: The framework was imposed by the University of Mysore's Kannada department to control textbook selection and academic appointments.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The framework is a Brahminical-colonial co-production that constructed a 'high culture' canon legitimising Wodeyar rule while marginalising traditions like the vachanas as 'sectarian'..

questions.text: In a Paper II explanation question on Kannada, the first step is to:

options.label: A
options.text: identify the text, author and context

options.label: B
options.text: summarise the plot

options.label: C
options.text: list all characters

options.label: D
options.text: give a personal opinion

questions.solution: Correct answer: identify the text, author and context.

questions.text: Which approach is best for a Kannada literary essay?

options.label: A
options.text: thesis, textual evidence, counter-argument, conclusion

options.label: B
options.text: plot summary only

options.label: C
options.text: biography of the author only

options.label: D
options.text: quotation collection without argument

questions.solution: Correct answer: thesis, textual evidence, counter-argument, conclusion.

questions.text: When quoting a Kannada text in an English answer, you should:

options.label: A
options.text: quote a translation without credit

options.label: B
options.text: give the original term with a translation and translator

options.label: C
options.text: invent a quotation

options.label: D
options.text: avoid all quotations

questions.solution: Correct answer: give the original term with a translation and translator.

questions.text: Literary criticism of Kannada should focus on:

options.label: A
options.text: only the author’s life

options.label: B
options.text: only the price of the book

options.label: C
options.text: traditional alamkara criticism, Navodaya humanism, modernist and postcolonial criticism, Dalit and Bandaya critique

options.label: D
options.text: only the number of pages

questions.solution: Correct answer: traditional alamkara criticism, Navodaya humanism, modernist and postcolonial criticism, Dalit and Bandaya critique.

questions.text: The safest way to handle uncertain dates in Kannada literary history is to:

options.label: A
options.text: invent exact years

options.label: B
options.text: skip all chronology

options.label: C
options.text: use only foreign dates

options.label: D
options.text: use approximate centuries and avoid precise unverified years

questions.solution: Correct answer: use approximate centuries and avoid precise unverified years.

questions.text: According to the lesson's analysis of Pampa's Vikramarjuna Vijaya, what is the primary critical function of the 'upama' (simile) beyond mere decoration?

options.label: A
options.text: To strictly adhere to Bharata Muni's rules on ornamentation in Sanskrit drama.

options.label: B
options.text: To elevate Arjuna from a mortal king to a divine avatar, reinforcing the text's theological agenda.

options.label: C
options.text: To introduce psychological realism and collapse the distance between reader and character.

options.label: D
options.text: To serve as a static device that prevents the narrative voice from becoming introspective.

questions.solution: Correct answer: To elevate Arjuna from a mortal king to a divine avatar, reinforcing the text's theological agenda..

questions.text: In the context of the 'Mechanism of Shift' described by critics like K.S. Narasimhaswamy, how does the critical approach change when moving from classical texts to modernist works like U.R. Ananthamurthy's Samskara?

options.label: A
options.text: The critic must shift from analyzing theological consistency and gunas to examining psychological contradictions and existentialism.

options.label: B
options.text: The critic must abandon the study of alamkara entirely in favor of only structuralist analysis.

options.label: C
options.text: The critic should focus solely on the fourth wall breaking techniques found in Girish Karnad's plays.

options.label: D
options.text: The critic must prioritize the use of Sanskrit metres over vernacular dialects to maintain traditional purity.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The critic must shift from analyzing theological consistency and gunas to examining psychological contradictions and existentialism..

questions.text: When addressing an essay question on the relevance of Samskara today, what is the 'Mechanism of Synthesis' strategy recommended by the lesson?

options.label: A
options.text: Argue that modernism severed the link with tradition and should be rejected in favor of classical purity.

options.label: B
options.text: Praise Ananthamurthy exclusively without acknowledging any potential criticisms of his work's social context.

options.label: C
options.text: Deconstruct false binaries by arguing that modernism is a dialogue with the past, redefining roots through self-reflection and critique.

options.label: D
options.text: Focus only on the caste system as depicted in the novel while ignoring its philosophical or psychological dimensions.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Deconstruct false binaries by arguing that modernism is a dialogue with the past, redefining roots through self-reflection and critique..

questions.text: Identify the specific exception to the rule that 'classical Kannada texts follow strict Sanskrit metres' as highlighted in the lesson's section on anomalies.

options.label: A
options.text: All classical poets strictly followed shloka and tripadi without any deviation or mixed metres.

options.label: B
options.text: Some verses in Vikramarjuna Vijaya use mixed metres to indicate a shift in tone, marking an early 'Navodaya' sensibility.

options.label: C
options.text: The introduction of vernacular dialects only occurred after the 20th century Navodaya movement was formally coined.

options.label: D
options.text: Pampa and Ranna are cited as examples who broke strict metrical rules to prioritize natural speech flow.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Some verses in Vikramarjuna Vijaya use mixed metres to indicate a shift in tone, marking an early 'Navodaya' sensibility..

questions.text: According to the lesson's 'Exception Detector' technique regarding Dalit literature, what is a key stylistic contradiction an advanced student should recognize?

options.label: A
options.text: Dalit authors exclusively write in vernacular dialects and never use ornamental styles.

options.label: B
options.text: A Dalit author might write in a highly ornamental style to reclaim the 'high' language for their own voice, contradicting the expectation of only simple protest literature.

options.label: C
options.text: The standard text on Dalit literature focuses solely on oppression without any mention of stylistic choices or language reclamation.

options.label: D
options.text: Dalit authors reject the influence of English literature and Freudian psychology entirely in favor of pure indigenous traditions.

questions.solution: Correct answer: A Dalit author might write in a highly ornamental style to reclaim the 'high' language for their own voice, contradicting the expectation of only simple protest literature..

questions.text: According to the lesson, what is the primary structural feature of the Vachana that forces the reader to confront the semantic weight of each word without decorative mediation?

options.label: A
options.text: Its strict adherence to the Sanskritised Champu metre

options.label: B
options.text: Its composition as a single declarative sentence broken into three lines (tripadi)

options.label: C
options.text: Its extensive use of Alamkara (ornamentation) derived from classical poetics

options.label: D
options.text: Its reliance on the Dwipada (two-line) metre for philosophical discourse

questions.solution: Correct answer: Its composition as a single declarative sentence broken into three lines (tripadi).

questions.text: In the intertextual dialogue between classical epics and Navodaya novels, which of the following is NOT identified as one of the three operating mechanisms?

options.label: A
options.text: Structural borrowing where the novel's chapter division mirrors the epic's Parva

options.label: B
options.text: Thematic inversion where the epic's dharma becomes a site of critique

options.label: C
options.text: Linguistic hybridity where Sanskritised diction coexists with colloquial Kannada

options.label: D
options.text: Complete rejection of epic characters in favour of entirely new fictional protagonists

questions.solution: Correct answer: Complete rejection of epic characters in favour of entirely new fictional protagonists.

questions.text: Regarding the Navya movement's critical reception, the lesson warns against which common analytical error?

options.label: A
options.text: Treating the Navya movement as a monolithic formalist project and ignoring its internal caste-gender critiques

options.label: B
options.text: Overemphasizing the influence of Western modernism on Navya poets like Gopalakrishna Adiga

options.label: C
options.text: Confusing the Navya movement with the earlier Navodaya renaissance period

options.label: D
options.text: Attributing the 'speech-act' quality of Vachanas solely to Navya innovations

questions.solution: Correct answer: Treating the Navya movement as a monolithic formalist project and ignoring its internal caste-gender critiques.

questions.text: What philological distinction does the lesson emphasize regarding the Halmidi inscription's language?

options.label: A
options.text: It is written in Old Kannada, identical to the language of early Vachanas

options.label: B
options.text: It is pre-Old Kannada and requires separate philological handling from Old Kannada

options.label: C
options.text: It represents the earliest form of Middle Kannada, bridging Old and Modern periods

options.label: D
options.text: It uses a Sanskritised register that reflects courtly patronage unlike later inscriptions

questions.solution: Correct answer: It is pre-Old Kannada and requires separate philological handling from Old Kannada.

questions.text: When discussing caste representation in Kannada Bhakti literature, the lesson instructs that a candidate must avoid a monolithic statement and instead illustrate differences across traditions. Which of the following correctly maps the three traditions to their specific caste negotiations as described?

options.label: A
options.text: Vachanas: dismantle varna hierarchy; Haridasa: devotee transcends birth; Dasa: Kanaka Dasa uses tradition's language to claim spiritual authority

options.label: B
options.text: Vachanas: devotee transcends birth; Haridasa: dismantle varna hierarchy; Dasa: Kanaka Dasa uses tradition's language to claim spiritual authority

options.label: C
options.text: Vachanas: Kanaka Dasa uses tradition's language; Haridasa: dismantle varna hierarchy; Dasa: devotee transcends birth

options.label: D
options.text: Vachanas: dismantle varna hierarchy; Haridasa: Kanaka Dasa uses tradition's language; Dasa: devotee transcends birth

questions.solution: Correct answer: Vachanas: dismantle varna hierarchy; Haridasa: devotee transcends birth; Dasa: Kanaka Dasa uses tradition's language to claim spiritual authority.

questions.text: Kashmiri belongs to which language family?

options.label: A
options.text: Dravidian

options.label: B
options.text: Austroasiatic

options.label: C
options.text: Indo-Aryan (Dardic group)

options.label: D
options.text: Tibeto-Burman

questions.solution: Correct answer: Indo-Aryan (Dardic group).

questions.text: Which script is used for Kashmiri?

options.label: A
options.text: Devanagari

options.label: B
options.text: Perso-Arabic

options.label: C
options.text: Perso-Arabic script (Sharada historically)

options.label: D
options.text: Roman

questions.solution: Correct answer: Perso-Arabic script (Sharada historically).

questions.text: When was Kashmiri included in the Eighth Schedule?
questions.solution: Correct answer: 1950.

questions.text: Who wrote Lalla Vakyani?

options.label: A
options.text: Lal Ded (Lalleshwari)

options.label: B
options.text: Nund Rishi

options.label: C
options.text: Habba Khatoon

options.label: D
options.text: Ghulam Ahmad Mahjoor

questions.solution: Correct answer: Lal Ded (Lalleshwari).

questions.text: Which of the following is a major period or movement in Kashmiri literature?

options.label: A
options.text: Shaiva mystic movement

options.label: B
options.text: Romanticism

options.label: C
options.text: Modernism

options.label: D
options.text: Post-modernism

questions.solution: Correct answer: Shaiva mystic movement.

questions.text: According to the lesson, a high-scoring answer on the Rishi tradition's syncretism must distinguish three specific layers. Which of the following correctly identifies these three layers?

options.label: A
options.text: Doctrinal convergence, ritual practice, and social function

options.label: B
options.text: Lexical substitution, metaphysical equivalence, and institutional merger

options.label: C
options.text: Scriptural harmonisation, liturgical uniformity, and political patronage

options.label: D
options.text: Theological synthesis, linguistic borrowing, and demographic integration

questions.solution: Correct answer: Doctrinal convergence, ritual practice, and social function.

questions.text: What critical methodological caution does the lesson highlight regarding feminist re-readings of Habba Khatoon's poetry?

options.label: A
options.text: The printed corpus should be privileged over oral variants because it represents the author's final intention.

options.label: B
options.text: Oral variants archived in university folklore collections must be acknowledged alongside the printed corpus.

options.label: C
options.text: Habba Khatoon's voice can only be recovered through Persian translations made during the Sultanate period.

options.label: D
options.text: Feminist readings should focus exclusively on the 'lol' genre and ignore her vakhs.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Oral variants archived in university folklore collections must be acknowledged alongside the printed corpus..

questions.text: In the context of post-1990 Kashmiri conflict literature, which formal strategy is explicitly mentioned as being used by younger poets to mimic psychological dislocation?

options.label: A
options.text: Strict adherence to classical Persian metres such as the masnavi and ghazal

options.label: B
options.text: Fragmented syntax and code-switching between Kashmiri, Urdu, and English

options.label: C
options.text: Exclusive use of the Sharada script to assert cultural continuity

options.label: D
options.text: Adoption of the doha metre to align with the North Indian Bhakti canon

questions.solution: Correct answer: Fragmented syntax and code-switching between Kashmiri, Urdu, and English.

questions.text: The lesson uses the translation history of Lal Ded's vakhs to illustrate how translational decisions affect the literary canon. Which of the following correctly describes the impact of the three translations mentioned?

options.label: A
options.text: K.A. Abbas's free verse obscured the mnemonic rhythm; J.L. Kaul's doha metre aligned her with the Bhakti canon; the 2010 Academy edition restored shloka-like lineation.

options.label: B
options.text: All three translations uniformly adopted the 1954 orthography, eliminating dialectal variation from the textual record.

options.label: C
options.text: The 1970 and 1995 versions imposed the Roman script, while the 2010 edition reverted to Sharada for authenticity.

options.label: D
options.text: Each translation progressively removed Sufi vocabulary to emphasise Lal Ded's Shaivite origins.

questions.solution: Correct answer: K.A. Abbas's free verse obscured the mnemonic rhythm; J.L. Kaul's doha metre aligned her with the Bhakti canon; the 2010 Academy edition restored shloka-like lineation..

questions.text: According to the lesson, the 1954 orthographic standard imposed on Devanagari print editions erased which specific phonemic contrast in the Bhatwari dialect?

options.label: A
options.text: The distinction between /t/ and /tʰ/

options.label: B
options.text: The distinction between /ɖ/ and /ɖʱ/

options.label: C
options.text: The distinction between /ʃ/ and /s/

options.label: D
options.text: The distinction between /n/ and /ɳ/

questions.solution: Correct answer: The distinction between /ɖ/ and /ɖʱ/.

questions.text: Which of the following accurately describes the structural and musical characteristics of Rouf as presented in the lesson?

options.label: A
options.text: A men's choral dance-song with free verse lyrics performed during harvest festivals

options.label: B
options.text: A women's circle dance-song with doha-like couplet structure and a distinct melodic mode (maqam) sung during Navreh

questions.text: Which of the following statements accurately describes the linguistic classification and early literary development of Kashmiri according to the lesson?

questions.text: In the context of literary criticism for Paper II, how should a candidate distinguish between the works of Lal Ded and Habba Khatoon regarding their script usage?

options.text: D Lal Ded's work was mass-produced in newspapers, while Habba Khatoon relied solely on monastic manuscript circulation.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Lal Ded's verses were originally composed in Sharada and later transcribed to Persian script, whereas Habba Khatoon's work was exclusively in Perso-Arabic from the start..

questions.text: According to the lesson, what is the primary thematic shift observed when comparing Nund Rishi's Shruks with Lal Ded's Vakhs?

options.label: A
options.text: Nund Rishi focuses on social critique and caste discrimination, while Lal Ded focuses on metaphysical abstraction.

options.label: D
options.text: D Nund Rishi rejected the Sharada script entirely, while Lal Ded insisted on using only Sanskrit vocabulary.

questions.solution: Correct answer: B Nund Rishi's work shifts from external social reform to internal spiritual realization and the concept of Wahdat-ul-Wujud (Unity of Being)..

questions.text: When analyzing Mahjoor's poetry in contrast to the Rishi tradition, which factor represents the definitive break from medieval mysticism towards modernity?

options.label: D
options.text: D Mahjoor revived the Sharada script to ensure literary authenticity and reject the Perso-Arabic standardization.

questions.solution: Correct answer: C Mahjoor functioned as a journalist and editor whose work appeared in mass-produced newspapers, targeting a literate public instead of a monastic audience..

questions.text: Which of the following sets of objectives were pursued by the early twentieth‑century Kashmiri Language Movement led by Prem Nath Bazaz, Ghulam Ahmad Mahjoor and the Anjuman‑e‑Taraqqi‑e‑Kashmiri?

options.text: Creating a new literary language based on Persian vocabulary, abandoning oral forms, and banning manuscript culture

questions.text: In Amin Kamil’s poem “Vath”, how does the poet rework Lal Ded’s Vakh 12 motif of the spiritual journey?

questions.text: Regarding the critical reception of Habba Khatoon, what is a common scholarly error highlighted in the lesson?

questions.text: What formal feature of Nund Rishi’s Shruks enacts the Sufi doctrine of Wahdat‑ul‑Wujud, and how does it function?

questions.text: What were the three major consequences of the transition from oral transmission to print culture for Kashmiri literary texts, as outlined in the lesson?

questions.text: How does the 1972 Academy edition's editorial replacement of the colloquial "prem" with the Persianised "ishq" in Habba Khatoon's lyric "Moi chhu chhui..." reshape the poem's gender politics?

questions.text: Which narrative strategy distinguishes Rahman Rahi's polyphonic narration in his post-1947 modernist prose from a linguistically homogeneous reading?

questions.text: In K. N. Dhar's 1995 translation of Nund Rishi's "Haqq", which translational choice most directly alters the target-language reader's understanding of the source text's metaphysical argument?

questions.text: According to the postcolonial analysis by Bashir Ahmad Dhar, what was the primary cultural-political consequence of the 1935 orthography reform in Kashmir?

questions.solution: Correct answer: Ignoring the script context and treating Konkani literature as a monolithic entity without acknowledging the Devanagari/Kannada divide..

questions.text: Which of the following statements accurately describes the linguistic significance of Thomas Stephens' Krista Purana (1616) in the formation of early Konkani print culture?

options.label: A
options.text: It was the first Konkani text printed in Devanagari script, establishing the standard orthography for future publications.

options.label: B
options.text: It employed the ovi metre and codified a literary vocabulary blending Sanskrit-derived terms with Portuguese loanwords, based on the spoken Goan Bardes dialect.

options.label: C
options.text: It introduced the Kannada script for Konkani printing, enabling wider dissemination in the Karnataka coastal region.

options.label: D
options.text: It abandoned the Jesuit pedagogical agenda in favour of secular folk narratives, marking a shift from didactic to literary prose.

questions.solution: Correct answer: It employed the ovi metre and codified a literary vocabulary blending Sanskrit-derived terms with Portuguese loanwords, based on the spoken Goan Bardes dialect..

questions.text: The Sahitya Akademi's 1992 decision to accept manuscripts in both Devanagari and Kannada scripts for award consideration was primarily a response to which criticism?

options.label: A
options.text: Early awards privileged Devanagari-script works from Goa, marginalising the Kannada-script tradition of Karnataka Konkani writers.

options.label: B
options.text: The Akademi was accused of favouring urban themes over agrarian narratives in its selection criteria.

options.label: C
options.text: North Konkan (Malvani) dialect writers were completely excluded from the first two decades of awards.

options.label: D
options.text: The 1975 recognition of Konkani as a literary language did not specify a standard script for official use.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Early awards privileged Devanagari-script works from Goa, marginalising the Kannada-script tradition of Karnataka Konkani writers..

questions.text: Regarding the Modernist poetry movement in Konkani, the lesson warns against which analytical error?

options.label: A
options.text: Attributing the emergence of free verse solely to the influence of the Marathi Navya movement without noting distinct socio-cultural triggers in the Konkani context.

options.label: B
options.text: Overemphasising the continuity of Bhakti metrics in modernist poetry and ignoring the complete rupture with traditional forms.

options.label: C
options.text: Confusing the Jesuit missionary prose style with the modernist poetic experimentation of the mid-twentieth century.

options.label: D
options.text: Assuming that the Sahitya Akademi awards for poetry consistently favoured free verse over metrical compositions after 1975.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Attributing the emergence of free verse solely to the influence of the Marathi Navya movement without noting distinct socio-cultural triggers in the Konkani context..

questions.text: In comparative translation studies of Konkani literature, what key difference has been observed between English and Marathi translations of the same work?

options.label: A
options.text: English translations retain more regional idioms and dialect-specific terminology, while Marathi translations standardise vocabulary for a pan-Indian readership.

options.label: B
options.text: English translations tend to foreground universal themes such as migration and identity, whereas Marathi versions preserve cultural specificities like zatra festival terminology.

options.label: C
options.text: Marathi translations employ more footnotes for cultural terms because the target audience is less familiar with Konkani cultural contexts than English readers.

options.label: D
options.text: English translations are typically produced by the original authors themselves, while Marathi translations are commissioned by the Sahitya Akademi.

questions.solution: Correct answer: English translations tend to foreground universal themes such as migration and identity, whereas Marathi versions preserve cultural specificities like zatra festival terminology..

questions.text: According to the Goa University Konkani Manuscript Digitisation Project's 2022 OCR benchmarks, what is the character-accuracy rate for Kannada-script folios, and what is the primary reason for the lower accuracy compared to Devanagari?

questions.text: In Ravindra Kelekar's novel Himalayant (1976), the opening Zagor-style invocation frames the protagonist's migration as a ritual journey. Which of the following accurately identifies a specific Zagor motif and its literary transmutation in this context?

options.label: D
options.text: The call-and-response pattern between performers and audience becomes the novel's primary mode of character dialogue throughout.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The improvised dialogue preserving archaic lexical items like 'bhav' and 'zori' is re-contextualised as a ritual invocation framing migration..

questions.text: The lesson identifies a common error in tracing the evolution of the Konkani novel as 'presenting the novel's evolution as a clean linear progression; ignoring the coexistence of historical-romantic and realist modes in the 1930s-40s.' questions.text: A candidate is asked to 'compare the dramatic techniques of a Tiatr and a modern Konkani play' in Paper II. According to the lesson, which distinction is essential for a competent response?

options.label: D

questions.text: The earliest phase of Konkani literature is best described as:

questions.text: According to the lesson's analysis of the Sahitya Akademi Award controversy regarding Damodar Mauzo's novel 'Karmelin', what was the primary thematic departure from earlier Konkani literature?

questions.text: In the context of the 'Script vs. Content' matrix discussed in the lesson, why did Ravindra Kelekar choose Devanagari script for his major works despite the existence of Kannadi script?

options.label: A

questions.solution: Correct answer: C To create a 'Unified Literary Language' and reach a wider readership in Goa and Maharashtra due to historical educational policies..

questions.text: Which of the following statements correctly identifies a critical trap to avoid when answering questions about Konkani literature status prior to 2018?

options.label: A

options.label: D
options.text: D Asserting that Shenoi Goembab's works were written purely in oral dialectal tradition without any Marathi influence.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Treating 'Goan dialect' as synonymous with the entire 'Konkani language' without acknowledging its status as a dialect..

questions.text: How does the lesson suggest one should approach the analysis of major works like those by Ravindra Kelekar regarding script usage?

questions.solution: Correct answer: C By checking if the work was published in a specific dialect-script combination that defined its audience, acknowledging the strategic choice of Devanagari for unification..

questions.text: According to the lesson, the emergence of explicit feminist consciousness in Konkani women's writing is associated with which writer and period?

questions.text: Which of the following terminological usages aligns with the lesson's guidance on periodization for the 'History of the Language' section of the syllabus?

questions.solution: Correct answer: Using the syllabus terminology: 'Goembab Era,' 'Modern Period,' or 'Language Movement Period' for the 1920–1961 phase, avoiding the invented consensus term 'Konkani Renaissance'..

questions.text: Which of the following statements accurately distinguishes the 1987 Goa Official Language Act from the 1992 Seventy-First Constitutional Amendment regarding Konkani?

questions.text: According to the lesson, Konkani poetic modernism is characterised by which of the following formal strategies?

questions.text: Why does the lesson identify Acchev (1977) as the beginning of the Konkani novel proper, rather than earlier works like Kristanv Ghorabo (1905) or Goa Maca?

questions.text: What methodological issue does the lesson highlight regarding the Lokved folklore documentation project?

questions.text: Regarding the 2007 Sahitya Akademi Script Neutrality Resolution, the lesson indicates it altered eligibility criteria for awards. The 2022 dual-translation of Borkar's 'Mogachi' is presented as a case study illustrating what?

questions.text: The lesson warns against a specific trap in ecocritical analysis of Konkani landscape poetry. What does the examiner require instead of merely descriptive nature imagery?

questions.text: In the context of performance studies and textualisation, the 2005 critical edition of Borkar's 'Mogachi' made a specific editorial choice regarding sigla and neumes. What was this choice and its scholarly consequence?

questions.text: The 2007 Sahitya Akademi Script Neutrality Resolution altered the publishing economy of Konkani literature by:

questions.solution: Correct answer: Declaring that eligibility for Sahitya Akademi awards would no longer be tied to a single script, enabling Romi and Kannada-script works to compete..

questions.text: In Pundalik Naik's novel Acchev (1977), the Mahabharata is engaged through which specific mode of intertextuality?

questions.solution: Correct answer: A structural re-imagining mapping the Pandava-Kaurava rivalry onto post-liberation land disputes in a contested village..

questions.text: Which of the following statements accurately describes the magical realist strand in the Konkani novel as discussed in the lesson?

questions.text: The role of Vauraddeancho Ixtt in Konkani canon formation is best characterised by which of the following?

questions.solution: Correct answer: It underwent editorial selection, critical commentary, and institutional endorsement, with its trajectory mappable through tables of contents and Academy annual reports..

questions.text: A strong UPSC essay answer on Konkani diaspora writing should demonstrate awareness of which institutional gap?

questions.text: According to the Supreme Court in State of Punjab v. Ram Singh (2000), when does a policy statement create a substantive legitimate expectation enforceable against the State?

questions.solution: Correct answer: Only a clear, unambiguous promise accompanied by reliance creates a substantive legitimate expectation..

questions.text: Under the ILC Articles on State Responsibility, which test is required for attributing the conduct of non‑State actors to the State?

questions.text: The lesson states that the consent model in the Data Protection Act is not sufficient for all processing contexts. Which type of data and situation demand stricter safeguards?

options.text: Data processed by private entities without State involvement.

questions.text: Which safeguard against judicial overreach in Public Interest Litigation is highlighted by the Supreme Court in Divisional Manager, Aravali Golf Club v. Chander Hass (2008)?

options.text: Judicial activism is synonymous with any expansive PIL order.

questions.text: Consider a hypothetical scenario where Parliament passes an amendment to abolish the office of the President entirely. According to the Basic Structure Doctrine and the 'What If' approach discussed in the lesson, what is the constitutional status of this amendment?

options.label: A
options.text: It is valid as long as it follows the procedure under Article 368 since the text does not explicitly forbid abolishing the office.

options.label: B
options.text: It violates the basic structure because the separation of powers and federalism are integral features identified by the Supreme Court.

options.label: C
options.text: It is valid only if ratified by more than half of the state legislatures, regardless of the Basic Structure Doctrine.

options.label: D
options.text: It falls within the plenary power granted to Parliament under Article 368 as interpreted in the Berubari Union case.

questions.solution: Correct answer: It violates the basic structure because the separation of powers and federalism are integral features identified by the Supreme Court..

questions.text: Under Article 226, High Courts possess a wider scope of power compared to the Supreme Court under Article 32. What specific type of right can a High Court enforce via writs that the Supreme Court generally restricts itself to Fundamental Rights?

options.label: A
options.text: Only Fundamental Rights guaranteed under Part III

options.label: B
options.text: Any legal right or statutory duty violation, including errors of jurisdiction by lower courts

options.label: C
options.text: Rights related exclusively to the enforcement of Directive Principles of State Policy

options.label: D
options.text: Fundamental Rights only when no remedy exists in ordinary law

questions.solution: Correct answer: Any legal right or statutory duty violation, including errors of jurisdiction by lower courts.

questions.text: Regarding the jurisdictional hierarchy between Article 32 and Article 226, what was the ruling in Raj Narain v. State of UP (1975) concerning the necessity of exhausting remedies?

options.label: A
options.text: Exhaustion of Article 226 remedies is mandatory before approaching the Supreme Court under Article 32.

options.label: B
options.text: It is not necessary to exhaust remedies under Article 226 before approaching the Supreme Court under Article 32.

options.label: C
options.text: Article 226 cannot be used if a National Emergency is declared under Article 352.

options.label: D
options.text: The Supreme Court can only intervene if the High Court has explicitly refused jurisdiction.

questions.solution: Correct answer: It is not necessary to exhaust remedies under Article 226 before approaching the Supreme Court under Article 32..

questions.text: In judicial review of administrative action, the Wednesbury unreasonableness test requires the court to determine whether:

options.label: A
options.text: The decision is disproportionate to the legitimate aim pursued by the authority.

options.label: B
options.text: The decision is so unreasonable that no reasonable authority could have reached it.

options.label: C
options.text: The decision violates a legitimate expectation of the affected person without adequate justification.

options.label: D
options.text: The decision was made in breach of procedural fairness or natural justice.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The decision is so unreasonable that no reasonable authority could have reached it..

questions.text: Regarding the domestic implementation of treaties under Article 253 of the Constitution, which statement reflects the Indian judicial presumption?

options.label: A
options.text: All treaties are self‑executing and directly enforceable in domestic courts without enabling legislation.

options.label: B
options.text: Treaties are presumed to be non‑self‑executing unless the treaty text expressly creates directly enforceable obligations.

options.label: C
options.text: Parliament must always enact legislation to implement any treaty, irrespective of its content.

options.label: D
options.text: The executive can implement treaties by executive order alone, bypassing Parliament.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Treaties are presumed to be non‑self‑executing unless the treaty text expressly creates directly enforceable obligations..

questions.text: In the context of diplomatic protection, the rule of exhaustion of local remedies means that:

options.label: A
options.text: A State may espouse its national's claim only after the national has pursued and exhausted all available local remedies in the respondent State, unless they are demonstrably futile.

options.label: B
options.text: The respondent State must exhaust its domestic judicial processes before an international claim can be brought against it.

options.label: C
options.text: The claimant State must exhaust diplomatic negotiations before resorting to international adjudication.

options.label: D
options.text: Local remedies refer only to administrative remedies, not judicial ones.

questions.solution: Correct answer: A State may espouse its national's claim only after the national has pursued and exhausted all available local remedies in the respondent State, unless they are demonstrably futile..

questions.text: Which of the following safeguards was NOT introduced by the 44th Amendment in relation to Emergency provisions?

options.label: A

options.label: B
options.text: The non‑suspendability of Article 21 (right to life and personal liberty) during any Emergency.

options.label: C
options.text: Removal of the President's power to suspend the enforcement of Fundamental Rights during a Financial Emergency under Article 360.

options.label: D
options.text: Requirement that the President's satisfaction under Article 356 is justiciable and cannot be used for political purposes.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Requirement that the President's satisfaction under Article 356 is justiciable and cannot be used for political purposes..

questions.text: In the doctrine of colourable legislation, the Supreme Court's two-step analysis requires first identifying the legislative field by applying which test, and then verifying constitutional competence?

options.label: C
options.text: Repugnancy test under Article 254; then checking legislative history

questions.solution: Correct answer: Pith and substance test; then checking the Seventh Schedule entry.

questions.text: According to Hamidullah v. State of Madhya Pradesh (1972), delegated legislation can be struck down on three grounds of ultra vires. Which of the following correctly lists these three grounds?

options.label: A
options.text: Substantive ultra vires, procedural ultra vires, and violation of the Wednesbury principle (arbitrary, unreasonable, or discriminatory)

options.label: B
options.text: Excess of jurisdiction, error of law apparent on face of record, and violation of natural justice

options.label: C
options.text: Lack of legislative policy, absence of guidelines, and excessive delegation

options.label: D
options.text: Non-compliance with parent statute, violation of fundamental rights, and breach of international law

questions.solution: Correct answer: Substantive ultra vires, procedural ultra vires, and violation of the Wednesbury principle (arbitrary, unreasonable, or discriminatory).

questions.text: Regarding the persistent objector rule in customary international law, the lesson clarifies a common misconception. What is the correct requirement for a State to successfully invoke persistent objection?

options.label: A

options.label: B
options.text: The State must formally notify the UN Secretary-General of its objection

options.label: C
options.text: The objection must be supported by at least three other States

options.label: D
options.text: The State must have consistently voted against the rule in UN General Assembly resolutions

questions.solution: Correct answer: The objection must be continuous from the rule's inception, not merely after crystallisation.

questions.text: The Supreme Court of India applies which standard for determining bias in administrative proceedings, distinguishing it from the English "real likelihood" test?

options.label: A
options.text: Reasonable apprehension of bias in the mind of a reasonable person

options.label: B
options.text: Real likelihood of bias as perceived by the court

options.label: C
options.text: Actual bias proven by direct evidence

options.label: D
options.text: Predetermined outcome based on prior statements

questions.solution: Correct answer: Reasonable apprehension of bias in the mind of a reasonable person.

questions.text: In harmonious construction of Fundamental Rights, the Supreme Court follows a three-step technique. What is the correct sequence of these steps?

options.label: A
options.text: (i) Identify literal meaning; (ii) Ascertain legislative intent and constitutional scheme; (iii) Adopt interpretation avoiding conflict and advancing constitutional purpose

options.label: B
options.text: (i) Ascertain legislative intent; (ii) Identify literal meaning; (iii) Apply doctrine of implied repeal if conflict persists

options.label: C
options.text: (i) Apply basic structure test; (ii) Check for repugnancy under Article 254; (iii) Invoke federal supremacy

options.label: D
options.text: (i) Determine pith and substance; (ii) Check legislative competence; (iii) Apply colourable legislation doctrine

questions.solution: Correct answer: (i) Identify literal meaning; (ii) Ascertain legislative intent and constitutional scheme; (iii) Adopt interpretation avoiding conflict and advancing constitutional purpose.

questions.text: Under Section 76 of the Indian Penal Code, which of the following statements correctly describes the defence of mistake of fact?

options.label: A
options.text: A mistake of law, if honest and reasonable, excuses criminal liability.

options.label: B
options.text: The mistake must be honest, reasonable, and relate to a fact which, if true, would make the act lawful.

options.text: The defence applies even if the accused’s belief was unreasonable, provided it was genuine.

options.text: The burden of proving the mistake lies on the prosecution beyond reasonable doubt.

questions.text: In State of Maharashtra v. Mayer Hans George (1965), the Supreme Court held that the burden of proving the defence of accident under Section 80 IPC rests on the accused. What is the standard of proof required?

options.label: A
options.text: Beyond reasonable doubt.

options.label: B
options.text: Preponderance of probability.

options.label: C
options.text: Clear and convincing evidence.

options.label: D

questions.solution: Correct answer: Preponderance of probability..

questions.text: Which principle was established in R v. Dudley & Stephens (1884) regarding the defence of necessity under Section 81 IPC?

options.label: A
options.text: Necessity can justify the intentional killing of an innocent person to save others.

options.label: B
options.text: Necessity is available as a defence to murder if the harm caused is proportionate.

options.label: C
options.text: The intentional killing of an innocent person cannot be justified by necessity, even to save others.

questions.text: Extortion under Section 383 IPC differs from theft primarily because extortion requires:

options.label: C

questions.text: A buys poison and keeps it at home intending to kill B. Later, A takes the poison to B's house but is caught by the police on the way before entering B's room. According to the doctrine of proximity and relevant case law, how is A's conduct classified under the Indian Penal Code?

options.label: B
options.text: Guilty of Preparation to Commit Murder under Section 43 IPC

options.label: C
options.text: Not guilty of any offence as no crime has been committed

questions.solution: Correct answer: Guilty of Attempted Murder under Section 511 IPC.

questions.text: In a case where an offender voluntarily abandons their criminal purpose before completing the act, they are not guilty of attempt. Which of the following scenarios would NOT constitute voluntary abandonment according to judicial precedents like Ramchandra v. State of Maharashtra?

options.label: A
options.text: An offender stops because they realize the police are nearby and arrest is imminent

options.label: B
options.text: An offender stops because they feel remorse and genuinely change their mind

options.label: C
options.text: An offender stops because they find out the victim has moved away permanently

options.label: D
options.text: An offender stops because they realize the specific method planned is impossible to execute

questions.solution: Correct answer: An offender stops because they realize the police are nearby and arrest is imminent.

questions.text: A and B agree to rob a shop, buy masks, and plan the route together. They intend to execute the robbery jointly, but only A enters the shop while B is caught at the scene before entering. If the preparation was part of a joint conspiracy, how is liability determined under IPC Sections 149 and 34?

options.label: A
options.text: Only A is liable for attempted robbery; B is not liable as he did not enter

options.label: B
options.text: Both A and B are liable for attempted robbery due to common intention formed during preparation

options.label: C
options.text: Only B is liable for conspiracy; A is liable for attempt separately

options.label: D
options.text: Neither is liable until the actual robbery is completed

questions.solution: Correct answer: Both A and B are liable for attempted robbery due to common intention formed during preparation.

questions.text: Regarding the distinction between Attempt and Abandonment, if an offender realizes their plan is impossible to execute and stops, what is the legal consequence under modern jurisprudence as noted in Krishna Prasad v. State of Madhya Pradesh?

options.label: A

options.label: B
options.text: It remains an attempt because the initial intention was present

options.label: C
options.text: It constitutes preparation punishable under Section 43 IPC

options.label: D
options.text: It is treated as a completed offence due to prior acts

questions.solution: Correct answer: It is considered voluntary abandonment and no offence of attempt is committed.

questions.text: In cases of private defence under IPC Sections 96-106, how does the preparation of an aggressor affect the victim's right to use lethal force?

options.label: A
options.text: The victim can use immediate lethal force as soon as the aggressor prepares to attack

options.label: B
options.text: The victim's right to private defence arises only when there is a reasonable apprehension of imminent harm from the preparation

options.label: C
options.text: The victim must wait until the aggressor actually strikes before using any force

options.label: D
options.text: Preparation by the aggressor justifies the victim in using excessive force regardless of proximity

questions.solution: Correct answer: The victim's right to private defence arises only when there is a reasonable apprehension of imminent harm from the preparation.

questions.text: In State of Maharashtra v. Mayer Hans George (1965), the Supreme Court established a test for determining when a statutory offence imposes strict liability. Which of the following accurately states this test?

options.label: B
options.text: The presumption of mens rea can be displaced only by clear legislative language or necessary implication.

options.label: C
options.text: Strict liability applies to all regulatory offences concerning public safety regardless of statutory wording.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The presumption of mens rea can be displaced only by clear legislative language or necessary implication..

questions.text: Regarding the distinction between abetment under Sections 107–120A IPC and criminal conspiracy under Section 120B IPC, which statement is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: Both offences require an overt act in furtherance of the agreement to constitute the offence.

options.label: B
options.text: Abetment requires the offence abetted to be committed or attempted, whereas conspiracy punishes the agreement itself.

options.label: C
options.text: The actus reus of both offences is identical, consisting solely of an agreement between two or more persons.

options.label: D
options.text: Criminal conspiracy is a species of abetment and cannot be charged independently under Section 120B.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Abetment requires the offence abetted to be committed or attempted, whereas conspiracy punishes the agreement itself..

questions.text: Under Section 165 CrPC, a police officer may conduct a search without a warrant. According to the Supreme Court's interpretation referenced in the lesson, what are the mandatory conditions for such a warrantless search to be valid?

options.label: A
options.text: The officer must have reasonable suspicion and obtain oral approval from a Magistrate within 24 hours.

options.label: B
options.text: The search must be based on urgent necessity and the officer must record written reasons for dispensing with a warrant.

options.label: C
options.text: The officer may search any place if the offence is cognizable and non-bailable, without further justification.

questions.text: Which of the following statements accurately describes the role of the Church Missionary Society (CMS) Press at Kottayam in the development of modern Malayalam prose?

options.label: A
options.text: It was established in the 1840s by the Basel Mission and printed the first Malayalam novel Indulekha.

options.label: B
options.text: It began operations in 1821, producing early printed books like Bhasha Keralam (1824) that introduced standardized orthography and punctuation.

options.label: C
options.text: It primarily published Sanskrit-Manipravalam texts to preserve classical literary traditions against vernacular prose.

options.label: D
options.text: It launched the first Malayalam newspaper Rajya Samacharam in 1847 to disseminate reformist ideas.

questions.solution: Correct answer: It began operations in 1821, producing early printed books like Bhasha Keralam (1824) that introduced standardized orthography and punctuation..

questions.text: What is the significance of digital platforms like Project Madurai and the Kerala Digital Library in the global circulation of Malayalam texts?

options.label: A
options.text: They replaced traditional publishing entirely, making print translations obsolete by the early 2000s.

options.label: B
options.text: They host Unicode texts of public-domain works, enabling crowd-sourced translations into languages like French, German, and Japanese, thus bypassing traditional publishing gatekeepers.

options.label: C
options.text: They were established in the 1970s to distribute Soviet-era Russian translations of Thakazhi and Basheer.

options.label: D
options.text: They exclusively publish commissioned English translations of Jnanpith-winning novels by the Sahitya Akademi.

questions.solution: Correct answer: They host Unicode texts of public-domain works, enabling crowd-sourced translations into languages like French, German, and Japanese, thus bypassing traditional publishing gatekeepers..

questions.text: Which of the following statements accurately distinguishes the publication history of the first Malayalam serialized novel from the first novel published in book form?

options.label: A
options.text: Kundalatha (1887) was the first novel published in book form, while Indulekha (1889) was the first serialized narrative.

options.label: B
options.text: Indulekha (1889) appeared first as a book after a brief run in Mithavadi, whereas Kundalatha (1887) was the first identifiable serialized narrative in Kerala Patrika.

options.label: C
options.text: Marthanda Varma (1891) was the first serialized novel commissioned by the Travancore palace, predating both Kundalatha and Indulekha.

options.label: D
options.text: Both Kundalatha and Indulekha were simultaneously serialized in Kerala Patrika and Mithavadi respectively before book publication.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Indulekha (1889) appeared first as a book after a brief run in Mithavadi, whereas Kundalatha (1887) was the first identifiable serialized narrative in Kerala Patrika..

questions.text: The Kavya movement's manifesto, published in the inaugural issue of Kavya magazine (1965), called for which specific poetic innovations?

options.label: A
options.text: A return to the metered sentimentality of the Venmani school with enhanced Sanskritised vocabulary.

options.label: B

options.label: C
options.text: Exclusive adoption of Dravidian metres and rejection of all Western modernist influences.

options.label: D
options.text: Revival of the Manipravalam style blending Sanskrit and Malayalam for courtly aesthetics.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Free verse, imagistic density, and a language stripped of ornamental Sanskritisms..

questions.text: Regarding the role of little magazines in post-Independence Malayalam literary publics, which assessment aligns with the lesson's analytical perspective?

options.label: A
options.text: Little magazines remained marginal ephemera with negligible influence on mainstream literary award circuits.

options.text: Little magazines like Kavya were central to institutional recognition, as seen in the Kerala Sahitya Akademi award to Ayyappa Paniker in 1971.

options.text: Little magazines primarily served as platforms for established writers, excluding experimental voices.

options.label: D
options.text: The little magazine network dissolved by the early 1970s due to lack of patronage and readership.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Little magazines like Kavya were central to institutional recognition, as seen in the Kerala Sahitya Akademi award to Ayyappa Paniker in 1971..

questions.text: How does the lesson characterize the relationship between folk performance traditions (Theyyam, Padayani) and written Malayalam literature in the modernist period?

options.label: A
options.text: Folk forms served as static, unchanging sources that modernist poets merely borrowed from without reciprocity.

options.label: B
options.text: Written literature completely subsumed folk traditions, rendering them obsolete by the 1970s.

options.label: C
options.text: Folk forms and written literature engage in a living feedback loop, with contemporary Theyyam artists incorporating lines from modern poets like Ayyappa Paniker into traditional thottam.

options.label: D
options.text: The interaction was unidirectional: modernist poets used folk rhythms, but folk performances remained insulated from printed literature.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Folk forms and written literature engage in a living feedback loop, with contemporary Theyyam artists incorporating lines from modern poets like Ayyappa Paniker into traditional thottam..

questions.text: What was the key recommendation of the 1971 Malayalam Language Commission (chaired by M. G. S. Narayanan) regarding the linguistic register for official use versus education?

options.label: A
options.text: Immediate enforcement of a fully Sanskritised register across all domains including school textbooks.

options.text: Adoption of a purified Dravidian lexicon for all official and educational purposes, rejecting Sanskritised forms.

options.label: D
options.text: Abandonment of legislative standardization in favor of organic evolution through digital publishing and Unicode.

questions.solution: Correct answer: A dual-track policy: official documents in a Sanskrit-enriched register, school textbooks in a simplified Dravidian register..

questions.text: When analyzing M.T. Vasudevan Nair's Randamoozham in relation to Ezhuthachan, what is the primary critical distinction highlighted in the lesson?

questions.text: According to modern scholarship discussed in the lesson, how is Adhyathmaramayanam best characterized regarding its textual origin?

options.text: Roman script, because it was the standard for government notifications and legal documents.

options.label: D
options.text: Devanagari, because it was the script of the Bengali-language newspapers allowed free circulation.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Bengali script, because the colonial bureaucracy was already familiar with it, making licence acquisition easier..

questions.text: In Lamabam Kamal's novel Madhabi (1930), the 'journey-return' motif from the oral epic Khamba Thoibi is adapted by transplanting it onto a modern domestic plot. Which of the following accurately describes this structural adaptation?

options.label: A
options.text: The protagonist Khamba leaves Moirang, faces trials in the colonial bureaucracy, and returns to his village transformed.

options.label: B
options.text: The protagonist Madhabi leaves her village for Imphal, undergoes trials in the colonial bureaucracy, and returns transformed.

options.label: C
options.text: The novel replaces the epic's sung verses with a secularised invocation to 'Mother Manipur' at each chapter opening, but retains the exile-to-Moirang plot.

options.label: D
options.text: The journey-return pattern is abandoned in favour of a linear realist narrative, though the formulaic epithet 'Lainingthou' is retained.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The protagonist Madhabi leaves her village for Imphal, undergoes trials in the colonial bureaucracy, and returns transformed..

questions.text: The 1948 dual publications of the Mahabharata in Manipuri are cited in the lesson as evidence for which scholarly claim about translation practices?

options.label: A
options.text: All early translations followed a single domestication strategy aimed at Sanskritised purity.

options.label: B
options.text: Translators uniformly adopted a foreignising strategy to preserve the epic's archaic diction.

options.label: C
options.text: The dual publications demonstrate a deliberate scholarly split in translation strategy, contradicting the assumption of a single domestication approach.

options.label: D
options.text: The two versions were identical except for script, one in Bengali script and one in Meitei Mayek.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The dual publications demonstrate a deliberate scholarly split in translation strategy, contradicting the assumption of a single domestication approach..

questions.text: When evaluating the explanatory power of Dr. M. Kirti Singh's colonial-period model versus Dr. N. Pramod's linguistic model for the emergence of modern Manipuri prose, which statement correctly reflects their respective strengths as per the lesson?

options.label: A
options.text: The colonial model better accounts for script transition, while the linguistic model better explains thematic shifts.

options.label: B
options.text: The linguistic model better accounts for script transition, while the colonial model better explains thematic shifts.

options.label: C
options.text: Both models equally explain script transition and thematic shifts, differing only in their chronological boundaries.

options.label: D
options.text: The colonial model is preferred for Paper I because it aligns with the 1972 Official Language Act's periodisation.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The linguistic model better accounts for script transition, while the colonial model better explains thematic shifts..

questions.text: The Manipuri Language Development Committee (MLDC), established in 1952, compiled a 1955 bibliography of 'approved' texts that effectively froze the canon for two decades. Which later institutional development transferred canon-making authority away from the MLDC and embedded the Parishad-approved texts into the pedagogical pipeline?

options.label: A

options.label: B

options.label: C
options.text: The 1972 Official Language Act creating the Directorate of Language Planning and Implementation (DLPI), which commissioned the 1975 'Manipuri Reader' series.

options.label: D
options.text: The 1915 extension of the Indian Press Act, which regulated publication licenses through the District Magistrate.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The 1972 Official Language Act creating the Directorate of Language Planning and Implementation (DLPI), which commissioned the 1975 'Manipuri Reader' series..

questions.text: The earliest phase of Manipuri (Meiteilon) literature is best described as:

questions.text: The language Manipuri (Meiteilon) is mainly spoken in:

questions.text: Which statement about Manipuri (Meiteilon) is correct?
